The word faith is explained first. It has been said that in this place the prayer is meant.

The sense of faith was expounded earlier. It is the holding-true, and that may come by the statement alone or by the deed alone or by both together, so what is meant is that Allah would not let the holding-true of his messenger, which the believers showed by praying as commanded toward Jerusalem, be lost.

An objection is then answered. The people addressed were anxious about their brothers who had died while praying toward Jerusalem, so how can Allah say of the living that their faith would not be lost. They were anxious about the reward of that prayer too, supposing it null. The verse was therefore addressed to the living, with the dead among them included.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is Ever Gracious and Most Merciful to humanity
phrases.explanation:
The closing words are then explained. Allah is toward mankind full of compassion and merciful, and the sense is that Allah is toward all His servants the possessor of compassion, and compassion is the highest of the meanings of mercy and is general for all creatures in this world and for some of them in the hereafter, while the Merciful is the possessor of mercy for the believers.

The recitation of the word for compassion is then discussed. It is the reading of most of the reciters of Kufa in one form, and the reading of most of the reciters of Medina in another, and the accepted reading is one of the first two.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We see you ˹O Prophet˺ turning your face towards heaven. Now We will make you turn towards a direction ˹of prayer˺ that will please you.
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained. By We see the turning of your face toward the heaven, the sense given is that We see how you turn and direct yourself.

The word for turning is explained. It means the turning about and the directing. And by toward the heaven, the meaning is in the direction of the heaven and toward its side, so the verse pictures the messenger looking up.

Why he longed for it is discussed. Others said that he longed for it because it was the prayer direction of his father Abraham, and the report naming who said that given.

The promise that follows is explained. By We will surely turn you to a prayer direction that pleases you, the sense is that We will turn you to a direction that pleases you, and by so turn your face, that you should turn your face and change its direction.

The occasion of the question is given. It is said to him because before the change of his prayer direction he used to raise his hands toward the sky. The reason for the dislike of the direction of Jerusalem is given, which is that the Jews said that he followed their direction but differed from them.

phrases.translation: So turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque ˹in Mecca˺—wherever you are, turn your faces towards it.
phrases.explanation:
The command about turning the face is explained first. By wherever you may be, turn your faces toward it, the sense given is that wherever the believers may be on the earth, they are to turn their faces toward the sacred mosque, and the suffix in its direction refers to it.

A disagreement about the door is then recorded. Others said that the entire house is a prayer direction, and that the prayer direction of the house is its door, and the report naming who said that given.

The ruling preferred is then given at length. It is what Allah said, that you should turn your face in the direction of the sacred mosque, and whoever turns his face in that direction has correctly faced the prayer direction. It suffices for one who directs himself toward it to have the intention in his heart, just as the one who follows an imam is only obliged to follow him even if his body is not in line with him. So too is the ruling of the prayer direction, for when he is to the right or to the left of it and facing it, he directs himself toward it validly, whether the distance be great or small, provided he does not turn his back to it.

The saying of the messenger is then given, that the house is the prayer direction and the prayer direction of the house is its door.

phrases.translation: Those who were given the Scripture certainly know this to be the truth from their Lord.
phrases.explanation:
The second half of the verse is explained first. By those who were given the Book, the sense is that the scribes of the Jews and the scholars of the Christians.

The knowledge named is then set out. By know for certain that it is the truth from their Lord, the sense is that these rabbis and scholars know for certain that the change of the prayer direction is the truth from their Lord, and by from their Lord, the meaning is that it is a binding obligation upon the servants of Allah and not a matter of their choice, since it comes from their Lord and is not left to them.

phrases.translation: And Allah is never unaware of what they do
phrases.explanation:
The closing words are then explained. By Allah is not unaware of what you do, the sense given is that Allah is not unaware of what the believers do, so the statement warns them that their deeds are watched, and the account of that is given.

The sense of it is set out at length. Allah is not unaware of what you do in your following of His command and your perseverance in obedience to Him in the obligations of the pilgrimage and the rest of the duties, and nothing you do is hidden from Him. The point is that the change of the prayer direction does not cancel what was done before it, and that the One who watches every deed is the One who will reward it.

phrases.translation: Even if you were to bring every proof to the People of the Book, they would not accept your direction ˹of prayer˺, nor would you accept theirs; nor would any of them accept the direction ˹of prayer˺ of another.
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. By even if you were to come to those who were given the Book with every proof, the sense given is that even if the messenger came with every proof of what he has brought them, they would still refuse it.

A point of grammar is given. The words for even if are answered with the past tense of the verb, whereas by rule they would be answered with the future tense.

The clause about not being followers of one another's prayer direction is explained. The sense is that the Jews and the Christians do not agree upon a single prayer direction, since if he follows that of the Jews he embitters the Christians.

He is then told to leave off what cannot be satisfied and to call them to the pure creed and the prayer direction of Abraham.

phrases.translation: And if you were to follow their desires after ˹all˺ the knowledge that has come to you, then you would certainly be one of the wrongdoers
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained. By even if you were to follow their desires, the sense given is that even if the messenger sought the satisfaction of these Jews and Christians, and were then to follow their prayer direction.

The clause that follows is explained. By after the knowledge has come to you, the meaning is after the knowledge has reached the messenger, in that it has been made known to him that they persist in falsehood and obstinate resistance against the truth, and that the prayer direction toward which he has been turned is the one imposed upon Abraham and his descendants among the messengers.

Then you would surely be among the wrongdoers is explained. The sense is that the messenger, if he were to do that, would be among the servants who wrong themselves.

phrases.translation: Those We have given the Scripture recognize this ˹Prophet˺ as they recognize their own children.
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. By those to whom We have given the Book recognize it, the sense given is that the scribes of the Jews and the scholars of the Christians know that the sacred house is their prayer direction, and the prayer direction of Abraham, and the prayer direction of the prophets before the messenger, just as they recognize their own sons.

The reason for the comparison is then given. The knowledge of these men is sound and complete, since they know the matter as a man knows his own child, so the likeness is not to the ignorance of others but to the sureness of what they know.

phrases.translation: Yet a group of them hides the truth knowingly
phrases.explanation:
The second half is then explained. By a group of them conceal the truth while believing in it, the sense is that a group of those to whom the Book was given, and they are the Jews and the Christians, conceal the truth even while they believe in it.

The sense of the concealment is then set out. Those who hold the truth of the messenger and the prayer direction he has been given nevertheless hide it from those who do not know, so that they may keep their own position and not lose the standing they have with the people who follow them. It has been said that the phrase means the people of the book, and the report of that is given.

phrases.translation: ˹This is˺ the truth from your Lord, so do not ever be one of those who doubt
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. By the truth from your Lord, the sense given is that the messenger should know that the truth is that which his Lord has made known to him and brought from Himself.

The warning is then explained. By so be not one of those who doubt, the sense is that the messenger should not be in doubt about the prayer direction toward which he has been turned.

The word used is then examined. It is a derived form from the word for doubt, and a line of poetry is cited as a witness.

A question is then raised. Was the messenger in doubt about the truth being from his Lord, such that doubting was forbidden him?

The question is then answered. That belongs to the manner of speech which the Arabs express in the form of a command to the one addressed while another is meant by it, and the example is the command to the prophet to be mindful of Allah.

phrases.translation: Everyone turns to their own direction ˹of prayer˺.
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. By for everyone, the sense is for every adherent of a religious community, and the rest of the phrase is left out.

The explanation of that view is given. For every adherent of a religious community there is a prayer direction toward which he turns and directs his face.

Another view is set out. For every cardinal direction toward which your Lord has turned you, there is a prayer direction, and Allah turns His servants toward it.

The word for direction is then examined. It is a verbal noun, like the manner of sitting and the manner of walking, derived from turning oneself, and its meaning is that toward which one turns in prayer.

The turning named in it is then explained. It means turning toward, and the Arabic usage is set out, since one says to another, turn to me, meaning turning yourself toward it.

The recitation of the phrase is discussed. It has been transmitted from a group of the early authorities that they read it as he is turned thereto, in the meaning that he is turned toward that direction.

Another reading is mentioned. It has been said that some of them read it as and for every direction, but that is a linguistic error and it is not permissible.

The reading preferred is then given. It is and for everyone there is a direction toward which he turns, meaning that everyone has a prayer direction and each of them turns his face toward it.

phrases.translation: So compete with one another in doing good. Wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together ˹for judgment˺. Surely Allah is Most Capable of everything
phrases.explanation:
The command to compete is explained. By so compete in good deeds, the sense given is that the believers should hasten to good works in gratitude toward their Lord and provide for themselves for the hereafter.

The gathering named next is explained. By wherever you may be, Allah will bring you all together, the sense is that in whatever place they perish, Allah will bring them all together on the day of resurrection.

The urging of the verse is then set out. It urges the believers to obedience and to providing for themselves, since they are told to compete in works of obedience and to hold fast to the prayer direction of Abraham.

The closing words are explained. By Allah is over all things Almighty, the sense is that Allah is able to gather them after their death from wherever they were, so they should hasten with good works.

phrases.translation: Wherever you are ˹O Prophet˺, turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque. This is certainly the truth from your Lord. And Allah is never unaware of what you ˹all˺ do
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. By from wherever you set out, the sense given is that from whatever place the messenger sets out, and toward whatever place he directs himself, he is to turn his face toward the sacred mosque, and the meaning of the word for direction was explained earlier.

The truth named in it is then explained. By and indeed it is the truth from your Lord, the sense is that directing oneself in that direction is the truth concerning which there is no doubt, coming from the Lord.

The closing words are then explained. By Allah is not unaware of what you do, the sense is that Allah is not unaware of the deeds of the believers, and the account of that is given.

phrases.translation: Wherever you are ˹O Prophet˺, turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque. And wherever you ˹believers˺ are, face towards it,
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. By from wherever you set out, turn your face toward the sacred mosque, the sense given is that from whatever place or region the messenger departs and sets out, he is to turn his face toward the sacred mosque, for that is its direction, and the turning in that direction means directing the face toward it.

The command to the believers is then explained. By wherever you are, turn your faces toward it, the sense is that wherever the believers may be, on whatever part of the earth of Allah, they are to turn their faces in their prayer toward it and take it as their goal.

phrases.translation: so that people will have no argument against you, except the wrongdoers among them. Do not fear them; fear Me,
phrases.explanation:
The reason given is explained first. By so that the people may have no argument against you, except those among them who do wrong, a group of the exegetes said that the people meant are the people of the book.

That answer is then given. It was said that the people of the book argued that the messenger and his companions did not know where their prayer direction was until they were guided, and that the messenger differs from them in religion yet follows their prayer direction.

The sense of the disputing is set out. It concerns only the disputations and the wrangling, and Allah cut off that argument by turning the prayer direction of the messenger and the believers away from the direction of the Jews toward that of Abraham.

The exception is then explained. Those who do wrong are the polytheists of Quraysh. The word for argument means precisely the disputation and the wrangling, so the meaning is that none of the people may have a disputation against them, except the polytheists of Quraysh, for they have a false claim and a disputation without right.

phrases.translation: so that I may ˹continue to˺ perfect My favour upon you and so you may be ˹rightly˺ guided
phrases.explanation:
The sense of the exception is explained. It is an exception in the well-known sense, which affirms for the excepted what was denied of the rest, as when one says that no one of the people travelled except your brother. So none of the people has a disputation against the messenger or his companions because of their turning toward the house, except those among Quraysh who have wronged themselves.

The claim that the exception means and not is set aside as false. If that were its meaning, the mention of the exception would add nothing but confusion, and it falls outside the language of the Arabs, since the word for except does not occur with that sense after a preceding exception.

A further claim is set aside, that the wrongdoers have no argument so should not be feared, and that is rejected on the agreement of all the exegetes.

Another claim is set aside, that the wrongdoers here are Arabs who were Jews and Christians, and that the argument of whoever argued was broken. That is rejected too, since the exception was directed at wrongdoers among the people of the book.

The closing clause is explained. By so that I may complete My favor upon you, the sense is that by turning the face toward the sacred mosque and taking it as a prayer direction, none of the people may have an argument except the polytheists of Quraysh, and so that by guiding them to the prayer direction of Abraham, whom He made a leader for the people, Allah may complete His favor and perfect His grace upon them

phrases.translation: Since We have sent you a messenger from among yourselves—reciting to you Our revelations, purifying you, teaching you the Book and wisdom, and teaching you what you never knew—
phrases.explanation:
The connection of the words is explained. The phrase just as is joined to the saying and so that I might complete My favor upon you, and not to the saying Remember Me.

That reading is then defended. The Arabs do not put a condition on the second part of such a phrase, so the reply Remember Me follows and the clauses stand apart.

That view is rejected as too far-fetched and as driving the saying from its well-known meaning.

The sense of just as is explained. It means the Arabs, so the address is to them to hold fast to obedience and to turn toward the prayer direction.

The work of the messenger is set out. By who recites to you Our signs, it means the signs of the Quran. By and purifies you, it means cleanses you of the filth of sins.

The last clause is explained. By teaches you what you did not know, it means the reports of the prophets, the accounts of the bygone communities, and what comes to pass among the Arabs.

phrases.translation: remember Me; I will remember you.
phrases.explanation:
The exchange is explained first. By Remember Me, I will remember you, the sense given is that the believers are to remember Allah by obeying Him in what He commands and forbids, and He will remember them through His mercy toward them and His forgiveness for them.

A point of grammar is then added, that the word may be derived from the word for remembrance in the sense of praise and laudation, so that the sense of the exchange is that remembrance of Allah on their side brings remembrance of them on His, and that the two run together as reward and grace in store for them.

phrases.translation: And thank Me, and never be ungrateful
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. By be grateful to Me, the sense given is that the believers are to be grateful to Allah for the favor He has bestowed upon them in the form of Islam and the guidance to the religion He has prescribed for His prophets.

The second half is then explained. By never be ungrateful, the sense is that they are not to deny His beneficence toward them, lest He deprive them of the favor He has bestowed, and rather they are to be grateful so that He may increase them and complete His favor.

The two words are then explained from what was shown earlier. Gratitude is the praising of a person for his praiseworthy deeds, and ungratefulness is the covering up of a matter.

phrases.translation: O believers! Seek comfort in patience and prayer. Allah is truly with those who are patient
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. By seek help through patience and prayer, the sense is that the believers are to seek help from what they are commanded to endure and to hold fast to, and the meaning of patience and of prayer was expounded earlier, so it is not repeated.

The closing clause is then explained. By Allah is with the patient, the sense given is that Allah is their helper and their support and is pleased with their deed, and it is like the saying of a man, do such-and-such, and I am with you, meaning that he is their helper in that deed and their support in it.

phrases.translation: Never say that those martyred in the cause of Allah are dead—in fact, they are alive! But you do not perceive it
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained. By seek help through patience, the sense given is that the believers are to seek help through patience in obeying Allah against the enemy.

The prohibition is explained. Do not say of those killed in the way of Allah that they are dead, since the dead one is the one from whom He has taken his life, and whoever is killed that way lives with Allah.

An objection is answered. If the favour of distinguishing the martyrs is not present here, the answer is that they knew their state through the earlier report.

The clause about not perceiving them is explained. By but you perceive it not, the meaning is that they do not see them, so they know they are living only through the report.

phrases.translation: We will certainly test you with a touch of fear and famine and loss of property, life, and crops. Give good news to those who patiently endure—
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. It is an announcement from Allah to the followers of His messenger that He will test them and put them to the trial with severe trials in all sorts of matters, so that He may know who follows and who turns back.

The word for trial is explained. And We will surely test you means that He will surely put them to the trial, and the sense of that word was expounded earlier.

The kinds of trial are then set out. With something of fear means the fear of the enemy. Hunger means famine, so a year of drought befalls them in which hunger and privation come. And wars take place between them and the unbelievers. All of this is a trial, so that the truthful may be told apart from the liars.

A point of grammar is given. The word for something was used rather than the word for things because of the diversity of the kinds, and the word for of indicates that with each it is understood.

phrases.translation: who, when faced with a disaster, say, “Surely to Allah we belong and to Him we will ˹all˺ return.”
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. By give glad tidings to the patient ones, the sense given is that the glad tidings are given to those who know that every grace befalling them comes from Him, who therefore acknowledge His claim as Lord over them.

Their state is then described. They submit to His decree, hope for His reward and fear His punishment, and say when He tests them with some of His trials and afflicts them with what He has promised, that they are the possession of their Lord as long as they remain alive and that they will return to Him after death, in submission to His decree and contentment with His judgments.

phrases.translation: They are the ones who will receive Allah’s blessings and mercy.
phrases.explanation:
The ones described are explained first. By those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy, the sense is that blessings are sent upon them and mercy is granted to them.

The word for blessing is then explained from what was shown earlier, and it means forgiveness, so what is promised for them is forgiveness, that is to say that they are forgiven. The word is traced to its origin in a word used earlier, where it was shown to mean the sending down of blessing upon a thing and the favour of it.

The announcement is then tied to what was said before it, since the mercy comes to them on account of their patience under the trials and their submission to His decree.

phrases.translation: And it is they who are ˹rightly˺ guided
phrases.explanation:
The second half is then explained. By those are the ones who are rightly guided, the sense is that they are the ones who have hit upon the path of truth, and the meaning of being rightly guided was explained earlier as correct guidance toward what is right.

It is announced alongside what was said about granting them forgiveness and mercy on account of their steadfast patience under the trials and their submission to His decree. The words and mercy are then explained, so that alongside the forgiveness by which He forgives and covers their sins there is mercy from Allah and compassion.

In agreement with what has been said about this, a group of the people of interpretation spoke, and the reports naming who said so are given.

phrases.translation: Indeed, ˹the hills of˺ Ṣafa and Marwah are among the symbols of Allah.
phrases.explanation:
The names are then examined. As for Marwah, it is the small pebble, and a small quantity of them is gathered together as marawāt and a large quantity as al-marw, and two lines of poetry are cited as a witness.

The word for symbols is then explained. By among the sacred symbols of Allah, the meaning is among the landmarks of Allah which He has made for His servants a marker and a sign by which they worship Him.

The two mountains are then specified. What is meant is the two mountains designated by these two names and located within the sacred precinct, and not the rest of the level ground and the pebbles.

phrases.translation: So whoever performs the pilgrimage or minor pilgrimage, let them walk between ˹the two hills˺. And whoever does good willingly, Allah is truly Appreciative, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation:
The rite is explained first. By Safa and Marwah are among the sacred symbols, Allah informed His believing servants that the running between the two is among the rites of the pilgrimage He instituted, which He commanded Abraham.

The one who performs the lesser pilgrimage is then explained. He is called that because, when he has gone around the House, he departs from it after his visit. Then there is no blame upon him in going around the two is explained as meaning that there is no sin upon him.

A recitation is rejected. Whoever distinguishes between the ruling of the two is asked for his proof, and the reading that has no blame upon him in not going around the two is rejected.

The recitation of the last clause is then set out. Some of the reciters read it with the letter that makes it a completed act and others with the letter that makes it an effort.

The correct view is given. It is not the voluntary walking between the two, since one who walks between the two can only do so in a pilgrimage, so what is meant is the voluntary performance of it.

phrases.translation: Those who hide the clear proofs and guidance that We have revealed—
phrases.explanation:
The ones described are explained first. By those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs, the sense is that the scholars of the Jews and their rabbis, and the scholars of the Christians, because of their concealing from the people the matter of the messenger and their refraining from following him, while they found him described in the Torah and the Gospel.

The clear proofs concealed are then named. It is that which was made clear concerning the matter of the messenger and his mission, namely the account of his prophethood, his mission and his description, in the two Books sent down to them.

phrases.translation: after We made it clear for humanity in the Book—
phrases.explanation:
The clause about making it clear is then explained. By after We have made it clear for the people in the Book, the sense is that a portion of the people, for the knowledge of the prophethood of the messenger, his description and his mission was only with the people of the book and with no one else, and they are the ones meant by the people of the book, and the book means the Torah and the Gospel.

The scope of the verse is then noted. This verse, even though it was sent down concerning a specific group of people, is nevertheless intended for every concealer of knowledge whose clarification to the people Allah has made clear in the Book.

phrases.translation: will be condemned by Allah and ˹all˺ those who condemn
phrases.explanation:
The guidance named is then explained. It is what was clarified to them of the matter of the messenger in the books sent down upon their prophets, so the verse refers to those who conceal from the people what was sent down in their books of clarification regarding the messenger, his prophethood, and the soundness of the community with which He sent him.

The curse named is then explained. By those are the ones whom Allah curses, these are the ones who conceal what Allah sent down concerning the messenger after He had made it clear to them in their books, and He curses them on account of their concealment and their refraining from making it clear.

The meaning of the verse is then given. They are the ones whom Allah removes from Himself and from His mercy, and the cursers ask their Lord to curse them, the cursing by the children of Adam being their saying, O Allah, curse him, since the curse means removal and driving away.

A question is then raised about who the cursers are, and it is noted that the plural of the beasts of the field is formed without the way it is formed for the children of Adam.

The view preferred is then given. The cursers are the angels and the believers, since Allah described the disbelievers with the attribute that the curse upon them is from Allah, the angels and mankind together, and the curse reported upon the other group is of the same kind.

phrases.translation: As for those who repent, mend their ways, and let the truth be known, they are the ones to whom I will turn ˹in forgiveness˺,
phrases.explanation:
The exception is explained first. By those who repent, and make it clear, the sense is that Allah and the cursers curse those who concealed from the people what they knew concerning the prophethood of the messenger, except the one among them who turns back from his concealment, who returns to repentance through faith in the messenger, who draws near to Allah with good deeds, and who makes clear what he knew of the revelation.

A claim is then rejected. It has been said that making it clear means that the repentance was made clear through sincerity of action, but the Book is against that.

Those concerned are named. They are Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions among the people of the book.

phrases.translation: for I am the Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation:
The closing words are then explained. By I am the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful, the sense is that He is the One who returns the hearts of His servants who have turned away from Him back to Him, and the Merciful toward those who turn to Him covers them with forgiveness.

A question is then raised. How can repentance be accepted from the one who has repented, and can there be one who repents without his repentance being accepted?

The answer is then given. This is a matter where one of the two cannot exist without the other accompanying it, so it is the same whether one says that the excepted are those whose repentance was accepted, or that they are those who repented, for indeed the acceptance of their repentance is announced.

phrases.translation: Surely those who disbelieve and die as disbelievers are condemned by Allah, the angels, and all of humanity
phrases.explanation:
The people described are explained first. By those who disbelieve, the sense is those who denied the prophethood of the messenger and held him to be a liar, from among the Jews and the Christians and the rest of the adherents of religious communities.

The curse is then explained. Upon them is the curse of Allah and of the angels, meaning that upon those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers is the curse of Allah, for Allah has removed them from His mercy. And of the angels means that the angels and mankind cursed them.

A disagreement is then recorded. Some of the exegetes said that by and of mankind all together, Allah meant the people who believe in Him.

That is set aside, and other views are given instead. Some said this concerns the day of resurrection, when the disbeliever is placed before the witnesses and all mankind curse him. Others said it concerns the saying of the speaker.

The view preferred is then given. Allah meant all mankind, in the sense of their cursing of them.

phrases.translation: They will be in Hell forever. Their punishment will not be lightened,
phrases.explanation:
The clause is explained first. Abiding therein eternally means that they abide in the curse eternally, so that the punishment is not lightened for them and they are not granted respite to excuse themselves with an excuse.

A question is raised about the case of the word abiding, and the answer is given. It stands in the accusative as an adverbial qualifier of state, derived from the letters in the phrase upon them, since the meaning is that they are the ones whom Allah curses, and the angels, and mankind together.

A recitation is then mentioned and rejected. Although it is permissible in Arabic, it is not permitted to recite according to that reading, since it conflicts with the codices of the Muslims and the recitation they have transmitted by widespread dissemination.

phrases.translation: nor will they be delayed ˹from it˺
phrases.explanation:
A point of grammar is then added. The word for the curse is a verbal noun from the saying that Allah cursed him, in the meaning that He removes him and drives him away, and the same is meant by the cursing of the children of Adam, which is their saying, O Allah, curse him.

The closing words are then explained. By they will not be granted respite, the sense is that they will not be given time to excuse themselves with an excuse.

The case of the two words is then set out, that they stand in the accusative as an adverbial qualifier of state, drawn from the two letters that occur in the words upon them.

phrases.translation: Your God is ˹only˺ One God. There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him—the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation:
The statement is explained first. The meaning of godhood was expounded earlier, and it pertains to the worship rendered by created beings. By your god is one God, the sense is that He who has a right to your obedience and deserves worship from you is one worshipped one and one Lord.

The oneness is then explained further. Some said that the meaning of the oneness of Allah is the negating of any of His kind or equal to Him.

The proof that follows is then explained. By the verse that follows, Allah made known to the polytheists the place where the people of understanding could derive the proof for His oneness. So He said, if you are in doubt about that announcement, then ponder the proofs, for among them are the creation of the heavens and the earth, the alternation of night and day, the ships that sail upon the sea.

phrases.translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth; the alternation of the day and the night;
phrases.explanation:
The proof named first is examined. The alternation means the form derived from succeeding one another, whereby each of the two replaces the other.

The creation is then named. By the creation of the heavens and the earth, the proof is set out at length, and it is explained that the denial of the disbelievers does not prevent everything He has mentioned being an indication of its Creator.

The scope of the argument is then set out. He argued only against a people who acknowledged that Allah was their Creator, except that in His worship they ascribed partners through the worship of images and idols, so the argument was against those, and the sun and the moon running untiring in their course for the benefit of their sustenance is the meaning of the alternation of night and day, and the rain sent down making their regions fertile is the meaning of the water sent down from the sky, and the cattle made subservient to them is the meaning of the scattering of every kind of creature, and the fertilizing winds and the clouds are the meaning of the directing of the winds and the clouds.

phrases.translation: the ships that sail the sea for the benefit of humanity;
phrases.explanation:
The explanation of the words is given first. By the ships that sail upon the sea with that which benefits mankind, the sense is indeed the ships that sail upon the sea.

The word for ships is then explained. It is the word for the ship, and the singular and the plural have the same form, and the word is used both as masculine and feminine, as it is used as masculine elsewhere.

The reading in this verse is set out. Here it is used as feminine, for when it is set in motion it is the running one, so the form for the feminine is added to it.

The last part of the clause is then explained. By with that which benefits mankind, its meaning is that it benefits mankind upon the sea.

phrases.translation: the rain sent down by Allah from the skies, reviving the earth after its death; the scattering of all kinds of creatures throughout;
phrases.explanation:
The water is then explained. By what Allah has sent down from the sky of water, the sense is the rain that Allah causes to descend from the sky.

The answer is then given at length. The denial of whoever denies does not prevent that everything He has mentioned is an indication of its Creator and Maker. The argument was against a people who acknowledged that Allah was their Creator, except that in His worship they ascribed partners through the worship of images and idols, so the rain sent down making the regions fertile is the meaning of the water sent down from the sky, and the cattle made subservient to them is the meaning of the scattering of every kind of creature, and the fertilizing winds and the clouds are the last clause.

phrases.translation: the shifting of the winds;
phrases.explanation:
The clause is then explained. By He scattered therein every kind of creature, the sense is in what He has scattered upon the earth of creatures.

Two points of grammar are then added. The word for scattered means distributed, derived from the saying of a commander who scattered his detachments of troops, and the letters in the word for therein refer back to the earth. And the word for creature is the active participle from the saying of a speaker that the creature crept with a creeping, and it is a designation for every animate being that is not a bird flying with its two wings, on account of its creeping over the earth.

phrases.translation: and the clouds drifting between the heavens and the earth—˹in all of this˺ are surely signs for people of understanding
phrases.explanation:
The occasion of the verse is then discussed. Others said that it was sent down because the polytheists asked the messenger for a sign, so that they might be taught by it that in the creation of the heavens and the earth and all the rest lies a clear sign of the oneness of Allah.

The correct view is then given. Allah directed His servants by this verse to the demonstration of His oneness and His being alone in the divine kingship to the exclusion of all else. It is possible that it was sent down for one of the two views and possible that it was sent down for the other, but the intent of the verse is what has been said.

The closing clause is then explained. By the directing of the winds, the sense is the directing of the winds, and the agent was left out and the action attached to the object, as when one says it pleases me that your brother is honored.

The clouds and the signs are then explained. The cloud is called that because one part of it drags the other along. And the meaning of signs is marks and indications that the Creator of all this is one god.

phrases.translation: Still there are some who take others as Allah’s equal—
phrases.explanation:
The exposition of the meaning is given first. It is that among mankind there are those who take, besides Allah, equals to Him, and that they love those equals as one loves Allah, while those who believe have a stronger love for Allah than they have for these equals.

The word for equal was set forth earlier, meaning the peer, and the testimonies indicating that were given with it, so it is not repeated here. The verse thus sets two groups beside one another, those who take equals and love them as they love Allah, and those whose love of Allah is stronger than the love of those equals.

phrases.translation: they love them as they should love Allah—but the ˹true˺ believers love Allah even more.
phrases.explanation:
The equals the people took are then discussed. The exegetes differed concerning them. Some of them said that they are their gods which they worshipped besides Allah, and the report naming who said that is given. Others said no, the equals here are rather their masters whom they obeyed in disobedience to Allah, and the report naming who said that is given.

The whole clause is then set out. The meaning is that among mankind are those who, O believers, take besides Allah equals whom they love as you love Allah.

The word for love is then explained, as one greets the emir, so they love them with the fullness of the love they have for Allah.

phrases.translation: If only the wrongdoers could see the ˹horrible˺ punishment ˹awaiting them˺,
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. And if those who did wrong could see, this is permissible when the word for indeed is put in the kasra as the opening of a new sentence, since the sense is if they could but know.

The reading preferred is then given. It is with the letter that makes it if you could see, and the sense is then you would see that the power belongs entirely to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment, with the second clause omitted.

The reason for preferring it is then given. The people, when they see the punishment, already know with certainty that the power belongs entirely to Allah, so there is no basis for saying if they could but see.

The clause about beholding the punishment is then explained. It means when they see the punishment with their own eyes.

phrases.translation: they would certainly realize that all power belongs to Allah and that Allah is indeed severe in punishment
phrases.explanation:
The reciters differed concerning the recitation of this. The majority of the people of Medina and Syria recited it with the letter that makes it if you could see and with the fatḥa on the words for indeed.

The case of the two words is then explained, that they stand in the accusative because of the omitted part of the phrase.

Other recitations are then set out. Some read the words for indeed with the kasra, so that the sense is that you would know the state into which they will come, and others read them with the letter that makes it if those who did wrong could see.

A grammatical claim is then mentioned, that the sense of that reading is if they could but know.

phrases.translation: ˹Consider the Day˺ when those who misled others will disown their followers—when they face the torment—
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. By when those who were followed disavow those who followed them and they see the punishment, the sense is that when those who were followed disavow their followers and behold the punishment.

A disagreement is then recorded. The people of interpretation differed concerning whom is meant by this, and the reports of what they said given.

The correct view is then given. Allah has announced that those who were followed in ascribing partners to Allah disavow their followers when they behold the punishment of Allah with their own eyes, and He did not single out some of them above others.

The indication of the verse is then noted, which confirms the reading that the equals here are the men whom they obey and through whom they disobey Allah.

phrases.translation: and the bonds that united them will be cut off
phrases.explanation:
The bonds are then explained. By the bonds between them are severed, the sense is that Allah is severe in punishment when those who were followed disavow and when the bonds between them are severed.

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of the bonds. Some of them said one thing, and others said that they are the abodes which they had among the people of this world, and the report naming who said that is given. And others said that the bonds are the deeds which they performed in this world.

The correct view is then given. Allah has announced that those who wronged themselves among the people of disbelief who died while they were disbelievers, that the followed one disavows the follower as soon as they behold the punishment of Allah with their own eyes, and that the bonds between them are severed.

The sense of the bonds is then explained further. All these are bonds by which one provides oneself in this world a means to one's desires, but Allah cut off their benefit in the hereafter for those who were disbelieving towards Him, because they were in conflict with His obedience, so their mutual friendship did not benefit them before their Lord, nor their worship of their equals, and no kinship ties defended them against Allah's retribution.

phrases.translation: The ˹misled˺ followers will cry, “If only we could have a second chance, we would disown them as they disowned us.”
phrases.explanation:
The followers are explained first. By those who followed will say, the sense is that the followers of those men, those whom they had taken as partners alongside Allah and obeyed in disobedience to Him, will say, when they behold the punishment of Allah in the hereafter, if only we had a return, that is a second chance by which they might return to the worldly life.

The saying of the followers is then set out. They would disown those whom they followed just as those whom they followed disowned them, and the whole of the saying is turned into a single cry of regret, since the wish is that they might return and then disown those who misled them, and then repent of what they did with them.

phrases.translation: And so Allah will make them remorseful of their misdeeds.
phrases.explanation:
Thus will Allah show them their deeds is explained first. The meaning is that just as He showed them the punishment which they denied in the worldly life, so too does He show them their corrupt deeds by which they deserved the punishment, as regrets for them.

The exegetes differed concerning the explanation of that. Some of them said that the meaning is that thus will Allah show them the deeds He prescribed for them in the worldly life but which they neglected and did not perform. Others said that thus will Allah show them their evil deeds as regrets for them, why did they do them, and why did they not do other deeds that please Allah.

The explanation preferred is then given. Thus will Allah show the disbelievers their corrupt deeds as regrets for them, why did they do them, and why did they not do others, so they feel regret over the evil deeds they committed.

A closing note is then added. What is most fitting is that to which the apparent meaning points and not that which the inner meaning might allow, since there is no indication that the inner sense is intended.

phrases.translation: And they will never ˹be able to˺ leave the Fire
phrases.explanation:
The closing words are explained. By they will not depart from the Fire, the sense is that these disbelievers, even though they feel remorse after beholding the punishment with their own eyes, so that their regret became intense and they wished for a return to the worldly life in order to repent therein, will not depart from the Fire in which Allah made them burn on account of their disbelief, and their regret there will not save them at that moment, but therein they will abide forever.

A note is then added. In this lies the proof that Allah gives the lie to those who claim that the punishment of the people of the Fire is finite and has an end.

phrases.translation: O humanity! Eat from what is lawful and good on the earth and do not follow Satan’s footsteps.
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. By eat of what is on the earth lawful and good, the address is to all people.

The footsteps of the devil are then discussed. The scholars of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of that phrase. Some of them said that the footsteps of the devil are his work, and others that they are his sins, and others that they are his obedience to him, and others that they are the vows in matters of disobedience, and the other sayings reported are close to one another in meaning, since each of them pointed to the prohibition of following the devil in his tracks and his deeds.

The proper meaning of the word is then given, that it is the distance between his two feet, and it is then used for all his tracks and paths. The meaning in the prohibition of following his footsteps is the prohibition of his path and his track in that to which he calls, which is contrary to obedience to Allah.

phrases.translation: He is truly your sworn enemy
phrases.explanation:
The address is then explained in full. Eat of the foodstuffs that have been made lawful for you through the tongue of the messenger and thereby made good for you, and not of that which has been forbidden, such as carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that over which another than Allah has been invoked. And abandon the footsteps of the devil, who ruins you and forbids you your own possessions.

The devil is then described. Truly he is to you a manifest enemy, for he has made his enmity to you manifest through his refusal to prostrate before your father and his deception of him until he caused him to be expelled from the garden.

The two words are then explained. Lawful means released, and good means pure, neither impure nor forbidden.

phrases.translation: He only incites you to commit evil and indecency, and to claim against Allah what you do not know
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. It continues the prohibition of following the footsteps of the devil, and by He only commands you the sense is that the devil commands you to do evil and the shameful and to say about Allah what you do not know.

The two words are then explained. Evil means sin, comparable to harm, derived from the saying of a person that a matter grieved him, so it is that which inflicts suffering upon the one who does it. And the shameful is a verbal noun, comparable to prosperity and adversity, and it is everything whose mention is regarded as shameful and whose hearing is detestable.

phrases.translation: When it is said to them, “Follow what Allah has revealed,” they reply, “No! We ˹only˺ follow what we found our forefathers practicing.”
phrases.explanation:
The pronoun is then discussed. Two readings are possible. The first is that the words them refer back to those who take equals besides Allah, so that when it is said to them, they say, no, we follow what we found our forefathers.

The second is that they refer to the people addressed in the preceding verse. The view preferred is then given, that they refer to the people, since this is a return from direct address to a report about an absent party. The verse was sent down concerning the Arabs of the time of ignorance.

The command is then explained. By follow what Allah has sent down, it means to act according to what Allah has sent down to His messenger, so declare lawful what He makes lawful and forbid what He forbids.

phrases.translation: ˹Would they still do so,˺ even if their forefathers had ˹absolutely˺ no understanding or guidance
phrases.explanation:
The whole verse is then set out. And when it is said to these unbelievers, eat of what Allah has made lawful for you and leave the footsteps of Satan behind you, then they show arrogance and refuse to submit to the truth, and they say, no, we follow the example of our forefathers, namely the making lawful of what they made lawful and the forbidding of what they forbade.

The closing clause is then explained. Even though their forefathers were, meaning the forefathers of these unbelievers who died in their disbelief, who understood nothing of the religion of Allah nor of His obligations and prohibitions, and who were not guided to the right path, so that others let themselves be guided by them?

phrases.translation: The example of the disbelievers ˹not responding to the Messenger’s warning˺ is like a flock not comprehending the calls and cries of the shepherd.
phrases.explanation:
The meaning of the verse is then discussed. The scholars of interpretation differed concerning it.

The first interpretation is then given. The meaning is that the likeness of the disbeliever, in his scant understanding of what Allah lays before him in His Book and in his poor acceptance of that to which he is called, namely the profession of the oneness of Allah, is as the likeness of the head of cattle that hears the sound when it is called out to but does not understand what is said to it.

The name of the one who said this is given, together with a poem in which the caller says to his sheep that his soul has shown him nothing but error in solitude.

phrases.translation: ˹They are wilfully˺ deaf, dumb and blind so they have no understanding
phrases.explanation:
Another interpretation is then given. The likeness of those who disbelieve in their invoking of their gods and their idols, which neither hear nor understand, is as the likeness of one who calls out to something hearing nothing but a shout and a call, that being the echo.

The interpretation preferred is then given. It is the first, namely that the likeness of the admonition of the disbeliever and his admonisher is as the likeness of one who calls out to his flock and his calling them thereto, for it hears his calling out but does not understand his words. A point of grammar is added, that the omission of the word for admonition is permissible.

The reason for choosing this interpretation is given. The verse was revealed concerning the Jews, who were not adherents of idols, and the evidence is the verses that precede it and follow it, so what lies between them is more fittingly a report about them.

The closing words are then explained. By deaf, dumb and blind, the sense is that they are deaf to the truth so that they do not hear it, dumb in that they are speechless with respect to proclaiming the truth, and blind to the guidance so that they do not see it. A point of grammar is added, that the nominative in those words accrues on account of the beginning of a sentence.

phrases.translation: O believers! Eat from the good things We have provided for you. And give thanks to Allah if you ˹truly˺ worship Him ˹alone˺
phrases.explanation:
The address is explained first. By O you who believe, the sense is those who have held Allah and His messenger to be true, who have surrendered themselves to servitude before Allah, and who have submitted to Him.

The command is then explained. Eat of the good things with which We have provided you means eat of the permitted provision which has been made lawful for you and became good for you, namely of that which you yourselves declared forbidden though it had not been forbidden to you. And be grateful to Allah means praise Allah for the blessings He has provided you. If it is truly Him whom you worship means if you submit to His command and are obedient.

phrases.translation: He has only forbidden you ˹to eat˺ carrion, blood, swine, and what is slaughtered in the name of any other than Allah.
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. He has only forbidden you the carrion and the blood and the flesh of swine and that over which at the slaughtering a name other than that of Allah has been invoked. The sense is that the believers are not to forbid for themselves what was not forbidden.

A point of grammar is then given. The word for only is a single particle, and for that reason the carrion and the blood stand in the accusative, and no other case is permissible with the carrion. But if it were two particles, then the carrion would stand in the nominative, and the meaning would be that what Allah has forbidden is the carrion, the blood and the flesh of swine alone.

Some of the reciters did recite it thus, and it is not permissible to recite that way, because of the agreement of the reciters upon the contrary. Two further possibilities are set out if the word for forbidden is read passively.

The correct judgment is then given. The lightening and the doubling in the letter are two well-known forms, both in recitation and in the speech of the Arabs, and with either a reciter recites it correctly.

The last item is explained. That over which at the slaughtering a name other than that of Allah has been invoked means that which is slaughtered for the false deities and the idols.

phrases.translation: But if someone is compelled by necessity—neither driven by desire nor exceeding immediate need—they will not be sinful.
phrases.explanation:
The exception is explained first. By but whoever is compelled by necessity, the sense is that whoever is driven by the necessity of hunger to that which has been forbidden, and is in the condition described, has no sin upon him in eating it if he eats it.

A point of grammar is then given. The phrase without being desirous stands in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier for whoever, so the sense is that whoever is compelled without being desirous and without transgressing and then eats it, for him that is permitted. It has also been said that the meaning is whoever is forced to eat it and then eats it, upon him is no sin.

The two phrases are then discussed. Some said that without being desirous or transgressing means without desiring the forbidden in his eating and without overstepping the limit of what is permitted him. Others said that it means without desiring it out of appetite and without overstepping the limit beyond what is indispensable for him.

The statement preferred is then given. Whoever is compelled by necessity, without being desirous by eating what is forbidden him, and without overstepping the limit in his eating, while he has the possibility and the capacity to refrain from eating it because of something else that Allah has permitted him. The word for transgressing is then examined, and it has been said that it means without eating so much that he becomes sated but only as much as keeps him alive.

The closing words are then explained. Upon him is no sin means that whoever eats that in the condition described has no liability for so eating it and no fault.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation:
The exposition of the meaning is then given. It is the interpretation of the words Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

By Allah is Forgiving, Merciful, the sense is that Allah overlooks what has gone before from error, sin and disobedience in the time of ignorance, if you obey Allah in your Islam, abstain from eating what He has forbidden you, and leave off following Satan in that which you held forbidden in that time, out of your obedience to Satan and the following of his footsteps, of that which He has not forbidden you.

Then He is overlooking it on your behalf and leaving off your punishment for it, and He is merciful toward you if you obey Him.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those who hide Allah’s revelations, trading them for a fleeting gain consume nothing but fire into their bellies.
phrases.explanation:
The people described are explained first. By those who conceal what Allah has sent down of the Book, the sense is the scribes of the Jews, who concealed from the people the matter of the messenger and his prophethood while they found it recorded in the Torah, in exchange for bribes they received for that.

The phrase about the price is then explained. And sell it for a paltry price means they purchase something with it, and the meaning is that with their concealing of what they concealed regarding the matter of the messenger they purchased a paltry price, since what they received for distorting the Book of Allah and explaining it in an incorrect manner was only paltry worldly goods.

phrases.translation: Allah will neither speak to them on the Day of Judgment, nor will He purify them. And they will suffer a painful punishment
phrases.explanation:
The first half is explained at length. Those who conceal what Allah has sent down of the Book regarding the matter of the messenger in exchange for the wretched bribery given to them, for which they distort the signs of Allah, eat nothing in their bellies but the Fire, that is, nothing but that which causes them to enter the Fire.

A question is then raised about whether eating can take place somewhere other than in the belly, and the answer is given that the Arabs do say that one became hungry in other than his belly, and so it was said in their bellies.

The closing clause is then explained. Nor purify them means nor purify them of the defilement of their sins and disbelief, and a painful punishment means an agonizing one.

phrases.translation: They are the ones who trade guidance for misguidance and forgiveness for punishment.
phrases.explanation:
The clause is explained at length. By those are they who have purchased error for guidance and chastisement for forgiveness, the sense is that they are those who have taken error and abandoned guidance, and who have taken that which makes them deserve the chastisement of Allah on the day of resurrection, and who have abandoned that which would make them deserve His forgiveness and good pleasure.

He contented Himself with mentioning the chastisement and the forgiveness without naming the cause that brings about deserving these two, because those who hear it understand its meaning and its intent, and the import of the phrase was expounded earlier.

phrases.translation: How persistent are they in pursuit of the Fire
phrases.explanation:
The sentence is discussed. The people of interpretation differed concerning the explanation of it. Some of them said that the meaning is how audacious they are in performing the deed that brings them near to the Fire. Others said that it is an exclamation of wonder, how intense is their audacity toward the Fire through their performing the deeds of the people of the Fire.

The explanation of each is then given. For those who read it as an exclamation of wonder, the sense is how intense is their audacity, through their performing what they have performed, toward that which makes them deserve the Fire, just as He said, cursed be man, how ungrateful he is. For those who read it as a question, the sense is what makes them steadfast toward the Fire, while no one has steadfastness toward it.

The view preferred is then given. How audacious they are toward the chastisement of the Fire, and how greatly they perform the deeds of its inhabitants, and the reason is that it has been transmitted from the Arabs, how audacious is so-and-so toward Allah, and Allah causes His creatures to wonder only through making manifest the report about those who conceal what He has sent down.

A closing note is then added. One contented oneself with mentioning the Fire without naming its chastisement, as one says how greatly your generosity resembles that of Hatim.

phrases.translation: That is because Allah has revealed the Book in truth. And surely those who differ regarding it are totally engrossed in opposition
phrases.explanation:
The reference is discussed first. There was disagreement over what is meant by that.

One view is then given. That means the deed of theirs, namely their audacity in the face of the punishment of the Fire and their concealing what Allah sent down concerning the messenger.

The view preferred is then given. That refers to all that the statement comprised, of His informing about the deeds of the rabbis of the Jews and what He has prepared for them of punishment. A point of grammar is then added, that for that there are two case endings, nominative and accusative.

The second half is then explained. By those who differed concerning the Book, the sense is the Jews and the Christians, who differed concerning the Book of Allah, the Jews disbelieving in what Allah related therein concerning Jesus, so they are in a dispute far from the truth.

phrases.translation: Righteousness is not in turning your faces towards the east or the west. Rather, the righteous are those who believe in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Books, and the prophets;
phrases.explanation:
The meaning of the verse is discussed. The scholars of interpretation differed. Some of them said that piety is not the prayer alone but consists of the qualities set forth in the verse. Others said that Allah meant the Jews and Christians.

The view preferred is then given. It is that of the two scholars who said that the Jews and the Christians are meant. So piety is not that some of you turn east and some west, but pious is he who believes in Allah and the last day, the angels and the book.

A further point is then added. It is also possible that the meaning is that pious is he who believes in Allah, in which case the word for piety would be a verbal noun in the place of the agent.

phrases.translation: who give charity out of their cherished wealth to relatives, orphans, the poor, ˹needy˺ travellers, beggars, and for freeing captives;
phrases.explanation:
The giving is explained first. By and who gives wealth in spite of his love for it, the sense is that he gave his wealth at the moment of his love for it, his greed with it and his stinginess over it.

The wayfarer is then explained. It is the one who passes by the man while traveling, and the scholars differed about his description, some of them saying that he is the guest, and the traveler is called son of the road because of his attachment to the road during his travel.

Another view is then given. The first wealth is the alms-tax, but Allah described the giving by the believers to those to whom they gave it, so He made known the places where they must spend their alms, and then indicated that the wealth the people gave is the obligatory alms-tax.

The fulfilling of covenants is then explained. And those who fulfill their covenant when they make a covenant means those who do not break the covenant of Allah after making it, but fulfill it and complete it in accordance with that over which they made it.

phrases.translation: who establish prayer, pay alms-tax, and keep the pledges they make;
phrases.explanation:
The freeing of slaves is then explained. By and for the freeing of necks, the sense is the freeing of necks from slavery, and these are the contract-slaves who strive to free their necks by fulfilling their manumission contracts, on which basis they are separated from their masters.

The prayer and the alms-tax are then explained. By and who performs the prayer, the sense is that he performed it constantly with its conditions, and by and who gives the alms-tax, that he gave it as Allah has prescribed for him.

A question is then raised about whether there is a due in wealth that must be discharged as an obligation other than the alms-tax, and it is answered that the scholars of interpretation differed about this, and the reports naming what they said are given.

phrases.translation: and who are patient in times of suffering, adversity, and in ˹the heat of˺ battle. It is they who are true ˹in faith˺,
phrases.explanation:
The meaning is then given. And those who restrain themselves, in adversity and in distress and in the hour of battle, from that which Allah disapproves of for them, and who hold the soul fast to that which He has commanded them of obedience to Him.

The phrase is then examined. The grammarians differed about it, some of them saying that adversity and distress is a verbal noun that has come upon the pattern of the broken plural and has no form of the sound plural, since it is a noun, and they have used the sound plural in the qualifier without its taking the broken plural form. A point of grammar is then added, that the phrase lion of the battle-array and man of insight is placed in the accusative in the manner of praise, while the noun before it was in the genitive, because it was a qualification of the singular.

The hour of battle is then explained. It means the time of the intensity of armed combat in war. A description of war is then given, that war is impregnated as the she-camel is impregnated and brings forth twins in one belly, and the ruddy one of Ad is explained as the ruddy one of Thamud, who hamstrung the she-camel of Allah, whereupon their Lord destroyed them.

phrases.translation: and it is they who are mindful ˹of Allah˺
phrases.explanation:
The interpretation of the verse is then given. And who gave wealth, while he loves it, is covetous of amassing it and is stingy with it, to his kinsfolk, and thereby maintained the ties of kinship with them.

The truthful ones are then explained. By those are the ones who were truthful, the sense is the one who believed in Allah and the last day and whom He described with the description with which He described them in this verse, so whoever performs these things is faithful to Allah in his faith and realized his word with his deeds.

The God-fearing are then explained. And those are the ones who feared the punishment of Allah and therefore avoided disobedience to Him and dreaded His threat, so they did not transgress His limits, and they feared Him and therefore performed the observance of His obligations.

phrases.translation: O believers! ˹The law of˺ retaliation is set for you in cases of murder—a free man for a free man, a slave for a slave, and a female for a female.
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. Retaliation for the slain is prescribed for you, the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female, and the sense is that it is obligatory upon you.

An objection is then answered. When a free person kills a free person, then the blood of the killer is an equivalent for the blood of the slain, and the retaliation strikes him and no one else, so do not transgress toward one who did not kill.

The people differed about the occasion of the verse. Some of them said that it was revealed concerning a people who were not content with the blood of a slave for their slain one until they killed his master. Others said that it was revealed concerning two groups who fought in the time of the messenger. Others said that it is a command to offset the blood money of the free, the slave, the man and the woman with mutual reckoning.

The ruling that the verse indicates is then applied. The reports of the messenger reinforce one another that the life of the free man is offset by way of retaliation against the life of the free woman, and it is agreed by all Muslims that it is forbidden for a man to destroy a limb of his body for a compensation, so the life of the free man serves as retaliation for the free woman's life. All are agreed without exception that the mutual reckoning of rights is not obligatory, so the correct view is the one that has been voiced.

phrases.translation: But if the offender is pardoned by the victim’s guardian,
phrases.explanation:
It has also been said that the meaning of retaliation here is the mutual offsetting of the blood money of some of the slain against others.

The exegetes differed over the clause whoever is pardoned something by his brother, and some said that it means whoever of the unlawful killing is remitted something.

A further view is then given from the interpretation transmitted from the early authorities, namely that whoever is remitted what was obligatory upon him for his brother, then there is a demand by the next of kin and payment by the killer.

The view preferred is then given. Whoever is remitted what was obligatory upon him for his brother of retaliation, for a blood money he accepts, then there is a demand in a fitting manner and payment by the killer.

phrases.translation: then blood-money should be decided fairly
phrases.explanation:
By then let there be a fitting demand, the sense is that there is a demand for what Allah has granted him as a right against the killer of his kinsman, without his being charged with more than what he is entitled to regarding the ages of the blood-money camels.

A point of grammar is then added. Some of the philologists said that its nominative rests on the meaning that upon the one who is pardoned something by his brother rests a fitting demand, and that is the view held here, whereas in the phrase then strike the necks the accusative is correct, because it is an exhortation to kill upon meeting the enemy.

phrases.translation: and payment should be made courteously. This is a concession and a mercy from your Lord.
phrases.explanation:
That is a lightening from your Lord and a mercy is explained. By that, the sense is this concerning which I have ruled and prescribed for you, namely My permitting you to refrain from retaliation upon the killer of your slain one for a blood money that you accept, which I had forbidden to the communities before you, so it is a lightening from Me and mercy for you.

The reading of those who say that retaliation here is the offsetting of the blood monies is then explained, that this which I have done with you is a lightening from Me of the heaviness of what rested upon you, and mercy for you.

phrases.translation: But whoever transgresses after that will suffer a painful punishment
phrases.explanation:
But whoever transgresses after that is explained. Whoever transgresses what Allah has granted him, after he has accepted the blood money, by way of transgression and injustice toward what He has not appointed for him, namely the killing of the killer of his kinsman and the shedding of his blood, for him is a painful punishment.

The exegetes differed concerning that punishment. Some of them said that it is the killing of him as retaliation for the one he killed after the acceptance of the blood money from him. And some of them said that it is a chastisement with which the ruler punishes him, according to the measure of what he deems fitting.

phrases.translation: There is ˹security of˺ life for you in ˹the law of˺ retaliation,
phrases.explanation:
The clause is explained first. By and in legal retaliation there is life for you, O people of insight, the sense is that for you, O people of understanding, there is in what I have prescribed for you, namely retaliation in cases of killing, wounds and head injuries, that restrains some of you.

The scholars of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of this, and some of them said something along the lines of what has been said, and the report naming who said so is given.

Another view is then given. The meaning is that in legal retaliation against the killer there is a continued existence for others, because according to the judgment of Allah, for the one killed none is killed except his killer, whereas in ignorance they killed the man for the woman.

phrases.translation: O people of reason, so that you may become mindful ˹of Allah˺
phrases.explanation:
The address is then explained. O people of insight means O people of understanding, and the word for minds is the plural of the intellect. And the address is directed specifically to the people of understanding, because they are the ones who comprehend the command and prohibition of Allah and reflect upon His signs and proofs, unlike others.

The closing clause is then explained. So that you may become God-fearing means so that you may fear retaliation and thereby refrain from killing.

A note is then added on the wording. The expression for restraining is taken from one who holds another back, and it is used with a soul that is covetous, meaning that they are restrained from what they covet and desire.

phrases.translation: It is prescribed that when death approaches any of you—if they leave something of value—a will should be made in favour of parents and immediate family with fairness.
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. It is prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you and he leaves behind good, to make a bequest in favor of the parents and the nearest relatives in a fitting manner, a duty upon the God-fearing.

The correct view is then given. It is that of al-Zuhri, for both little property and much property fall under the designation of good, and Allah did not specify it by a limit nor except anything from it, so that it would not be permissible to divert the outward meaning toward a hidden one. So everyone whose death approaches while he has property, little or much, is obligated to make a bequest from it in favor of whoever among his fathers, mothers and nearest relatives does not inherit from him, in a fitting manner.

phrases.translation: ˹This is˺ an obligation on those who are mindful ˹of Allah˺
phrases.explanation:
By it is prescribed for you, the sense is that it is imposed upon you as a duty, the bequest, when death approaches one of you and he leaves behind good, in favor of the parents and nearest relatives who do not inherit from him, in a fitting manner, one which does not exceed the third part, and a duty upon the God-fearing means it is imposed upon whoever fears Allah.

A question is then raised. Is it an obligation upon the man who possesses property to make a bequest in favor of his parents and nearest relatives who do not inherit? The answer is given. He has made known to us that He has prescribed it and imposed it as a duty, just as He says fasting is prescribed for you, and whoever neglects it while able to do so has neglected a duty.

A group then contradicts this. It is a firmly established verse, not abrogated, and when the scholars disagree about its abrogation it is not permissible to rule that it is abrogated except on the basis of a proof to which one must submit, since this ruling and that on inheritance may coexist.

Others said that it is a verse by which the ruling was obligatory and acted upon for a time, and then the verse on inheritance abrogated the bequest in favor of the parents and nearest relatives who do inherit, while the obligation remained for the others.

phrases.translation: But whoever changes the will after hearing it, the blame will only be on those who made the change. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation:
The clause is explained first. By whoever alters it after he has heard it, the sense is that whoever alters what the testator has left as a bequest, from his lawful disposition, then the sin of that alteration rests upon whoever alters it.

A question is then raised about what the word in whoever alters it refers back to, and the answer is that it refers back to something omitted from the words, namely the matter of the deceased.

The closing words are explained. By Allah is All-Hearing, the sense is that Allah hears the bequest, whether you act justly in it or deviate from the truth, and All-Knowing of what your breasts conceal.

phrases.translation: Whoever suspects an error or an injustice in the will and brings about a ˹fair˺ settlement among the parties will not be sinful. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation:
The people differed about the meaning of the verse.
