Some of them said that it is whoever is present with a sick person at the threshold of death who fears that the sick man is committing an error in his will or deliberately intending injustice in it, so there is no objection to the one who brings about reconciliation between him and his heirs by enjoining justice in his will. Others said that it is whoever, from among the kinsfolk of the deceased or the one in authority over the affairs of the Muslims, fears partiality in the will.

The most correct of these statements is then given. Whoever fears from a testator partiality or sin, namely that he deviates by an error on his part to something other than the truth, or that he deliberately intends a sin in his will, by making a will in favor of his parents and near relatives who do not inherit from him for more than is permitted him to leave to them, or that he exceeds the third or leaves the entire third while there is little property and many heirs, then there is no objection upon the one who is present with him that he brings about reconciliation between those for whom the will is made and the deceased.

The reason for this choice is then given. It has been preferred only because He said, whoever fears from a testator partiality or sin, meaning whoever fears from a testator that he will be partial or will sin, for the fear of partiality and sin exists only before their occurrence, and had that been the meaning it would have been said whoever ascertains from a testator partiality or sin.

A question is then raised about what bringing about reconciliation means, since reconciliation takes place between people who disagree, and the answer is given that bringing about reconciliation between two parties in that concerning which it is feared that disagreement will arise is of the meanings of the phrase.

The closing words are explained. By Allah is Forgiving, Merciful, the sense is that Allah is forgiving toward the testator for that to which he had incited himself of partiality and sin when he refrains from sinning in his will, and merciful toward the one who brings about reconciliation between the testator and the one against whom he wished to commit injustice in favour of another.

phrases.translation: O believers!
phrases.explanation:
The exposition of the meaning is then given. It is the interpretation of the words O you who believe, fasting is prescribed for you, as it was prescribed for those before you, so that you may become mindful of Allah.

The address is then explained. By O you who believe, the sense is those who believe in Allah and His messenger and who have affirmed and acknowledged them both, and the rest of the sentence is set out with it.

And by fasting is prescribed for you, the sense is that fasting is made obligatory upon you, in the same way as it was made obligatory upon those before you, and the purpose of it is that you may become mindful of Allah.

phrases.translation: Fasting is prescribed for you—as it was for those before you—so perhaps you will become mindful ˹of Allah˺
phrases.explanation:
The word for fasting is then examined. It is a verbal noun, from the saying of a person that I abstained from it, and its meaning is abstaining from that which Allah has commanded one to abstain from. It is also said that the horses fasted when they stopped from travelling.

The comparison with those before is then explained. As it was prescribed for those before you means it is made obligatory upon you equal to that which was made obligatory upon them, and the exegetes differed concerning whom is meant and in what sense the comparison was made.

One answer is then given, that the comparison is only because their fasting was from the evening prayer to the evening prayer, which was the obligation upon the believers when fasting was first made obligatory, and those who held this said those meant are the Christians. Others said that those meant are the people of the book.

The correct view is then given, that the comparison falls upon the time, since those before were obligated with the month of Ramadan equal to that which was obligated upon us. The closing words are then explained, that you may become God-fearing means that you may abstain from food, drink and intercourse with women in it.

phrases.translation: ˹Fast a˺ prescribed number of days. But whoever of you is ill or on a journey, then ˹let them fast˺ an equal number of days ˹after Ramaḍân˺.
phrases.explanation:
The first clause is explained first. Prescribed for you is fasting for a number of appointed days. The word for days stands in the accusative because of an elided verb, and the phrase as it was prescribed for those before you pertains to the fasting.

The view preferred is then given. Allah meant by the days of appointed days the days of the month of Ramadan, because no report has come upon which a proof can be founded that the people of Islam were prescribed any fasting other than that of Ramadan.

The second clause is then explained. Whoever of you is sick or on a journey, then a number of other days, meaning that upon him rests the fasting of the days he broke during his illness or on his journey.

phrases.translation: For those who can only fast with extreme difficulty, compensation can be made by feeding a needy person ˹for every day not fasted˺. But whoever volunteers to give more, it is better for them. And to fast is better for you, if only you knew
phrases.explanation:
The recitation is then discussed. The reading of all Muslims is and for those who are able to do it, and upon it their codices are based, and no one may deviate from it because of its transmission by all of them generation after generation.

The reciters differed concerning its meaning. Some of them said that was at the beginning, when fasting was prescribed, and that whoever of the non-travellers was able to perform it would fast it if he wished, and if he wished he would break it and ransom it until that was abrogated. Others said that it was a special ruling for the man of great age and the old woman who were indeed able to fast.

The answer is then given. The men are excluded from being intended by it, for if the women alone were meant, it would have been said and for the women who are able to perform it. And it is agreed by all that the resident healthy man who is able to fast is not permitted to break the fast and ransom it.

The meaning of the ransom is then given. It is the compensation, and the sense is that upon those who are able to perform the fasting there rests a compensation, the feeding of a needy person for each day that he breaks.

The recitation of the last clause is then discussed. Some read it with the ransom annexed to the food, and others with the two words separated, and the more correct is the annexation, since the ransom is the name of the action and is something other than the food with which the fasting is ransomed. And the reading of the needy person in the singular is preferred, because in clarifying the ruling of whoever breaks one day there lies access to the ruling of whoever breaks the whole month.

The closing clause is then explained. And that you fast is better for you means that fasting what is prescribed for you of the month of Ramadan is better for you than that you break the fast and ransom it.

phrases.translation: Ramaḍân is the month in which the Quran was revealed as a guide for humanity with clear proofs of guidance and the standard ˹to distinguish between right and wrong˺.
phrases.explanation:
The month is explained first. The word for month is derived from the word for notoriety and making conspicuous, and one says of a man that he brandished his sword when he draws it from the sheath, and likewise the month became conspicuous when its new moon appears. As for Ramadan, some claimed it was so named because of the intensity of the heat in it, so that the young camels were scorched by the ground.

The case of the word is then explained. It stands in the nominative in relation to the days mentioned before, and it is also permissible that the nominative carries the meaning that that is the month of Ramadan, and that the month has been prescribed for you. Some reciters read it in the accusative.

The two phrases are explained. A guidance for mankind means a guide for mankind to the path of truth, and clear proofs means clear signs of guidance, that is the exposition that points to the limits of Allah and His duties.

phrases.translation: So whoever is present this month, let them fast. But whoever is ill or on a journey, then ˹let them fast˺ an equal number of days ˹after Ramaḍân˺.
phrases.explanation:
The clause is explained first. Whoever is ill or on a journey during the month and on that account breaks the fast, upon him rests the fasting of the days that he broke, on days other than the days of Ramadan.

The people differed over the illness in which breaking the fast was permitted, and some said that it is the illness in which the affected person cannot perform his prayer standing. The meaning of a number of other days is then given.

A question is then raised. If that is the interpretation, what of the man who was ill or on a journey and yet fasted the month? It is answered that the people of knowledge differed over all of this.

The indication of the verse is then given as sufficient. There is no greater hardship than that there should be imposed upon the man who fasted on his journey other days, and the saying that Allah desires ease for you is enough.

The reports about the messenger are then set out, that when he was asked about fasting on a journey he said, if you wish, fast, and if you wish, break the fast. A question is then raised about the report that it is not of piety to fast on a journey.

phrases.translation: Allah intends ease for you, not hardship,
phrases.explanation:
The correct view is then given. The illness in which Allah has permitted the breaking of the fast is that of the man whom fasting exhausts in an unbearable manner, and for him there is the breaking of the fast and the making up of other days, since otherwise he would be burdened with hardship and the ease would be denied him. As for the man whom fasting does not exhaust, he has the status of the healthy person who can bear fasting.

A second statement is then given, and it is the most in accord with the correct view, since it is agreed by all that an ill person who fasts the month while he belongs to those for whom breaking is permitted has his fasting suffice him.

phrases.translation: so that you may complete the prescribed period and proclaim the greatness of Allah for guiding you, and perhaps you will be grateful
phrases.explanation:
By and that you complete the number, the sense is that you complete the days that you broke, on other days imposed upon you to make up, after your recovery or your becoming resident.

The next clause is then explained. By and that you magnify Allah for that to which He has guided you, the sense is that you exalt Allah by the remembrance of Him on account of the guidance with which He has favoured you, which He withheld from others to whom the fasting of Ramadan had been prescribed.

The closing words are then explained. By and that you may perhaps be grateful, the sense is that you may thank Allah for that with which He has favoured you, and the word for perhaps here means that.

phrases.translation: When My servants ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about Me: I am truly near. I respond to one’s prayer when they call upon Me. So let them respond ˹with obedience˺ to Me and believe in Me, perhaps they will be guided ˹to the Right Way˺
phrases.explanation:
The question is explained first. By and when My servants ask you about Me, the sense is that they ask where I am, and indeed I am close to them, I hear their supplication and I answer the supplication of the one among them who supplicates.

The occasion of the revelation is then given. Some of them said that it was sent down because of a questioner who asked the prophet, saying, is our Lord near so that we may confide in Him, or is He far away so that we must call out to Him? Others said that it was sent down as an answer to the question of a group who asked the prophet, at what hour should we call upon Allah? And others said that it was sent down as an answer to a group who said, toward where should we call upon Him!

The clause about believing is then explained. And let them believe in Me means and let them affirm, so let them believe in Me when they respond to Me through obedience, that I stand as guarantor for them behind their obedience, regarding the reward for it and My honour upon them.

The closing clause is then explained. That they may be rightly guided means so let them respond to Me through obedience and let them believe in Me, so that they affirm that upon their obedience there follows reward from Me.

The meaning of the supplication is then given at length. The first is that by the supplication is meant acting according to that which Allah has urged and commanded, so the sense is that I am near to the one who obeys Me, and I answer him with reward for his obedience, and the calling is the servant's request to his Lord for that which He has promised the faithful as reward.

phrases.translation: It has been made permissible for you to be intimate with your wives during the nights preceding the fast. Your spouses are a garment for you as you are for them. Allah knows that you were deceiving yourselves. So He has accepted your repentance and pardoned you.
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. It has been made lawful for you means it has been released and permitted to you, and the night of the fast means on the night of the fast, and the word used is a euphemism for sexual intercourse.

The metaphor of the garment is then examined. Your women are a garment for you and you are a garment for them, and the first meaning is that each of the two is made a garment for the other because of their being together during sleep, under one robe, and the joining of bodies.

The other possibility is then given, that each of the two is made a garment for the other because he finds rest in the other, as He has made the night a garment and the wife a repose in which he finds rest. A third sense is then added, that what covers a thing is said to be its garment, so each of you is a covering for the other.

phrases.translation: So now you may be intimate with them and seek what Allah has prescribed for you.
phrases.explanation:
The word for intercourse is then explained. It is the coming together of skin with skin, and the skin of the man is his outer skin, and Allah has described by these words only sexual intercourse, so the sense is that now that He has made lawful for you intercourse with your women, then have intercourse with them until the dawn breaks, that is the becoming distinct of the white thread from the black thread of the dawn.

The correct view is then given at length. By seek what Allah has prescribed for you, the sense is that you should seek what Allah the Exalted has decreed for you, and He means only that you should seek that which He has prescribed for you in the Preserved Tablet to be lawful, so that it is released to you. The seeking of the child, when the man seeks it by his intercourse with the woman, belongs to what has been prescribed for him, and the meaning most consonant with the apparent form of the verse is that it means seek what Allah has prescribed for you of offspring.

phrases.translation: ˹You may˺ eat and drink until you see the light of dawn breaking the darkness of night, then complete the fast until nightfall. Do not be intimate with your spouses while you are meditating in the mosques. These are the limits set by Allah, so do not exceed them. This is how Allah makes His revelations clear to people, so they may become mindful ˹of Him˺
phrases.explanation:
The people of interpretation differed concerning this. Some said that by the white thread is meant the light of day, and by the black thread the darkness of night, and the interpretation according to that view is that you eat at night in the month of your fasting, and drink, and have intercourse with your women, seeking what Allah has prescribed for you of offspring.

The ground of that view is then given, namely the whiteness of the dawn and the blackness of the night. And others said that the white thread is the light of the sun, and the black thread is the blackness of the night.

phrases.translation: Do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly, nor deliberately bribe authorities in order to devour a portion of others’ property, knowing that it is a sin
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. Let not one of you consume the wealth of another through falsehood, and He made the one who consumes the wealth of his brother through falsehood equal to the one who consumes his own wealth through falsehood.

The second half is then explained. And do not litigate with your wealth before the judges, to consume a portion of the wealth of people through sin, while you know. And by through sin, the meaning is through the forbidden which Allah has declared forbidden, and while you know means that you deliberately consume that with premeditation.

The word for lowering is then explained. Its origin is the letting down by a man of the bucket into a well on a rope, and it is said of the one who argues for his claim that he adduced such and such as argument.

phrases.translation: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about the phases of the moon. Say, “They are a means for people to determine time and pilgrimage.”
phrases.explanation:
The question is then set out in the words of the Exalted, that they ask you about the new moons, and the answer is that they are appointed times for mankind and for the pilgrimage.

The occasion is then explained. It has been transmitted that the messenger was asked about the waxing and waning of the new moons and the variation in their states, whereupon Allah sent down this verse as an answer to that about which they asked. The mention of the reports concerning that is then given.

The second half is then explained. By and the pilgrimage, the sense is that He also made them an appointed time for your pilgrimage, so that through them you may know the time of your rites and your pilgrimage.

phrases.translation: Righteousness is not in entering your houses from the back doors. Rather, righteousness is to be mindful ˹of Allah˺. So enter your homes through their ˹proper˺ doors,
phrases.explanation:
It has been said that the verse was sent down concerning a people who, when they entered the state of ritual consecration, would not enter their houses through their doors.

The explanation of the verse is then given. Righteousness does not consist, O people, in your entering the houses in the state of your consecration from their backs, but righteous is he who fears Allah, so fears Him and avoids His prohibitions, and obeys Him by performing His obligations. And as for entering the houses from their backs, in that there is no righteousness toward Allah. So enter them from whichever side you wish, through their doors or otherwise.

phrases.translation: and be mindful of Allah so you may be successful
phrases.explanation:
The closing words are then explained. And fear Allah, O people, so be on your guard against Him and hold Him in awe by obeying Him in what He has imposed upon you of His obligations, and by avoiding what He has forbidden you, so that you succeed.

And the meaning of success is then set out, that you may thereby attain your desires with Him, and thereby reach the abiding in His gardens and the eternity in His bliss.

A note is then added on the word for consecration. The one who is severe and harsh in his religion was called such, and those who so abstained in the time of ignorance were the people of Mecca, who in that state did not melt fat or cook curd.

phrases.translation: Fight in the cause of Allah ˹only˺ against those who wage war against you, but do not exceed the limits. Allah does not like transgressors
phrases.explanation:
The question of abrogation is discussed first, and the correct view given. It is the statement that Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz made, since the claim of a verse being abrogated while it is possible that it is not, without proof, is arbitrary.

The explanation of the verse is then given. And fight, O believers, in the way of Allah, and His way is the path He has made clear and the religion He has prescribed, so fight in obedience to Me and according to what I have prescribed for you, and call to whoever has turned away from it until they return to obedience to Me.

The last clause is then explained. Do not kill a newborn, nor a woman, nor whoever gives you the jizyah, and those who overstep His limits are transgressors.

phrases.translation: Kill them wherever you come upon them and drive them out of the places from which they have driven you out.
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. Kill, O believers, those among the polytheists who wage war against you, wherever you encounter them in a condition in which you are able to overcome them and kill them.

The word is then explained. Its meaning with regard to a matter is to be skilled and sharp-sighted in it, and one says of a man that he is truly on his guard in battle when he has keen perception of the places where killing can be done, and the word has another meaning, namely the straightening. So kill them in every place where you are able to kill them and where you have keen perception of the places where they can be killed.

phrases.translation: For persecution is far worse than killing.
phrases.explanation:
The clause is then explained. And the tribulation is worse than killing means that ascribing partners to Allah is worse than killing. The origin of the word for tribulation is trial and testing, and it was explained earlier.

The meaning of it is then set out. The trial of the believer in his religion, until he apostatises from it and thus, after his Islam, becomes one who ascribes partners to Allah, is worse for him and more harmful than that he be killed while remaining steadfast in his religion, holding fast to it and adhering to the truth in it. So the verse is set out on that footing.

phrases.translation: And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque unless they attack you there. If they do so, then fight them—that is the reward of the disbelievers
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. And do not fight them at the sacred mosque until they fight you there, but if they fight you, then kill them, such is the recompense of the unbelievers.

The recitation is then discussed. The reciters of Medina and Mecca read it as do not fight them at the sacred mosque until they fight you there, so that you do not begin the fighting against the polytheists there until they begin it against you. And most of the reciters of Kufa read it as do not kill them until they kill you there.

The correct reading is then given. It is the first, because Allah did not command His prophet and his companions to surrender themselves to the polytheists until they had first made one slain among themselves.

phrases.translation: But if they cease, then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation:
The exposition of the meaning is then given. It is the interpretation of the words But if they cease, then Allah is indeed Forgiving, Merciful.

The clause is then explained. If the unbelievers whom you fight cease from fighting you and from their unbelief in Allah, and they desist from that and repent, then Allah is indeed forgiving with regard to the sins of whoever among them believes and repents from his polytheism and returns to Allah from his acts of disobedience and the days that have passed, and merciful toward him in his hereafter through His favour to him and by granting him what He grants to the people of obedience of reward.

phrases.translation: Fight against them ˹if they persecute you˺ until there is no more persecution,
phrases.explanation:
The exposition of the meaning is then given. It is the interpretation of the words And fight them until there is no more trial and the religion belongs to Allah.

The command is explained first. And fight the polytheists who fight you until there is no more trial, meaning until there is no more ascribing of partners to Allah, and until none is worshipped besides Him, and the worship of idols, gods and equals ceases, and worship and obedience belong to Allah alone to the exclusion of the other false deities and idols. That is the sense of the religion belonging to Allah alone and to no one else.

phrases.translation: and ˹your˺ devotion will be to Allah ˹alone˺.
phrases.explanation:
The words are then explained. When they abhorred the religion, he means when they abhorred obedience and refused it. And his word that he humbled them means he humbled them, subdued them and compelled them to obedience. And his word successive means the one overtaking the other, and to assault against his enemy means he leapt upon him and attacked him.

As for the religion which Allah mentions in this place, that is the worship of and obedience to Allah in His command and prohibition.

And his word that he humbled the Ribab means he humbled them, subdued them, and compelled them to obedience, and his word successive means the one overtaking the other.

phrases.translation: If they stop ˹persecuting you˺, let there be no hostility except against the aggressors
phrases.explanation:
The clause is explained first. But if the unbelievers who fight you cease fighting you, and they enter your community of faith, and they acknowledge what Allah has imposed upon you as obligations, and they abandon that which they were upon, namely the worship of idols, then abandon the hostility against them, the fighting of them and the struggle against them. For it is not fitting that hostility be committed except against the wrongdoers, and they are those who ascribe partners to Allah and those who have abandoned His worship and worship another than their Creator.

This is entirely comparable to His saying that Allah mocks them, and to the saying that they ridicule them and Allah ridicules them, and the explanation of this and of similar cases was set forth earlier.

phrases.translation: ˹There will be retaliation in˺ a sacred month for ˹an offence in˺ a sacred month, and all violations will bring about retaliation. So, if anyone attacks you, retaliate in the same manner.
phrases.explanation:
The sacred month is explained first. By the sacred month for the sacred month, the sense is the month of Dhu al-Qada, in which the messenger intended to perform the lesser pilgrimage of al-Hudaybiya, and in which the polytheists of Mecca barred him from access to the sacred house. He made peace that year on the condition that he would return the following year, enter Mecca and remain there three days. When the following year came he set out with his companions, and he completed his lesser pilgrimage and returned to Medina.

The name of the month is then explained. Allah called it the sacred month only because the Arabs in the time of ignorance held fighting and killing to be forbidden therein and laid down their weapons, and they had named it Dhu al-Qada because of their sitting therein, abstaining from raids and wars.

The more fitting of the two interpretations is then given, that which is transmitted from the one who said that, since the verses before it are nothing other than a command to fight in a particular manner, and the sentence about aggression stands only in the context of that command, and Allah did not prescribe fighting for the believers except after the migration.

From this it is known that the sentence is Medinan and not Meccan, and that it is equal to the saying, fight those who fight you, so whoever commits aggression against you in the sanctuary then commit aggression against him by means of fighting, proportionate to his aggression against you. And the other interpretation is then given, that the word means the rushing and pouncing.

phrases.translation: ˹But˺ be mindful of Allah, and know that Allah is with those mindful ˹of Him˺
phrases.explanation:
The exposition of the meaning is then given. It is the interpretation of the words And fear Allah, and know that Allah is with the God-fearing.

The closing words are then explained. And fear Allah, O believers, with regard to His sacred things and His limits, that you commit no transgression therein and do not overstep therein what He has set forth and bounded for you, for the sacred things are a matter of retaliation.

And know that Allah loves the God-fearing, who fear Him by fulfilling His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions, and the sense of being with the God-fearing is that He gives them His help and His companionship in what they do.

phrases.translation: Spend in the cause of Allah
phrases.explanation:
The meanings are discussed first. Some of them said that what is meant is that the way of Allah is His path along which He has commanded marching out against His enemy among the polytheists, and that do not cast yourselves into destruction means do not abandon spending in the way of Allah, for Allah will recompense you for it with a reward and will soon provide for you in this life. Others said that the meaning is that spending is intended, and that do not cast yourselves into destruction means do not march out in the way of Allah without provisions and without the means to bear it. Others said that it means through the sins you have committed, so that you despair of the mercy of Allah, but hope for His mercy and perform good deeds.

The correct view is then given. Allah commanded spending in His way, and His way is the path He has prescribed for His servants and made clear to them, so the meaning is that you spend in making strong His religion through struggle against your enemy who has set up war against you on account of disbelief in Him, and He forbade them to cast themselves into destruction with their own hands.

And since all these meanings can be borne by the words, and Allah has not singled out any of them above another, the correct view is that Allah has forbidden us to cast ourselves down with our own hands into that in which our ruin lies, and to surrender ourselves to ruin, namely the punishment, by abandoning the obligations He has imposed upon us. It is therefore not permitted for us to engage in anything Allah disapproves of, that by which we deserve His punishment.

phrases.translation: and do not let your own hands throw you into destruction ˹by withholding˺.
phrases.explanation:
A question is raised about the reason for the insertion of the particle in the words and do not cast yourselves with your own hands, since it is customary in well-known usage to say I threw so-and-so a dirham and not with a dirham.

The answer is then given. It has been said that it is added, just as the speaker adds the particle in his words I pulled at the garment and I pulled the garment, and I clung to it and I clung it, and in the saying of the one who brings forth oil, while it is in fact brings forth the oil.

The word for destruction is then examined. It is formed on the pattern that means perishing, and its origin is perishing.

phrases.translation: And do good, for Allah certainly loves the good-doers
phrases.explanation:
The closing words are then explained. By and do good, the sense is do good, O believers, in fulfilling the obligations that I have imposed upon you, in avoiding what I have commanded you to avoid of acts of disobedience to Me, in spending in My way, and in the returning of the strong among you to the weak who is in need, for I love those who do good in that.

The sense is then narrowed down. Some of them said that its meaning is to have a good opinion of Allah, and the reports naming who said that are given. And others said that it means to do good by returning to the needy, and the reports naming who said that are given.

phrases.translation: Complete the pilgrimage and minor pilgrimage for Allah. But if prevented ˹from proceeding˺, then ˹offer˺ whatever sacrificial animals you can afford. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal reaches its destination. But if any of you is ill or has a scalp ailment ˹requiring shaving˺,
phrases.explanation:
The scholars differed concerning the prevention for which Allah imposed upon the one afflicted by it the duty of whatever is easy of a sacrificial animal. Some of them said that it is every impediment or detainer that impeded the person in the state of consecration.

The more correct interpretation is then given. If the fear of an enemy, or an illness, or an affliction prevents you from coming to the house, that is to say, your fear or your illness causes you to hold yourselves back, and therefore it was said if you are prevented, because the mention of the fear and the illness has been omitted.

The occasion of the verse is then given. It was sent down on the occasion of the lesser pilgrimage of al-Hudaybiya, at which one was prevented.

phrases.translation: then compensate either by fasting, charity, or a sacrificial offering.
phrases.explanation:
The question is then raised. If those who refused that the sheep falls under whatever is easy of a sacrificial animal held that it does not deserve the name of sacrificial animal, any more than if someone were to offer a chicken or an egg, then it is said that if there were a disagreement about the chicken and the egg like that about the sheep, their way would be the same.

But since that which is less than the yearling of the sheep and the two-year-old of the goats is excluded from being a valid sacrificial animal, by the proof transmitted from the prophet, that was excluded from being intended.

phrases.translation: In times of peace, you may combine the pilgrimage and minor pilgrimage then make the sacrificial offering you can afford. Whoever cannot afford that ˹offering˺, let them fast three days during pilgrimage and seven after returning ˹home˺—completing ten. These offerings are for those who do not live near the Sacred House. And be mindful of Allah, and know that Allah is severe in punishment
phrases.explanation:
The scholars then differed again concerning the meaning of whatever is easy of a sacrificial animal. Some of them said that it is a sheep, and the report naming who said that is given, and in one of them a man who had performed the lesser pilgrimage is told a sheep.

And others said that it is something from the camels and the cattle, but of a younger age than the regular age, and the report naming who said that is given, and there the highest of it is a sacrificial camel, the middle a cow, and the least a sheep.

And in other reports it is said that the animal is the lesser camel and the lesser cow, and that the wealthy one sends a camel and the other sends from the small livestock.

phrases.translation: ˹Commitment to˺ pilgrimage is made in appointed months.
phrases.explanation:
The months are explained first. The pilgrimage takes place in well-known months, meaning that the time of the pilgrimage is the well-known months. The months stand in the nominative because of the pilgrimage, even though the pilgrimage forms a temporal determination for them and not an adjectival qualification.

A question is then raised about the basis of those who say the pilgrimage occupies three full months, when the rites of the pilgrimage are not performed after the passing of the days of Mina. It is answered that they meant the months of the pilgrimage and not the months of the lesser pilgrimage, even though the rites are performed only in a part of them.

A further question is then raised, how the pilgrimage can be said to be months when it is two months and a part of the third. It is answered that the Arabs do not refrain, particularly with regard to temporal designations, from the use of something of the like, since one says I have not seen him for two days while one means only one day and a part of another.

The undertaking of the pilgrimage is then explained. Whoever makes the pilgrimage obligatory upon himself and binds himself to it in these months, and making it obligatory upon oneself is the firm resolve to perform everything Allah has imposed upon the pilgrim and to abstain from what He has commanded him to abstain from.

The three possibilities are then set out. The undertaking may consist of the firm resolve alone, or of the firm resolve together with the proclamation of the pilgrimage, or of the firm resolve with the man in the state of consecration through imposing it upon himself. And since the first two possibilities are invalid, the third is the correct one.

phrases.translation: Whoever commits to ˹performing˺ pilgrimage, let them stay away from intimate relations, foul language, and arguments during pilgrimage. Whatever good you do, Allah ˹fully˺ knows of it. Take ˹necessary˺ provisions ˹for the journey˺—surely the best provision is righteousness. And be mindful of Me, O people of reason
phrases.explanation:
The exegetes differed concerning the meaning by which a man undertakes the pilgrimage, after the agreement of all of them that the meaning of undertaking is obligation and binding. Some of them said that the undertaking of the pilgrimage is the pronouncing of the proclamation, and the report naming who said that is given.

They differed again concerning the word for obscenity in this place. Some said it is the uttering of obscenities to the woman in words, that he says, when we are out of the state of consecration, I will do this and that with you, without veiling it. And others said that it is sexual intercourse itself, and the report naming who said that is given.

They differed again concerning the word for transgression. Some said it is all acts of disobedience. And others said that it is that by which one disobeys Allah during the consecration of what He has forbidden therein, such as the killing of game, the removal of hair and the cutting of nails.

phrases.translation: There is no blame on you for seeking the bounty of your Lord ˹during this journey˺.
phrases.explanation:
The permission is explained first. There is no blame on you that you seek a bounty from your Lord. And the word for blame means constraint and burden, so nothing weighs against you and restricts you.

The phrase about seeking is then explained. It means that you endeavor to obtain a bounty from your Lord, and the word carries the sense of seeking and pursuing, for one says of a thing that he sought and pursued it.

It has been said that the meaning of seeking the bounty of Allah is seeking Allah's provision by means of trade, and that this verse was revealed concerning a people who held that one was not permitted to trade when one had entered the state of ritual consecration, thereby seeking piety. Then He let them know that there was no piety in that, and that trading was permitted.

phrases.translation: When you return from ’Arafât,
phrases.explanation:
The reason for the name is then discussed. The scholars differed concerning why Arafat is called Arafat. Some of them said that it was so named because Abraham, the bosom friend of Allah, recognized it when he saw it, by the description he had with him, and said, I have recognized it, after which it was called Arafat for that reason. And that saying indicates that it is a name for the place and that it was so named after itself and what lies around it, as one says a worn-out garment and a flat land.

The correct view is then given. It is a name for a single place, named with a plural, so if it is declined with nunation it is taken in the sense of the plural that it originally was, and if the nunation is omitted it is taken as the name of a single known place, and then the nunation is omitted just as it is in the names of known towns and villages.

phrases.translation: praise Allah near the sacred place
phrases.explanation:
The remembrance is then explained. When you depart and return from Arafat to the place from which you had begun the journey, then remember Allah, and this means the prayer and the supplication at the sacred standing place.

A point of grammar is then added. The landmarks have already been explained as derived from the saying of a person, I knew it, and the landmark is so named because the prayer at it and the supplication belong to the landmarks of the pilgrimage.

The saying of one of the early authorities is then explained. When he came to al-Muzdalifa he said, all of this are landmarks up to Mecca, and the meaning of that is that they are landmarks among the landmarks of the pilgrimage, at which one performs a portion of the rites.

phrases.translation: and praise Him for having guided you, for surely before this ˹guidance˺ you were astray
phrases.explanation:
The clause is explained first. And remember Him as He has guided you, and the sense is that you remember Allah at the sacred standing place by praising Him and thanking Him for His favours upon you, and let your remembrance of Him be through submission to His command, obedience to Him and gratitude for the grace with which He has favoured you regarding the success toward the practices of Abraham after the state of ascribing partners and the going astray.

The last clause is then addressed. Among the linguists there are those who direct the interpretation of the word in toward the meaning of negation and the interpretation of the particle toward except, and the meaning of that is that you remember Allah as He has remembered you with guidance and thus guided you toward that which was pleasing to Him of the religions, while you were already before that time among those who went astray.

phrases.translation: Then go forth with the rest of the pilgrims. And seek Allah’s forgiveness.
phrases.explanation:
The exegetes differed over the explanation of this. Who is meant by the command to pour forth from where the people pour forth, and who are the people who were commanded to pour forth from there?

One answer is then given. What is meant by then pour forth are the Quraysh and those whom the Quraysh had begotten, who in the time of ignorance were called the Hums, and in Islam they were commanded to pour forth from Arafat, which is the place from which all the remaining people poured forth, because the Quraysh said, we do not leave the sacred precinct.

Another answer is given, that those addressed are all the Muslims together, and that from where the people pour forth means from Jam, and that by the people is meant Abraham.

The correct view is then given. By this verse the Quraysh are meant, and those among the remaining Arabs who had joined themselves to the Hums, on account of the agreement among the exegetes. And the explanation of the verse is then given as a whole, that whoever undertakes the pilgrimage as an obligation has no sexual intercourse nor licentious conduct nor dispute during it, then pours forth and asks Allah for forgiveness.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation:
The exposition of the meaning is then given. It is the interpretation of the words and ask Allah for forgiveness, truly Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.

The sense is then set out at length. When you then pour forth from Arafat, on the way to Mina, then remember Allah at the sacred standing place, and call upon Him and worship Him there, just as He has guided you with His guidance and favoured you with that with which He pleased His friend Abraham, to which He guided him of the prescriptions of His religion, after you had strayed from it.

And the last words are then explained, that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful with those who ask Him for forgiveness.

phrases.translation: When you have fulfilled your sacred rites, praise Allah as you used to praise your forefathers ˹before Islam˺, or even more passionately. There are some who say, “Our Lord! Grant us ˹Your bounties˺ in this world,” but they will have no share in the Hereafter
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. When you have completed your rites, meaning when you have finished your pilgrimage and have slaughtered your sacrificial animals, then remember Allah.

Two explanations are then given. Some of them said that the people in the time of ignorance used to gather after finishing their pilgrimage and boast about the glorious deeds of their fathers, and then Allah commanded them in Islam that their remembrance should consist of praise, gratitude and glorification of their Lord and no one else. Others said that it was said to them, remember Allah as you remember your fathers, because they, when they had completed their rites, remembered no one but their fathers.

The correct statement is then given. Allah commanded His believing servants to remember Him through obedience to Him, in submission to His command and worship of Him, after the completion of their rites, and this remembrance may be the proclamation of the greatness of Allah which He commanded with His saying, and remember Allah during a numbered number of days, and urged perseverance in it, just as the sons persevere in remembering the fathers in their transmitted deeds.

The second half of the verse is then explained. Remember Allah as you remember your fathers, or with even stronger remembrance, and turn yearningly to Him for the good of this world and the hereafter that is with Him, with supplication and humility, and make your deeds pure for the sake of His face, and do not be like the one who has bought the worldly life at the expense of the hereafter, so that there is for them no portion in the reward of Allah.

The meaning of share is then noted, that it means the portion, and it was explained elsewhere with the testimonies from the proofs.

phrases.translation: Yet there are others who say, “Our Lord! Grant us the good of this world and the Hereafter, and protect us from the torment of the Fire.”
phrases.explanation:
The people described are explained first. The correct view concerning that is that Allah has informed about a group of people who believe in Him and in His messenger, among them those who have performed the pilgrimage to His House, that they ask their Lord for the good in this world and the good in the hereafter, and that He protect them from the punishment of the fire. And the good from Allah may comprise well-being in the body, livelihood, provision and the like, as well as knowledge and worship.

Two other readings are then recorded. Some of them said that what is meant is that among the people are those who say, our Lord, give us well-being in this world and well-being in the hereafter. And others said that Allah intended by the good, in this world, knowledge and worship, and in the hereafter, the garden.

The closing clause is then explained. And protect us from the punishment of the fire means turn away from us the punishment of the fire.

phrases.translation: It is they who will receive a ˹heavenly˺ reward for the good they have done. Surely Allah is swift in reckoning
phrases.explanation:
The people meant are then explained. By those, He means those who, after the completion of their pilgrimage rites, say, our Lord, give us in this world good and in the hereafter good and protect us from the punishment of the fire. Thus He has made known that they have a portion and a share in their pilgrimage and an abundant reward for the work they have earned.

The closing words are then explained. And Allah is swift in the reckoning means that He encompasses the work of both groups, that of the one whose request is give us in this world, and that of the other whose request is give us in this world good and in the hereafter good, and then He recompenses each for it.

phrases.translation: And remember Allah during ˹these˺ appointed days.
phrases.explanation:
The days are explained first. Remember Allah by professing His oneness and by proclaiming His greatness during a counted number of days, and these are the days of casting the pebbles, for He commanded His servants on those days to perform the proclamation of the greatness after the prayers and at the casting, with each pebble of the pebbles with which one pelts one of the pillars.

A question is then raised. When the prophet said concerning the days of Mina that they are days of eating and drinking and the remembrance of Allah, he did not inform his community that these are the appointed days which Allah mentions in His Book, so what then do you deny in the possibility that the prophet intended by the remembrance of Allah the well-known days.

phrases.translation: Whoever departs swiftly on the second day is not sinful, neither are those who stay behind ˹till the third—seeking additional reward˺, so long as they are mindful ˹of their Lord˺.
phrases.explanation:
The sentence is explained first. Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him, for whoever fears.

The exegetes differed concerning its meaning. Some of them said that whoever hastens in two of the days of tashriq and departs on the second day has no sin upon him in his departing, and whoever delays his departure until the third day has no sin upon him in his delaying. Others said that the meaning is that there is no objection upon him in his hastening his departure, if he is careful not to kill game until the third day has passed.

The meaning preferred is then given at length. Similar narrations indicate that whoever performs the pilgrimage and accomplishes it according to its limits as Allah has commanded him comes out of his sins, and the objection is removed from the agent only with respect to something whose omission rested upon him, so that it is permitted to him to do it, or with respect to something whose doing rested upon him. And since the pilgrim can be in no other case than that his duty is departure on the second day, or that his duty is remaining until the third day, the second clause has no meaning.

The narration of the messenger explicitly declares that he, by accomplishing his pilgrimage as he was commanded, comes out of his sins as on the day his mother bore him, and therein lies a clear indication of the incorrectness of the view that there is no sin upon him until the following year.

The answer to that is then given. What governs it is the meaning of the sentence, for in it lies the meaning that the sins have been taken away and the offenses remitted, so the mention of the remission of sins was omitted because the indication of the sentence sufficed.

A grammatical point is then added. Some of the grammarians of Basra have claimed that it is as though He thereby informed of something, and so said, for whoever fears, that is to say, this is for whoever fears. And another possibility is then given, namely that neither of the two groups is to brand the other as sinful.

phrases.translation: And be mindful of Allah, and know that to Him you will ˹all˺ be gathered
phrases.explanation:
The exposition of the meaning is then given. It is the interpretation of the words And fear Allah and know that to Him you will be gathered.

The sense is then set out at length. And fear Allah, O believers, in that which He has imposed upon you of obligations, fear Him against neglecting and failing in them, and in that which He has forbidden you in your pilgrimage and your rites, and in that with which He has charged you in your consecration, that you should fall short in accomplishing and carrying it out. And know that to Him you will be gathered, for He will requite you according to your deeds, and repay every soul among you in full for what it has performed, while no injustice will be done to you.

phrases.translation: There are some ˹hypocrites˺ who impress you with their views regarding worldly affairs and openly call upon Allah to witness what is in their hearts, yet they are your worst adversaries
phrases.explanation:
The description is explained first. This is a description by Allah of the hypocrites, that among the people is one whose outward speech and open declaration please you, and who calls Allah to witness over what is in his heart, while he is the most contentious of disputants, a disputant by means of falsehood.

The occasion of the revelation is then discussed. Some of them said that it was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, who came to the messenger and claimed that he desired Islam and swore that he had come only for that, and then went off and wrought harm among the possessions of the Muslims. Others said that it was revealed about a group of the people of hypocrisy who spoke about the raiding party of the messenger that was struck down at al-Raji. And others said that by it were meant all the hypocrites, and by the phrase about the contradiction between their inner and their outer.

The recitation is then discussed. There are two modes of reading the clause about calling Allah to witness. Most of the readers read it as he calls Allah to witness over what is in his heart, with the meaning that the hypocrite whose speech pleases the messenger calls Allah to witness over what is in his heart, that his speech accords with his conviction and that he believes in Allah and His messenger, while he is lying.

A report from Allah is then given, that the hypocrite about whom He informed His prophet that he pleases him when his word and his speech please him calls Allah to witness that he speaks the truth in that saying of his, on account of the severity of his dispute and his contentiousness by means of falsehood.

The last phrase is then explained. The one who is the most severe in dispute among men is the one who is obstinate in argument. The exegetes differed concerning its interpretation. Some said that it means he is a disputant. And others said that the meaning of that is that he is not upright in dispute, but crooked therein. And others said that the meaning of that is that he is a liar in his speech.

phrases.translation: And when they leave ˹you˺, they strive throughout the land to spread mischief in it and destroy crops and cattle. Allah does not like mischief
phrases.explanation:
The correct view is then given. Allah described this hypocrite as one who, when he turns away and turns his back on the messenger, commits corruption upon the earth of Allah, and under the phrase of spreading corruption all forms of disobedience may fall, so Allah did not restrict His description to some meanings of it to the exclusion of others. Except that what most resembles the apparent meaning is that he cut off the road and spread fear upon the path.

The exegetes differed concerning it, and some of them said that the meaning of it is the severing of kinship ties and the shedding of the blood of the Muslims.

The manner of the destroying is then discussed. The exegetes differed concerning it, and his destroying of the seed sown is his burning of it. And it may be that it was through the withholding of the rain on account of his disobedience, and it may be that it was through his killing of those who tend it until it spoiled, and likewise the destroying of the offspring was through his killing of the mothers or fathers. What is more in agreement with the apparent meaning is the burning of the crops of a group of Muslims.

A recitation is then noted, that some reciters have read the words with the nominative, and the meaning given is that the crops and the offspring perish.

The closing clause is then explained, that Allah does not love the deeds of disobedience, and the cutting off of the path and the spreading of fear upon the road. And a point of grammar is added, that the word for corruption is a verbal noun from the saying of a person that the thing became corrupt.

phrases.translation: When it is said to them, “Fear Allah,” pride carries them off to sin. Hell will be their proper place. What an evil place to rest
phrases.explanation:
The verse is explained first. He means that when it is said to this hypocrite, whose characteristic He described to His prophet, fear Allah and be wary of Him, then arrogance seizes him in sin.

The people of interpretation differed concerning whom this verse means. Some of them said that by it was meant every transgressor and hypocrite, and the report naming who said that is given. And others said that by it was meant al-Akhnas ibn Shariq.

The closing words are then explained. And what a wretched resting place means what a wretched sleeping place and bed is hell, which he has prepared for himself through his hypocrisy.

phrases.translation: And there are those who would dedicate their lives to Allah’s pleasure.
phrases.explanation:
The word for selling was explained earlier, meaning that which is bought. And by seeking the good pleasure of Allah, the sense is that this seller, when he buys, seeks the good pleasure of Allah.

The interpreters differed concerning whom this verse is about. Some said it was revealed concerning the emigrants and the helpers, and that those intended are the ones who fight in the path of Allah. Others said it concerned certain men among the emigrants.

The correct view is then given. Allah described one who sells himself seeking His good pleasure, so everyone who sells himself in obedience to Him until he is killed therein, or who seeks death even though he is not killed, is intended, whether that came from him in the struggle against the enemy or in commanding the right.

phrases.translation: And Allah is Ever Gracious to ˹His˺ servants
phrases.explanation:
The explanation of the saying is then given. And Allah is gentle toward the servants, and the word for gentleness was demonstrated earlier, meaning the tenderness of mercy.

The meaning of it is then set out at length. Allah is possessor of a wide mercy toward His servant who sells himself for Him in the struggle against whoever turns against Him in His cause among the people of shirk and moral corruption, and toward the rest of His believing servants, in their near future and in their future place of return, so He fulfills for them the reward for what they have been tried with in obedience to Him in this world, and He causes them to dwell in His gardens for what they performed therein of that which is pleasing to Him.

phrases.translation: O believers! Enter into Islam wholeheartedly and do not follow Satan’s footsteps. Surely he is your sworn enemy
phrases.explanation:
The meaning of peace is discussed first. The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of the word for peace in this place. Some of them said that it means Islam, and others said that it means enter into obedience.

The recitation is then discussed. The reciters differed, most of the reciters of the people of Hijaz reciting it with the vowel that makes it peace, and most of the reciters of the people of Kufa with the other.

The question is then raised which of these two groups was called to enter all together into Islam. Some of them said that those called to it were the believers in Muhammad and in what he brought. Others said that those called to it were the believers in the prophets before him who denied Muhammad. And others said that the group called to peace, to whom it was said enter into it by this verse, are the people of the book, and they were commanded to enter into Islam.

The correct view is then given. Allah commanded those who believed to enter into acting according to all the legal ordinances of Islam, and under those who believed may fall those who believed in Muhammad and in what he brought and those who believed in the prophets and messengers before him, and He called both groups to act according to the legal ordinances and the prescribed punishments of Islam and to observe His obligations, and He forbade them to neglect anything of that, so the verse is general for everyone whom the name of faith encompasses.

The phrase all together is then explained, meaning collectively, all together.

The last clause is then explained. Act, O believers, according to all the legal ordinances of Islam, and enter into believing in it with word and deed, and leave the ways of Satan and his traces, lest you follow them, for verily he is for you an enemy whose enmity toward you is clear. And the way of Satan which He forbade them to follow is whatever contradicts the ruling and the legal ordinances of Islam, and to that belongs the keeping of the Sabbath and all other customs of the adherents of the religions that contradict the religion of Islam.

phrases.translation: If you falter after receiving the clear proofs, then know that Allah is indeed Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: By this He means, but if you miss the truth, and thereby stray from it, and oppose Islam and its legal ordinances, after My proofs and the clear signs of My guidance have come to you, and the correctness of the matter of Islam has become clear to you through the indications that have cut off your excuse, then know that Allah is the Possessor of might, who is prevented by no obstacle from taking vengeance upon you and held back by no deterrer from punishing you for your opposition to His command, and All-Wise in what He does with you of punishment for your disobedience, after He has established the proof against you, and in all His other affairs.

phrases.translation: Are they waiting for Allah ˹Himself˺ to come to them in the shade of clouds, along with the angels?
phrases.explanation:
The question is explained first. Are those who declared the prophet and what he brought to be lies waiting for anything other than that Allah should come to them in shadows of clouds with the angels?

The recitation is then discussed. Some read the angels with the nominative, so that it is joined to the name of Allah, and others read it with the genitive, so that it is joined to the shadows.

The phrase are they waiting is then explained. It means they are not waiting, and that was expounded earlier.

Four views are then given. Some said that for that there is no further manner than that with which He has described Himself, the coming, the approaching and the descending, and it is not permitted for anyone to burden himself with a statement about that except on the basis of a report from Allah or from a sent messenger. Others said that His coming is like what is known of the coming of one who comes from one place to another. Others said that what is meant is that His reward, His reckoning and His punishment should come to them.

phrases.translation: ˹If He did˺, then the matter would be settled ˹at once˺. And to Allah ˹all˺ matters will be returned ˹for judgment˺
phrases.explanation:
A point of grammar is then given. Whoever read it as in shadows understood it as the plural of shadow, and that plural takes two forms, just as the plural of friendship takes two.

The exegetes differed over the words shadows of clouds, whether this is connected to the act of Allah or to the act of the angels. Some of them said that it is connected to the act of Allah, so the sense is that Allah should come to them in shadows of clouds and that the angels should come to them. And the statement that differs in the manner of the angels requires the genitive.

The more correct interpretation is then given, that the words shadows of clouds are connected to the act of the Lord, so the sense is that Allah should come to them in shadows of clouds and that the angels should come to them. And the sense of the whole verse is given, that those who refrain from the submission and follow the footsteps of Satan are waiting for anything other than that Allah should come to them in shadows of clouds.

The closing clause is then explained at length. And to Allah all matters are returned means that to Allah returns the decision between His creatures on the day of resurrection, and the judgment between them in their affairs that occurred in the worldly life, of the wronging of one by another and the well-doing of the well-doer, so He separates between those who mutually wrong one another, requites the people of well-doing with bounty and the people of evil-doing with what He sees fit.

phrases.translation: Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We have given them.
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs He has given them.

The sense of it is then set out. Ask, O Muhammad, those who expect nothing other than that He should come to them in shadows of clouds, and ask them how many a sign and proof He brought them before you with regard to what He imposed upon them of obligations. Yet they denied His proofs, gave the lie to His messengers, altered His favours toward them, and changed His covenant.

A note is then added on the word. The sign has already been explained earlier in the book, and here it means that which Allah has mentioned in the Quran and that which He has not mentioned, and they are the Jews.

phrases.translation: And whoever trades Allah’s favour—after receiving it—˹for disbelief˺ should know that Allah is indeed severe in punishment
phrases.explanation:
Allah informed His prophet of these signs only, and commanded him to be patient toward whoever gave him the lie and arrogantly exalted himself against his Lord, and told him that the like of that was done by the predecessors of the communities.

The second clause is then explained. And whoever changes the favor of Allah means whoever alters that which he promised Allah concerning His favor that is Islam, namely acting upon it and entering into it, and thus denies it, so He will punish him, for Allah is severe in punishment.

The explanation of the verse is then given. O you who have believed in the Torah and have thus confirmed it, enter all of you into Islam and abandon disbelief and that to which Satan has called you of his error.

phrases.translation: The life of this world has been made appealing to the disbelievers, and they mock the believers. Those who are mindful ˹of Allah˺ will rank above them on the Day of Judgment.
phrases.explanation: The meaning is then given. For those who disbelieve, the love of the hastening worldly life with its pleasures has been made fair-seeming, so they strive therein to outdo one another in possessions and to boast over one another, and they seek positions of leadership and pomp, and they exalt themselves haughtily above following you, and they mock whoever follows you among the people of faith, because these people have abandoned the mutual outdoing in possessions and the boasting over the world by pursuing what is with Me. And those who have worked for Me and rejected the pleasures of the world are above those who disbelieve on the day of resurrection, in that the God-fearing are admitted into the garden and those who disbelieve into the fire.

phrases.translation: And Allah provides for whoever He wills without limit
phrases.explanation:
The clause is then explained. And Allah gives to those who are God-fearing on the day of resurrection of His favours, His honours and His abundant gifts, without reckoning them for the honour with which He has favoured them.

A question is then raised about what praise there is in the saying that He provides for whom He wills without reckoning. It is answered that the praise is the announcement that He does not fear the exhaustion of His storehouses, since reckoning occurs on the part of the giver only so that he may know the magnitude of the gift. But our Lord does not fear the exhaustion of His storehouses, nor any diminution of His possession through that which He gives, so that He would have need to reckon what He gives.

phrases.translation: Humanity had once been one community ˹of believers before they lost faith˺. Then Allah raised prophets as deliverers of good news and as warners, and revealed to them the Scriptures in truth to judge among people regarding their disputes.
phrases.explanation:
The scholars differed concerning the meaning of the community and of the people whom Allah described as having been one community. Some of them said that they are those who lived between Adam and Noah, and they were ten generations, all of them following a law of truth and then differing. Others said that Adam was upon the truth as a leader for his progeny, whereupon Allah sent the prophets among his descendants, and they directed the meaning of the community toward obedience to Allah, and the calling of the prophet of each generation was to those who had come to believe in the predecessor. And it is as though the one who proclaimed this view deemed it permissible to designate the individual by the name of the group, on account of the gathering of the good qualities in the one whom he called the community. Others said that the meaning is that mankind was one community upon one religion on the day He brought forth the progeny of Adam from his loins and showed them to Adam.

The correct interpretation is then given. Allah informed His servants that mankind was one community upon one religion and one creed, and He sent messengers who gave good tidings to whoever obeyed Allah of an abundant reward and a noble return, and who warned whoever disobeyed, and He sent down to them the Book in truth to judge between them concerning their disputes.

A point of wording is then added. The root meaning of the word for community is the group that unites upon one religion, and the report about the community stands in place of the report about the religion, because it points to it. And the religion they followed was the religion of truth, and the proof of the Quran is clear that those of whom Allah informed that they were one community were one community only upon faith and the religion of truth.

phrases.translation: And no one disputed the Scriptures except the very people who received them after clear proofs had come to them—out of jealousy.
phrases.explanation:
The clause is then explained. And none differed over it means none differed concerning the Book which He sent down, namely the Torah, except those who were given it, by which He means the Jews of the Children of Israel, and the reason for their difference was out of mutual transgression, which is derived from the saying of a person that he transgressed against another when he tyrannized over him.

A point of grammar is then added, and the question is raised about the particle in after the clear proofs had come to them. Two views are then given. On the first, the particle belongs to those who were given the Book and what follows it is a subordinate clause. On the second, the particle belongs to the coming of the proofs, so the sense is that the people differed after the proofs came and out of transgression.

The second view is then preferred, for the people differed only after the proof had been established against them and the clear proofs of Allah had come.

phrases.translation: Then Allah, by His grace, has guided the believers to the truth regarding those disputes. And Allah guides whoever He wills to the Straight Path
phrases.explanation:
Then Allah guided means that Allah granted right discernment to those who believed, and they are the people of faith in Allah and in His messenger, to the truth concerning which these factions of the Children of Israel differed.

And the phrase by His permission is explained as through His knowledge of that to which He guided them. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path means that He grants right direction to whom He wills of His creation and directs him to the straight way upon the truth in which there is no crookedness. And in this verse lies the clear exposition of what the people of truth said, that every favor to the servants is from Allah.

A question is then raised whether He guided them to the truth or to the disagreement, and it is answered that the meaning is only that He guided those who believed to the truth about which those given the Book differed.

phrases.translation: Do you think you will be admitted into Paradise without being tested like those before you? They were afflicted with suffering and adversity and were so ˹violently˺ shaken that ˹even˺ the Messenger and the believers with him cried out, “When will Allah’s help come?” Indeed, Allah’s help is ˹always˺ near
phrases.explanation:
The question is explained first. Or did you suppose is as though He poses a question at the outset without an interrogative particle preceding it.

The meaning of the statement is then given. Or did you suppose, O you who believe in Allah and His messengers, that you would enter Paradise without there having befallen you the like of what befell those who were before you, namely the followers of the messengers who were tested before you with the like of what you are tested with, so that you might be like them.

The occasion is then given. This verse was revealed on the Day of the Trench, when the believers underwent what they underwent of severe hardship through the fear of the Confederates, and the report naming those who said that is given.

The phrase is then explained, meaning the like of those who passed away and thus went by before you, and the word for likeness was shown elsewhere to mean likeness and semblance. And the shaking is explained as merely the fear of the enemy and not the earthquake, and for that reason it was of long duration.

phrases.translation: They ask you ˹O Prophet in˺ what ˹way˺ they should donate.
phrases.explanation:
Your companions ask you, O Muhammad, which matter of their possessions they should spend and give as alms, and to whom they should spend that which they expend, so say to them, whatever you spend of your possessions and give as alms, spend it and assign it to your fathers and mothers and your near relatives, and to the orphans among you, and the needy, and the traveler on the way. For whatever good you do, indeed Allah knows of it.

A point of grammar is then added. The first reading takes the question word as carrying the meaning of which matter, so it is in the accusative on account of the word they spend.

A further view is then recorded, that it is possible that on the day this verse was revealed there was as yet no alms-tax, and that it was only the maintenance that a man spends on his family and the alms that he gives, and that it was thereafter abrogated.

phrases.translation: Say, “Whatever donations you give are for parents, relatives, orphans, the poor, and ˹needy˺ travellers. Whatever good you do is certainly well known to Allah.”
phrases.explanation:
The meaning of neediness and of the traveler on the way was expounded earlier, and the same sense is meant here, so that the repetition is not needed.

A point of grammar is then added about the phrase with the accusative, by omission of the preposition or of the adverbial of place, that is to say, come to know your female companion at the dwelling places of Mina, so he says, I do not know anyone who knows her among those who visit Mina, so that I might ask him about her.

The point of the example is then explained, that the word for everyone is put in the nominative and not the accusative, because the meaning of his saying is a negation of the recognition.

phrases.translation: Fighting has been made obligatory upon you ˹believers˺, though you dislike it. Perhaps you dislike something which is good for you and like something which is bad for you.
phrases.explanation:
Fighting has been imposed upon you, that is to say the fighting against the polytheists, and it is hateful to you.

The people of knowledge differed concerning who were meant by the prescribing of fighting. Some of them said that by this were meant exclusively the companions of the messenger, and no one else. And this is a saying that has no sense, for the abrogation of rulings comes from the side of Allah, not from the side of the servants.

Another view is then given, that it rests upon every individual person until those who carry it out are sufficient by their action, whereupon the obligation falls away from the remaining Muslims, like the prayer over the deceased and the burial of the dead, and this is the position of the majority of the scholars. And others said that it is a binding obligation upon the Muslims until the Hour.

That is then said to be the correct view, because of the agreement of the proof upon it and because of the saying that Allah has made those who strive with their wealth and their lives excel over those who remain behind by a rank, and to both Allah has promised the best, for the excellence belongs to those who strive and both they and those who remain behind have the best in prospect.

A point of grammar is then added, that the word for hateful and the word for disgust are two variants with the same meaning, and one of them is a noun and the other a verbal noun. And the next clause is then explained, that you should not dislike the fighting since you may dislike it while it is good for you, and should not love the abandonment of the struggle since you may love it while it is bad for you.

phrases.translation: Allah knows and you do not know
phrases.explanation: By this He means that Allah knows what is good for you in distinction from what is bad for you, so do not dislike what He has prescribed for you of the struggle against your enemy and the fighting against whom He has commanded you to fight, for He knows that your fighting against them is good for you in your present life and in your future life, and that the abandonment of it is bad for you, while you do not know thereof what He knows. By this He urges them to the struggle against His enemies and arouses in them the longing for the fighting against whoever disbelieves in Him.

phrases.translation: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about fighting in the sacred months. Say, “Fighting during these months is a great sin.
phrases.explanation:
The sense of the question is explained. That is to say, about fighting therein. Say, fighting therein is a great matter, up to the saying that the affliction is greater than killing, that is to say, if you have killed in the sacred month, then they have hindered you from the path of Allah, along with disbelief in Him, and from the sacred mosque, and your expelling out of it, while you are its inhabitants and custodians, is greater with Allah than the killing of those of them whom you have killed. And the affliction is greater than killing means they used to turn the Muslim away from his religion until they led him back to disbelief after his faith.

Two possibilities are then recorded from the grammarians of Kufa for the case of the word hindering, and both are then set aside as error, since the first of them would make fighting in the sacred months into disbelief in Allah, which contradicts what all the people of Islam adhere to, and the second would make the expelling of the people of the sacred mosque more enormous with Allah than disbelief in Him, which falls into the same error. And one of the linguists of Basra used to make the first statement.

A further view is then recorded, that it is abrogated by the words fight the polytheists collectively and then kill the polytheists.

The occasion is then explained.
