If anyone supposes that the prohibition came about after the regarding of the sacred month as violable by the prophet, then he has supposed out of ignorance, for this verse concerns the matter of Abdullah ibn Jahsh and his companions and the slain man whom they killed, and it was revealed at the end of Jumada al-Akhira of the second year after the arrival of the messenger at Medina, while the battle of Hunayn took place in Shawwal of the eighth year.

phrases.translation: But hindering ˹others˺ from the Path of Allah, rejecting Him, and expelling the worshippers from the Sacred Mosque is ˹a˺ greater ˹sin˺ in the sight of Allah. For persecution is far worse than killing. And they will not stop fighting you until they turn you away from your faith—if they can.
phrases.explanation:
Say, O Muhammad, fighting therein, that is to say in the sacred month, is a great matter, that is to say it is an enormous thing with Allah to regard that month as violable.

The reason is then given. He said only say fighting therein is a great matter, because the Arabs would not clash their spearheads against one another therein, for a man would meet the killer of his father and do nothing.

The words are then explained. The meaning of hindering from something is restraining from it and warding it off. And disbelief in Him means disbelief in Allah, and the particle in Him refers back to the name Allah in the path of Allah. And a point of grammar is then added, that the hindering is set in the nominative by the words is greater with Allah.

phrases.translation: And whoever among you renounces their own faith and dies a disbeliever, their deeds will become void in this life and in the Hereafter. It is they who will be the residents of the Fire. They will be there forever.”
phrases.explanation: By His word and whoever of you turns back from his religion, He means whoever of you returns from his religion, and from this is the expression that so-and-so reclaimed his right from so-and-so, when he reclaimed it from him. And His word and dies while he is a disbeliever means whoever turns back from his religion, the religion of Islam, and dies before he repents of his disbelief, those are they whose works have become fruitless, and by fruitless He means become void and fallen away, so their reward falls away and the recompense for them in this world and the hereafter. And the last clause is explained, that those who turned back from their religion and died in their disbelief are the people of the fire, who remain therein forever.

phrases.translation: Surely those who have believed, emigrated, and struggled in the Way of Allah—they can hope for Allah’s mercy. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation:
The meaning is explained first. Those who have held to be true Allah, His messenger, and what he brought, and by those who have emigrated are meant those who abandoned dwelling with the polytheists and turned away from them and their land.

A point of grammar is then added about the root of striving, which is the reciprocal form, so that when two parties each endure from his companion, one is said to strive against the other.

The whole clause is then explained: those who have emigrated and striven in the way of Allah are those who turned away from the rule of the people of shirk and out of fear of trial.

And those hope for the mercy of Allah means they yearn that Allah be merciful to them and admit them into paradise.

phrases.translation: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about intoxicants and gambling. Say, “There is great evil in both, as well as some benefit for people—but the evil outweighs the benefit.” They ˹also˺ ask you ˹O Prophet˺ what they should donate.
phrases.explanation:
The question is explained first. Your companions ask you about wine and the drinking of it, and wine is every drink that befogs the intellect, covers it and veils it, and whatever befogs the intellect through sickness or intoxication is wine.

The interpretation preferred is then given. The great sin in the case of wine is the loss of the wine-drinker's intellect when he has become intoxicated, until the knowledge of his Lord escapes him. And as for gambling, it is the occupation with it that distracts from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer.

The recitation is then discussed. The majority of the people of Medina and some of the Kufans and Basrans read it with the letter that makes it a great sin, and others among the people of the two garrison towns read it as in both there are many sins.

The next clause is then explained. The sin of the drinking of this and this gambling is greater and more enormous in harm to them than the benefit they obtain through both, and this verse was revealed concerning wine before its prohibition was expressly declared.

phrases.translation: Say, “Whatever you can spare.” This is how Allah makes His revelations clear to you ˹believers˺, so perhaps you may reflect
phrases.explanation:
The reciters differed concerning the reading of the surplus. Most of the reciters of Hijaz and the majority of the Kufans read it in the accusative, and some Basrans read it in the nominative. He who read it in the accusative placed it there on account of the word they spend, and he who read it in the nominative so the sense is that what is it that they spend, and with whichever of the two it is read it is correct.

The closing clause is then explained, that thus Allah makes clear to you the signs, that is, just as He has made clear to you His signs.

phrases.translation: upon this world and the Hereafter. And they ask you ˹O Prophet˺ concerning orphans. Say, “Improving their condition is best. And if you partner with them, they are bonded with you ˹in faith˺. And Allah knows who intends harm and who intends good.
phrases.explanation:
The answer is then given on account of the difference in the meaning of the two. The orphans of the believers are the brothers of the believers, whether the believers mix with them with their property or not, and the brothers is in the nominative on account of the omitted meaning.

A point of grammar is then given about the phrase on foot or riding, which is in the accusative because both are adverbial states attached to the verb which are not permanent and to which he does not fit.

The whole sense is then given at length. Your Lord has permitted you mixing with the orphans in the manner He has permitted it, so fear Allah within yourselves, lest you mix with them while intending to consume their property unjustly.

phrases.translation: Had Allah willed, He could have made it difficult for you. Surely Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.”
phrases.explanation:
One of the exegetes is then cited. He means by it the grazing of the cattle of the guardian of the orphan together with the cattle of the orphan, and the eating of his seasoning.

These sayings are then compared, and they are close to one another in their meanings, for whoever is forbidden something is straitened in that respect, and whoever is straitened is oppressed therein, and all of that returns to the meaning of heaviness and difficulty.

The sense is then given at length. Allah is Almighty in His sovereignty, no hinderer hinders Him in what He would bring down upon you of punishment, had He burdened you heavily with what the accomplishment of it wearies you. But He has, out of the abundance of His mercy, refrained from imposing that upon you. And He is All-Wise therein and in all His other rulings.

phrases.translation: Do not marry polytheistic women until they believe;
phrases.explanation:
The people of interpretation differed concerning this verse. Was it released with the intent of comprising every polytheistic woman, or was only a part of the polytheistic women meant by its ruling? And after its ruling became obligatory, is anything of it abrogated or not?

Some of them said that it was released with the intent of prohibiting the marriage of every polytheistic woman by every Muslim, of whatever kind of shirk she might be, whether an idolatress, a Jewess, a Christian, a Zoroastrian or of another kind, and that the prohibition of marrying the people of the book was thereafter abrogated by the verse permitting the chaste women among the believers and the chaste women among those who were given the book before you.

phrases.translation: for a believing slave-woman is better than a free polytheist, even though she may look pleasant to you.
phrases.explanation:
The Exalted means by the words and a believing slave-woman truly, believing in Allah, in His messenger and in that which he brought from Allah, that she is better with Allah and more excellent than a polytheistic unbelieving free woman, even if her lineage is noble and her origin honorable.

It has already been mentioned that this verse was released concerning a man who married a slave-woman and was therefore rebuked, while a polytheistic free woman was being offered to him.

And the clause is then explained, that even if the polytheistic woman who does not belong to the people of the book pleases you in beauty, noble descent and wealth, then do not marry her.

phrases.translation: And do not marry your women to polytheistic men until they believe, for a believing slave-man is better than a free polytheist, even though he may look pleasant to you.
phrases.explanation:
The clause is explained first. And do not give the polytheistic men in marriage until they believe means that Allah forbade the believing women to marry a polytheist, whoever the polytheist may be and of whatever kind of shirk, so do not give them in marriage to them, for that is forbidden to you, and that you give them in marriage to a believing slave who holds true Allah, His messenger and that which he brought is better for you than that you give them in marriage to a free polytheist, even if his lineage is noble and his origin honorable.

A further point is then added, that this statement of Allah is an indication that the guardians of the woman have more right to give her in marriage than the woman herself.

phrases.translation: They invite ˹you˺ to the Fire while Allah invites ˹you˺ to Paradise and forgiveness by His grace.
phrases.explanation:
The verse is explained first. They are the ones who call to the Fire, that is to say, they call you to the doing of that which leads you into the Fire, namely unbelief in Allah and His messenger. So do not accept from them what they say, and do not marry them nor give in marriage to them, for they spare no effort to harm you.

And He calls you to the garden, that is to say, He calls you to the doing of that which leads you into the garden, and to that which effaces your missteps, so that He forgives them and covers them for you.

phrases.translation: He makes His revelations clear to the people so perhaps they will be mindful
phrases.explanation:
Other views are then recorded. Some said that the ruling of the verse is directed at the polytheistic women of the Arabs, that nothing of it is abrogated and nothing is excepted. Others said that it comprises every polytheistic woman of whatever kind of shirk.

The view preferred is then given. It is the saying of one of the exegetes, that Allah meant those among the polytheistic women who did not belong to the people of the book, and that the verse is general in its outward form and specific in its inward meaning, and that nothing of it is abrogated, and that the women of the people of the book do not fall under it. So the meaning of the words is that you do not marry any polytheistic women other than the people of the book until they believe.

And the phrase with His permission is explained as meaning that He calls you to that by making known to you His way along which one attains the garden and forgiveness.

phrases.translation: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about menstruation.
phrases.explanation:
The question is explained first. Your companions ask you about menstruation. And it has been said that it is called that because, for a verb whose past tense has a vowel on the second radical and a vowel in the imperfect, the Arabs construct the verbal noun on one pattern and the noun on another, such as the place of striking and the place of descending, and it is heard in words with a yāʾ, an alif and a yāʾ.

Another view is then given, that the meaning is that you approach them by the manner by which Allah has commanded you to approach them, and that manner is purity and not menstruation, so approach them at the beginning of their purity.

phrases.translation: Say, “Beware of its harm!
phrases.explanation:
The Exalted means by it, say to whoever of your companions asks you about menstruation, it is a harm. And the word for harm is that by which one is hindered through something objectionable in it, and it is called a harm in this place on account of its stench, its foulness and its impurity, and it encompasses several meanings among the kinds of harm, more than one.

The exegetes differed in explaining it, though the meanings of part of what they said are close to one another. Some of them said that it means it is filth, and the report naming who said that is given. And others said, say, it is blood, and the report naming who said that is given.

phrases.translation: So keep away, and do not have intercourse with your wives during their monthly cycles until they are purified.
phrases.explanation:
The argument of the proponent of this view is the establishment of the proof by the mass-transmitted reports from the messenger that he would touch his wives while they were menstruating, and if it were obligatory to abstain from them entirely then the messenger would not have done that. And since this is established as authentic, it is known that what Allah intended by His word so keep away from women during menstruation is abstention from one part of her body and not from another part, and that it must be the sexual intercourse over the prohibition of which there is agreement.

Others said that what Allah commanded to abstain from is what lies between the navel and the knee, while what is above and below that of her is permitted.

The most correct of the views is then given, that a man is permitted of his menstruating wife what is above that which is covered by the waist-wrapper, and what is below it.

A recitation is then noted, that those who read it with the light letter and the vowel directed its meaning to and do not approach the women in the state of their menstruation, until the blood ceases from them and they become pure.

The most correct view is then given at length, that the meaning is to approach them at the beginning of their purity, since every command to a thing is a prohibition of its opposite, and if the meaning were to approach them by the exit of the blood from where the command to abstain was given, then the words and do not approach them until they are pure would have to mean that and do not approach them by the exit of the blood and nothing else of the places of her body, such that approaching them by their hindquarters during menstruation would be permitted.

phrases.translation: When they purify themselves, then you may approach them in the manner specified by Allah.
phrases.explanation:
The more correct of the two readings is then given. It is the reading of the one who read until they purify themselves thoroughly, with the doubling, in the meaning of until they wash, on account of the agreement of all that it is forbidden for the man to approach his wife after her menstrual blood has ceased until she is pure. And since there is agreement of all that she does not become permitted to her husband upon the ceasing of the blood until she purifies herself, it is clear that the more correct of the two readings is the one that most removes confusion in the understanding of the hearer, and that is what we have chosen, since in the other reading there is something by which one is not safe from confusion, such that he supposes that it is permitted for the husband of the menstruating woman to copulate with her after her blood has ceased but before her washing.

The most correct of the two interpretations is then given, that the meaning of and when they have purified themselves is when they wash, on account of the agreement of all that she does not become pure by the washing with water with the purity by which prayer becomes permitted to her.

And in the agreement of all the community that prayer is permitted to her only after the washing lies the clearest indication of the correctness of what we have said, namely that copulating with her is forbidden except after the washing.

The reading of those who said the access of the matter and its manner is something other than the matter itself is then discussed at length. If the meaning were as they interpreted it, then the text would need to read and when they have purified themselves, then approach them in that which Allah has commanded you, and the customary expression when that is meant is that one says, so-and-so approached his wife by way of her private part, and one does not say he approached her out of her private part. And the access of the private part must be something other than the private part itself, just as the saying approach the matter by its access only means to seek it by its place of seeking.

And since that is so, and the meaning in their view is that they approach them by their fronts in their private parts, then according to their own saying it would necessarily be forbidden to approach them by their hindquarters, and whoever says that places himself outside the saying of the people of Islam and acts in contradiction to the explicit text of the Book of Allah and to the saying of the messenger, for Allah says your women are a tillage for you, so approach your tillage as you wish, and the messenger gave permission to approach them in their private parts by their rear side.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah loves those who always turn to Him in repentance and those who purify themselves.”
phrases.explanation:
By His word truly, Allah loves the repentant, the sense is those who return from turning away from Allah and from His obedience to Him and to His obedience.

They differed about the meaning of His word and He loves those who purify themselves. Some said they are those who purify themselves with water. Others said that its meaning is that truly, Allah loves the repentant from sins is and He loves those who purify themselves from the hindquarters of women. And others said that they purify themselves from sins.

And the most correct of the views about that is the saying of the one who said, truly, Allah loves the repentant from sins, and He loves those who purify themselves with water for prayer, for that is the most predominant of its outward meaning.

The reason is then given, that Allah mentioned the matter of menstruation and forbade them what they used to do in the time of ignorance, their refraining from living together with the menstruating woman, eating with her and drinking with her.

phrases.translation: Your wives are like farmland for you, so approach them ˹consensually˺ as you please.
phrases.explanation:
Your women are the sowing-place of your children, so approach your sowing-place as you wish and where you wish. By tilth only the sowing-place is meant, for the tilth is the crop, but because women are among the causes of sowing they are called tilth, since the meaning of the word is understood.

The second clause is then explained. Have intercourse with the sowing-place of your children from whatever manner of approach you wish, and the approaching here is a euphemism for sexual intercourse.

Another view is then recorded, that the meaning is that if you wish you withdraw and if you wish you do not withdraw. And others said that it is from where you wish, and through whatever manner you prefer. And others said that it means when you wish.

phrases.translation: And send forth something good for yourselves. Be mindful of Allah, and know that you will meet Him. And give good news to the believers
phrases.explanation:
The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of as you wish. Some of them said that the meaning of the phrase is how. And others said that it is from where you wish, and through whatever manner you prefer. And others said that it means when you wish.

The phrase send forth for yourselves is then explained, and the people differed about it. Some of them said that the meaning is send forth for yourselves the good. Others said that the meaning is the remembrance of Allah at intercourse, before one approaches her.

The closing clause is then explained at length. It is a warning from Allah to His servants against their committing anything of what He has forbidden them, and a striking of fear into them of His punishment at His meeting, and a command to His messenger that he give glad tidings to that one of His servants of triumph on the day of resurrection, of the honor of the hereafter.

phrases.translation: Do not use Allah’s Name in your oaths as an excuse for not doing good, not guarding against evil, or not making peace between people. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation:
The people of exegesis differ over the interpretation. Some said that you should not make Allah a pretext for your oaths, so that when one of you is asked to do something good he says, I have sworn by Allah that I will not. Others said that you should not invoke swearing by Allah as an argument for neglecting the good.

The more correct is then given, that you should not make swearing by Allah an argument for neglecting the good. And the word for excuse means strength and power, so the sense of the verse is that you should not make Allah a strength for your oaths so as not to be righteous.

phrases.translation: Allah will not hold you accountable for unintentional oaths, but for what you intended in your hearts. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Forbearing
phrases.explanation:
The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of the idle words in your oaths. Some said that it means that which your tongues have hastily uttered, without your intending it. Others said that it is the oath the swearer makes while he supposes it is as he swears and it turns out otherwise.

The explanation of the words is then given, that you should not make Allah an object of your oaths in your swearing that you will not be benevolent nor God-fearing, for Allah does not call you to account for that which your tongues have uttered of idle talk, but He will call you to account for that which your hearts have acquired.

phrases.translation: Those who swear not to have intercourse with their wives must wait for four months.
phrases.explanation:
Some of them said that the oath by which the man becomes one who swears with respect to his wife is that he swears concerning her in a state of anger, in the manner of inflicting harm, that he will not have sexual intercourse with her in her private part, but if he swears without the intention of inflicting harm and without anger, then he is not one who swears with respect to her.

The argument of that view is then given. Allah made the term He fixed for it only a way out for the wife from the tyranny of the man and his harming of her, and when the man neither tyrannizes nor harms her by his oath but thereby seeks her contentment and provides for her need, then by that oath he is not one who swears, because no harm has occurred to the wife on the basis of which the term would be made for her a way out from it.

The most correct interpretation is then given. Every oath that prevents the one who takes it from sexual intercourse for longer than the period Allah has set for the one who swears is such an oath, whether he made it in anger or in contentment, and this is the correct one concerning that, because the breaking of the oath makes atonement obligatory in everything in which the breaking is engaged after the swearing, whether the oath was over a disobedience or over an obedience.

phrases.translation: If they change their mind, then Allah is certainly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation:
The Exalted means thereby that if they return to abandoning that which they had sworn, namely the refraining from intercourse with them, and they then have intercourse with them and break their oath, then truly Allah is forgiving for what had proceeded from them of the falsehood in their oaths, namely that they would not come to them and then came afterward, and for what had earlier proceeded from them, namely the oath concerning something about which it was not permissible for them to swear but about which they nonetheless swore, and merciful toward them.

The most correct of the statements is then given, that the return is sexual intercourse, since the man becomes one who swears with respect to his wife only through the oath of refraining from intercourse with her for the period mentioned, and the return that annuls the ruling can only be that which is the opposite of that concerning which he swore, so it is known that the return to it is the doing of that which he swore to refrain from if he is able to do it. Except that when there comes to stand between him and the return an impediment through an excuse, it is not permissible that he in reality be the one who refrains, for the human being is only the one who refrains from that to which he has a way to do it or to refrain from it.

Another view is then given, that the meaning is that Allah is forgiving toward you for what you did wrong by your return to them, namely the breaking of the oath, and merciful toward you by lightening for you the atonement for your oaths which you swore concerning them and then broke.

phrases.translation: But if they settle on divorce, then Allah is indeed All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation:
Some of them said that the meaning is that for those who swear to abstain from their wives there is a waiting period of four months, and then if they return and turn to what Allah has made obligatory of proper conduct during the four months and treat them properly in that respect, then Allah is forgiving and merciful toward them, but if they refrain from returning during the four months until they have elapsed, then their wives are divorced from them by their elapsing, and the elapsing is the proof that the one who swears is resolved upon the divorce of his wife.

Others said that the meaning is that for those who swear to abstain from their wives there is a waiting period of four months upon his part and hers, and then if they return after the elapsing of the four months and turn to proper conduct with them and proceed to intercourse with them, then Allah is indeed forgiving and merciful, and if they are resolved upon divorce then Allah is indeed All-Hearing of their divorcing of them and All-Knowing of what they did to them of good and evil.

The view preferred is then given. It is the statement of Umar ibn al-Khattab, Uthman and Ali and of those who adopt their statement, that the words mean only this, that if they return after the imam has brought them to a stand following the elapsing of the four months and they turn to fulfilling the right Allah has imposed upon them toward their wives, then Allah is forgiving and merciful toward them, and if they are resolved upon divorce then Allah is indeed All-Hearing of their divorce of them and All-Knowing of what they did to them.

phrases.translation: Divorced women must wait three monthly cycles ˹before they can re-marry˺. It is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs, if they ˹truly˺ believe in Allah and the Last Day. And their husbands reserve the right to take them back within that period if they desire reconciliation. Women have rights similar to those of men equitably, although men have a degree ˹of responsibility˺ above them. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.explanation:
What the divorced woman is forbidden to conceal from her husband who repudiated her is then explained. It is the menstruation and the pregnancy, for there is no disagreement among all that the waiting period elapses upon the bearing of the child that Allah has created in her womb, and likewise as it elapses by the blood when she sees it after the third period of purity. And since that right is nullified by what they bear and by the elapsing of the three periods, they are forbidden to conceal either of the two.

A question is then answered. If they believe in Allah and the last day, the meaning is other than what you are going toward, for the concealment by the divorced woman of the menstruation and child during her waiting period, in order to harm him, is not the act of one who believes in Allah and the last day, nor does it belong to his nature, rather that is the act of one who does not believe. So do not, O believing women, adopt their nature.

The exegetes differed about the meaning of the waiting period, and some of them said that it is the purity, and others said that it is the coming of the menstruation, since the Arabs sometimes called the time of the coming of the menstruation a qurʾ, and others called the time of the coming of the purity a qurʾ.

The right of the husbands is then explained. The husbands of the divorced women, upon whom it has been imposed that they keep themselves in waiting for three periods, have more and greater right to take them back during their waiting period, and to return them to their marriage bond, than they may withhold that from them for themselves.

What is most fitting is then given. The women who have been repudiated once or twice have a right toward their husbands that these not take them back in order to harm them during their three periods, unless they intend the improvement of her affair, equal to what is upon them toward them, namely that they not conceal what Allah has created in their wombs in order to harm them.

The exegetes differed about the degree the men have above them. Some said that it is the precedence by which Allah has favoured them over her in inheritance and in struggle, and others said that it is the authority and the obedience. The most correct is then given, that the degree is the forgoing of the man toward his wife of a part of the obligatory upon her, and his overlooking of it for her.

The closing words are then explained. Allah is All-Mighty in His requital to whoever transgresses His command and oversteps His limits, and to whoever of the women conceals from their husbands what Allah has created in their wombs, and to whoever marries during her waiting period, and All-Wise in what He has decreed.

phrases.translation: Divorce may be retracted twice, then the husband must retain ˹his wife˺ with honour or separate ˹from her˺ with grace. It is not lawful for husbands to take back anything of the dowry given to their wives, unless the couple fears not being able to keep within the limits of Allah. So if you fear they will not be able to keep within the limits of Allah, there is no blame if the wife compensates the husband to obtain divorce. These are the limits set by Allah, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah, they are the ˹true˺ wrongdoers
phrases.explanation:
The reciters have differed over its recitation. Some of them recited it with the verb that means they both fear, with the meaning that the man and the woman both fear that they will not maintain the limits of Allah, and in the recitation of one of the companions it is with the verb that means they both suppose. And the other reading is then examined. He has made the verb govern something whose naming is omitted and also the particle, so he has made it govern three things, and the Arabs do not say in their language that he supposed that they both stand.

A question is then raised about which state it is in which it is feared for them both that they will not maintain the limits of Allah, and it is answered that it is the state of her disobedience and her aversion toward him, and it is feared for her that she will abandon obedience to Allah in what has been imposed upon her, and for her husband that he will neglect what is obligatory for her.

The people of interpretation differed about the fear, some of them saying that it is that the woman displays bad character toward her husband, and others saying that it is that she does not keep his oath and does not obey his command.

A further question is then answered. If the disobedience comes from her side and not from his, it ought to be obligatory that it be forbidden for him to accept the ransom from her until there is from him as much aversion toward her as from her toward him. It is answered that the matter is other than that, because in her disobedience toward him there lies an incitement for him to fall short in what is due to her, and that is the cause which produces the fear for them both.

phrases.translation: So if a husband divorces his wife ˹three times˺, then it is not lawful for him to remarry her until after she has married another man and then is divorced. Then it is permissible for them to reunite, as long as they feel they are able to maintain the limits of Allah. These are the limits set by Allah, which He makes clear for people of knowledge
phrases.explanation:
The scholars of interpretation differed concerning that to which this saying points. Some of them said that it points to the fact that, if the man pronounces against his wife the third divorce, then that wife is no longer lawful to him until she marries another husband.

The clause is then explained. If the second husband, who married her after her irrevocable divorce from the first, divorces the woman who had become irrevocably divorced by the last of the three divorces, then there is no sin upon the two of them, that they return to each other by a new marriage.

The condition is then explained. Provided that they think that they will uphold the limits of Allah means if they hopefully expect that they will uphold them.

phrases.translation: When you divorce women and they have ˹almost˺ reached the end of their waiting period, either retain them honourably or let them go honourably.
phrases.explanation:
And when you divorce your women, and they reach their term, that is the time He has fixed for them, namely the completion of the three menstrual periods if she is among those who menstruate, or the completion of the months if she is among those who reckon by the months, then retain them, that is, take them back if you desire to take them back in the divorce in which taking back is possible, either at the first divorce or at the second.

A further point is then added, that in an honorable manner means in the manner that is permitted regarding the taking back, namely the summoning of witnesses for the taking back before the expiry of the waiting period.

phrases.translation: But do not retain them ˹only˺ to harm them ˹or˺ to take advantage ˹of them˺.
phrases.explanation:
The phrase in an honorable manner is then explained. It means the manner that is permitted regarding the taking back, namely the summoning of witnesses for the taking back before the expiry of the waiting period, and not the taking back through sexual intercourse and cohabitation, for that is permitted for the man only after the taking back. And or release them in an honorable manner means or let them complete their waiting period entirely, by fulfilling in full to them their rights in respect of the bridal gift, the maintenance and other rights which they have over you.

And His saying so that you transgress, that is to say: in order that you wrong them by overstepping, in their affair, My bounds.

phrases.translation: Whoever does that surely wrongs his own soul. Do not take Allah’s revelations lightly.
phrases.explanation:
The origin of the word for release is then given. It comes from the driving forth of the herd, and that is what one lets loose of livestock to graze, and one says of the loose livestock sent to the pasture that this is the driving forth of the people, and the saying of Allah about the cattle and their being driven out in the morning bears that sense, so it was said of a woman when her husband lets her loose that he has released her.

And the clause is explained, that whoever takes back his wife after having divorced her in the divorce in which he has the right of taking back, in order to harm her so that he transgresses the bound of Allah in her affair, has indeed wronged himself, and has earned sin for himself and brought upon himself a punishment from Allah.

phrases.translation: Remember Allah’s favours upon you as well as the Book and wisdom He has sent down for your guidance. Be mindful of Allah, and know that Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things
phrases.explanation:
The clause is then explained at length. Do not take the indications of Allah and His distinctions between His permitted and His forbidden as derision and play, for He has clarified to you what is due to you of the right of taking back over your wives, and this is out of mercy toward you.

And the next clause is then explained. Remember the grace of Allah upon you with Islam, and all His other graces, and thank Him for that by obeying Him, and remember likewise what He has sent down of His Book, the Quran, and act on it.

And the closing words are then explained, that He admonishes you with the Book which He has sent down, and fear Allah, and know that Allah is Knowing of all that you do.

phrases.translation: When you have divorced women and they have reached the end of their waiting period,
phrases.explanation:
It has been related that this verse was revealed concerning a man who had a sister married to a cousin of hers, and he divorced her and let her go, and he did not take her back until her waiting period had elapsed, and then he asked for her hand in marriage, but he refused and held her back from him while she desired him.

The correct view is then given, that Allah revealed it as an indication that He forbids the guardians of the women to harm those of whom they are guardians, by preventing them from marrying whom they wish of the husbands they have had and from whom they are separated.

The word for injustice is then explained, its original meaning being constriction, and the saying of one of the companions is cited in that sense, that the people of Iraq have put him in a tight position. And the phrase when they have come to a mutual agreement among themselves in a proper manner is explained as when the husbands and the women reach mutual agreement over what is lawful.

And a long argument is then given, that in this verse lies the clear proof of the soundness of the view of whoever says that there is no valid marriage except with a guardian from the male paternal blood-relatives, because Allah has prevented the guardian from preventing the woman if she wishes to marry, and if it were permitted for the woman to marry herself off, then the prohibition addressed to her guardian against preventing her would have no intelligible meaning.

A question is then raised about how the phrase by that is admonished can stand with the singular pronoun while the address is to a plural.

phrases.translation: do not prevent them from re-marrying their ex-husbands if they come to an honourable agreement. This is enjoined on whoever has faith in Allah and the Last Day.
phrases.explanation:
The Exalted means by His saying by that what is mentioned in this verse, the prohibition addressed to the woman's guardians against preventing her from marrying. He says, this from which I have restrained you is an admonition from Me to whoever among you believes in Allah and the last day, so that he fears Allah and does it no wrong by harming his ward.

The answer is then given, that this is not permissible with the ordinary nouns, since a listener who hears one saying to a group, O people, this is your servant, will not understand that he means your servant in the plural. But it is so with that phrase because of its frequent use until the pronoun in it has become like a letter among the letters of the word.

phrases.translation: This is purer and more dignifying for you. Allah knows and you do not know
phrases.explanation:
The Exalted means by His saying that their marrying their husbands and the taking back of them by their husbands, in the manner He has permitted them, by a new marriage and a new gift, is purer for you.

And by is purer for you He means more excellent and better with Allah than their separation from their husbands, and the meaning of purity was expounded earlier.

And by and more chaste He means purer for your hearts, their hearts and the hearts of their husbands, free of suspicion, since when in the soul of each of the two there exists a bond of love one cannot be certain that they will not transgress it. Therefore Allah commanded the guardians, when the husbands wish to take each other back, that he should not prevent his ward.

phrases.translation: ˹Divorced˺ mothers will breastfeed their offspring for two whole years, for those who wish to complete the nursing ˹of their child˺.
phrases.explanation:
The Exalted means thereby that the women who are separated from their husbands and who have children whom they bore from them, they shall suckle their children, and He means thereby that they have a greater right to the suckling of their children than others. This however is not an obligation that He imposes upon them when the father of the child is alive and of means, so He has not imposed that upon her. It is therefore known that this saying is an indication of the utmost limit of the suckling, by which it is decided between the two parents when they disagree after its expiry.

The objection is then answered, that the Arabs sometimes say that so-and-so resided in that place two years while he resided there only one day and a part of a second, so it was said two complete years.

Another view is then given, that it was an indication that it was obligatory for the mothers to suckle them for two complete years, after which He lightened that with His saying for whoever wishes to complete the suckling, so He has left the choice to the fathers and the mothers.

And it is then said that it is an indication that thereby every child is meant, regardless of the time of its birth, and the answer to that is given at length, that Allah has not made His saying about the bearing and the weaning thirty months a religious duty not to exceed.

The recitation is then discussed, and the reading with the yāʾ and the accusative is preferred, because they are the ones who complete it.

phrases.translation: The child’s father will provide reasonable maintenance and clothing for the mother ˹during that period˺.
phrases.explanation:
And upon the fathers of the children rests, for the suckling women, their provision, and by provision He means that which nourishes them of food and their clothing, and by with that which is fitting He means what is obligatory for someone like her.

And no soul is burdened with any matter except with that which does not distress it, so Allah imposes upon the men nothing beyond their capacity.

A point of grammar is then given, that capacity is the verbal noun of a person's saying that a matter falls within his capacity, and the soul is burdened only with what affords it the room to give.

The reading is then preferred, the one in the accusative, because it is a prohibition from Allah to each of the two parents against harming one another.

phrases.translation: No one will be charged with more than they can bear.
phrases.explanation:
The reciters disagreed about the reading. The majority of the reciters of the people of Hijaz, Kufa and Syria read it with the fatḥa of the rāʾ, in the manner of the prohibition.

The meaning is then given, that the father of a child does no harm to the mother of his child because of his child from her, nor does the mother harm the father because of her child from him.

A claim is then made and set aside, that it was given only the fatḥa because that is one of the vowels, but that has no tenable meaning.

And it is then said that if the meaning were that the mother is the one not harmed, then the revelation would have to read let a mother do no harm to her child.

phrases.translation: No mother or father should be made to suffer for their child.
phrases.explanation:
The adherents disagreed about the heir of the child whom Allah obliged with the like of what He described. Some of them said that it is the heirs of the child on the father's side from his agnatic relatives, whoever it be, a brother, an uncle, a paternal cousin or a brother's son, and the report naming who said that is given.

Another group said that the one meant is the child itself, and the report naming who said that is given.

Others said that it is the one of the two parents of the child who remains after the death of the other of them, and the report naming who said that is given.

phrases.translation: The ˹father’s˺ heirs are under the same obligation. But if both sides decide—after mutual consultation and consent—to wean a child, then there is no blame on them. If you decide to have your children nursed by a wet-nurse, it is permissible as long as you pay fairly. Be mindful of Allah, and know that Allah is All-Seeing of what you do
phrases.explanation:
The scholars of interpretation differed about the interpretation of His saying like that. Some of them said that the interpretation thereof is that upon the heir of the child, after the death of its two parents, rests the like of what rested upon its father of suckling wage and maintenance, when the child has no property, and the report naming who said that is given.

A further point is then added, that Allah set the suckling at two years for whoever wishes to complete the suckling, and then He said that if the two of them both desire a weaning by mutual consent and consultation then no sin is upon them both, whether they wish to wean the child before the two years or after them.

phrases.translation: As for those of you who die and leave widows behind, let them observe a waiting period of four months and ten days.
phrases.explanation:
As for those of you who pass away and leave behind wives, let them observe a waiting period of four months and ten days, and the clause about the waiting is then explained. They restrain themselves, observing the waiting period, away from husbands, from perfume, from adornment and from removal from the dwelling they inhabited during the lifetime of their husbands, for four months and ten days, unless they are pregnant, in which case the waiting rests upon them until the moment they bring forth what they bear, and when they have brought forth what they bear their waiting period ends at that moment.

A point of grammar is then added, that some have claimed the predicate of those who pass away has been omitted, and the meaning is that those of you who pass away and leave behind wives, it behooves these to wait after their death, and that they wait stands in the nominative because it takes the place of it behooves.

A question is then raised about how it is said four months and ten and not two tens, and whether the woman observes the ten according to the nights or according to the days. Then the answer is given, that she observes them according to the days with their nights, and that it is the custom of the Arabs, when men and women are together and one leaves their number indefinite, that they express it according to the counting of the masculine and not of the feminine.

A further view is then recorded, that the woman whose husband has died has only been commanded to restrain herself away from husbands in particular, and not from perfume and adornment and passing the night outside the dwelling.

phrases.translation: When they have reached the end of this period, then you are not accountable for what they decide for themselves in a reasonable manner.
phrases.explanation:
The Exalted means thereby that when they reach the term in which it is permitted to them what was forbidden to them during their waiting period on account of the death of their husbands, after the passing of the four months and ten days, then there is no sin upon you concerning what they do with themselves properly, whereby He says, then there is no offense upon you, O guardians, concerning what the women whose husbands have died do with themselves, of using perfume, adorning themselves, removing from the dwelling in which they observed the waiting period, and marrying whomever it is permitted for them to marry.

And it has been said that He meant thereby only marriage in particular, and that the meaning of His saying in a proper manner is the permitted marriage.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Aware of what you do
phrases.explanation:
The Exalted means thereby that Allah is, with what you do, O guardians, in the matter of those of whom you are the guardian of your women, in preventing them and in marrying them off to whomever they wish to marry in a proper manner, and in other matters of yours and of theirs, well-acquainted, that is the possessor of acquaintance and knowledge, for nothing of that remains hidden from Him.

A question is then raised about the meaning of the addition of these ten days to the months, and it is said that something has been said about that in what follows, and the verse then closes with the command to fear Allah and the statement that Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

phrases.translation: There is no blame on you for subtly showing interest in ˹divorced or widowed˺ women or for hiding ˹the intention˺ in your hearts. Allah knows that you are considering them ˹for marriage˺.
phrases.explanation:
The Exalted means thereby that there is no blame upon you, O men, in that whereby you allude to a proposal of marriage to the women, namely to the women who are passing the waiting period on account of the death of their husbands, so long as you do not expressly conclude a marriage contract, and that is the whole of what the verse permits.

A point of grammar is then added, that the grammarians differed concerning the meaning of the proposal, some of them saying that it is the mentioning, and the preferred view is then given, that it is the form of the saying of one who says I proposed to so-and-so, and that the meaning of it is that he requested of her his proposal with respect to herself.

And as for the allusion, that is that which belongs to the implication of speech, whereby the hearer understands that which he would understand from the open utterance of it.

phrases.translation: But do not make a secret commitment with them—you can only show interest in them appropriately.
phrases.explanation:
And the secret tryst is then explained. The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of the secret that Allah forbade His servants to arrange with the women in the waiting period. Some of them said that it is fornication. And others said that the meaning of it is that no pledge or covenant is to be taken from them during their waiting period that they will marry none other than you. And others said that the meaning of it is that the man says to her, do not pass me by with yourself. And others said that the meaning of it is that they are not to be married in secret during their waiting period.

And it is then shown that the word can be directed to only two of three meanings, since the third, the choicest and the nobility, is not intended here, and those two are the thing that the soul of the one making the tryst conceals between the two parties to the tryst, and lying together and sexual intercourse. And one says of everything that a person conceals within himself that it is his secret.

The most correct of the statements in the explanation thereof is then given, that the word means in this place fornication, because the Arabs call sexual intercourse and the man's lying with the woman by that word, as that belongs to what takes place in secrecy between men and women, not openly and not observed. And the first of the two is then set aside, since if it were the meaning it would not be forbidden to him to arrange with her openly, and the fact that it is forbidden both in secret and in public makes clear that the meaning is the other one.

The explanation of the verse is then given. There is no blame upon you, O people, in that whereby you allude toward the women in the waiting period on account of the death of their husbands, with respect to the proposal to the women, so long as you do not openly utter to them marriage and the need for them, when you conceal it within yourselves, so long as they are in their waiting period.

And He forbade you to arrange sexual intercourse with them in their waiting period, by one of you saying to one of them, I have married you within myself, and I only await the elapsing of your waiting period, whereby he requests of her that she make possible for him sexual intercourse and lying together.

The exception is then explained. He made the proper word an exception to that which He forbade, namely the secret tryst of the man with the woman, and its meaning is that you speak a proper word, so He permitted one to speak to her the proper word in her waiting period, and that is what He permitted with His saying that there is no blame upon you in that whereby you allude to a proposal of marriage to the women.

The command is then explained. Do not make the conclusion of the marriage contract valid during the waiting period of the woman who is passing her waiting period, so as to make it binding between you and them and conclude it before the elapsing of the waiting period, until the prescribed term reaches its end.

phrases.translation: Do not commit to the bond of marriage until the waiting period expires. Know that Allah is aware of what is in your hearts, so beware of Him. And know that Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Forbearing
phrases.explanation:
The Exalted means by His saying or you conceal it within yourselves, or you conceal within yourselves and keep secret, namely the proposal to them and the intention to marry them, while they are in their waiting period. Then there is likewise no blame upon you in that, so long as you do not firmly resolve to conclude the marriage contract until the prescribed term reaches its end.

And know, O people, that Allah knows what is within yourselves of desire for them, so beware of Him, and know that Allah is forgiving and Forbearing.

A point of wording is then added, that one says of a thing kept hidden within oneself that the person keeps it hidden, and that one says of a thing covered that he covers it.

phrases.translation: There is no blame if you divorce women before the marriage is consummated or the dowry is settled.
phrases.explanation:
The reciters have recited it differently. The general reading of the reciters of Hijaz and Basra recites it without the alif, derived from the expression of touching, shortened, with the shadda.

Others recite it with the vowel and with the alif after the mīm, in order to make it accord with the reading upon which there is agreement in His word that the freeing of a slave is obligatory before they touch one another, and they gave to it the meaning of the act of both the man and the woman toward his companion.

And it is then shown that no rational person is ignorant, when it is said to him that he touched his wife, that the body of the touched woman has met that of the body of the touching man, so that by the report that he touched his companion it is understood that his companion touched him, and therefore there is no ground to judge one of the two readings as more correct than the other.

The sense of the whole clause is then given. There is no blame upon you if you divorce the women so long as you have not touched them, at whatever time you wish to divorce them, for there exists no prescribed manner in their divorce. But that is not so for the woman whom he has touched, for her husband may not divorce her except according to the waiting period.

phrases.translation: But give them a ˹suitable˺ compensation—the rich according to his means and the poor according to his.
phrases.explanation:
The sense of the clause is then explained at length. Allah meant by it only the women who are divorced before one cohabits with them, in a marriage for which a bridal gift has already been stipulated, and since it is learned from what follows that only the woman for whom it has been stipulated is meant.

The correct ruling is then given, that what is obligatory of it for the divorced woman as a charge upon the man is according to the measure of his hardship and his ease, not according to the measure of the woman, for if that were obligatory for the woman according to the bridal gift of her like then His words upon the well-to-do is according to his means would have no comprehensible meaning.

And it is then made clear that this is according to the measure of the man and not of her, since the bridal gift of a woman like her may be a great sum while the man is needy and owns nothing, and if an amount equal to half of it were imposed upon him he would be obligated to something of which even the well-to-do are incapable.

Another view is then recorded, that the gift is obligatory for every divorced woman except the one for whom the bridal gift has been stipulated, who if divorced before he has entered in upon her has no gift and is entitled only to half of the stated bridal gift.

The view most in accordance with correctness is then given, that for every divorced woman there is a gift, because Allah has said that for the divorced women there is a gift according to what is proper, a duty upon the God-fearing, and He has not excepted one of them to the exclusion of another.

A question is then raised about the one who was divorced before the touching when something had been stipulated for her, and the answer is given that they are both two readings that the community has transmitted and that they agree in meaning, and the preference of one reading is permissible only where it is distinguished by an additional meaning.

The interpretation of the verse is then given, that there is no objection upon you because you have divorced the women while you had stipulated for them as long as you have not touched them, and if you divorce them while you have not touched them before you have stipulated for them, and provide all of them with a gift, as for him among you who has amplitude and wealth from his gift according to the measure of his wealth, and as for him among you who has need and poverty according to his capacity.

phrases.translation: A reasonable compensation is an obligation on the good-doers
phrases.explanation:
A point of grammar is then added. By a duty upon the doers of good, the meaning is a gift according to what is proper, which is a duty upon the doers of good, and since the insertion of the alif and the lam indicated the right, and that is of the quality of what is proper, it is in the accusative as a detachment from it.

Another claim is then set aside, that it is in the accusative with the meaning that He confirmed that as a right, for that contradicts the outward purport of the recitation, since Allah made the gift for the divorced women into a right for them as a charge upon their husbands, and the interpretation of the statement is then that you provide for them a gift according to what is proper.

And by the doers of good it means those who do good to themselves in hastening to obedience to Allah in what He has imposed upon them, and by according to what is proper it means according to what Allah has commanded you with respect to your giving that to them.

phrases.translation: And if you divorce them before consummating the marriage but after deciding on a dowry, pay half of the dowry, unless the wife graciously waives it or the husband graciously pays in full. Graciousness is closer to righteousness. And do not forget kindness among yourselves. Surely Allah is All-Seeing of what you do
phrases.explanation:
The clause is explained first. The phrase means the husband in whose hand is the knot of his own marriage, and those who take it to be the guardian have erred.

The view most fitting is then given, namely that some of you remit in favour of others, O husbands and wives, of what was due to one chargeable to the other, and that is nearer to godfearingness.

The clause about kindness is then explained. Let the man who has divorced his wife before touching her be kind and make her bride-gift complete for her, and if both are niggardly then there is due to her half.

The closing words are then explained. Verily, Allah is, with respect to what you do, seeing, whereby He means the possessor of sight, and He reckons it up.

phrases.translation: Observe the ˹five obligatory˺ prayers—especially the middle prayer—and stand in true devotion to Allah
phrases.explanation:
Thus he urged toward guarding over it with an urging such as he did not urge toward any other prayer, and he warned his community against neglecting it, and promised them double the reward of what He promised for the rest of the prayers.

And it is so because Allah has made the night for rest, and so it is with the morning prayer. And as for the noon prayer, its time is the time of the people's rest from their occupations during the intense heat and in the winter days, and the times at which they occupy themselves with their occupations are two, the beginning of the day, in which Allah has lightened their burden, and the end of the day, in which He prescribed the afternoon prayer and urged toward guarding over it.

phrases.translation: If you are in danger, pray on foot or while riding.
phrases.explanation:
The Exalted means by this that you stand before Allah in your prayer obedient to Him, and if you fear an enemy of yours, at the moment of your encounter with them, you are apprehensive for your own lives, that you cannot pray standing upon your feet, devout before Allah, then pray on foot, while you are in your war and fighting against your enemy, or mounted upon the backs of your mounts.

A point of grammar is then given, that the accusative of the two is permissible on the basis of the elided meaning, since the Arabs do this especially in the conditional, whose second part resembles something joined to the first, so they join the answer to the first part.

And the fear on the basis of which it is permitted is then set out. It is the fear for one's life at the baring of the swords and the swordfighting in the fight against whom one is commanded to fight, an enemy of the Muslims, or the attack of a beast of prey, or a flood in which one fears drowning.

And the prophet made a distinction between the ruling concerning the prayer of fear outside the state of swordfighting and pursuit and the ruling concerning it in the state of intense fear.

phrases.translation: But when you are safe, ˹take time to˺ remember Allah for teaching you what you did not know
phrases.explanation:
The explanation of it is that when you are secure, O believers, from your enemy, that he might be able to kill you while you are occupied with your prayer, and you have come to rest, then remember Allah in your prayer and outside it, with thankfulness to Him, praise and glorification of Him, for that with which He has favoured you, namely the favour of attaining the truth from which your enemies have strayed, as He has guided you by teaching you His prescriptions and the accounts of the communities that preceded you, and the events that will occur after you. Thus He taught you from Himself what you did not know.

And in the words and when you are secure lies the clear indication of the correctness of that interpretation.

phrases.translation: Those of you who die leaving widows should bequeath for them a year’s maintenance without forcing them out.
phrases.explanation:
The Exalted means by this, O you men, those of you who die and leave wives behind, that is, wives who during his lifetime were his women through marriage, and then the discourse is turned away from the mention of the one about whom it originally began to speak toward the mention of their wives.

A point of grammar is then added, that the bequest, when it stands in the nominative, stands there with the meaning that prescribed for you is a testamentary bequest for your wives, for the Arabs with indefinite nouns place that which makes them nominative before them.

The reading preferred is then given, that of the nominative, on account of the outward wording of the Quran indicating that the residence of the widow in the house of her deceased husband for a full year was a right belonging to her.

The answer is then given, that since the one who makes a testament disposes only during his lifetime over that whose execution he commands after his death, we know that the residence of the wife during the year is a right belonging to her that became obligatory in his estate.

Moreover, if that were obligatory upon them through a bequest of their husbands, then it would not have been a right for them when their husbands had not bequeathed in their favour, and their heirs would have had the right to expel them before the end of the year, whereas He has said without expulsion. Rather, the explanation is that Allah has prescribed for their wives upon you a bequest from Himself, that you do not expel them for a year.

The phrase without expulsion is then explained, that He has made what He has allotted to them a provision from Himself for them until the end of the year, not as an expulsion from the dwelling of the husband.

phrases.translation: But if they choose to leave, you are not accountable for what they reasonably decide for themselves. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.explanation:
The most fitting of these statements is then given, that Allah had allotted to the wives of the men who died a year's residence in his dwelling and her maintenance from the estate of her husband until the expiry of the year.

And a point of grammar is added, that the provision stands in the accusative only because in the words a testamentary bequest for their wives lies the meaning of Allah has given them a provision.

The sense of the clause is then explained, that the provision holds for them only as long as they remain in the dwellings of their husbands, and their rights lapse by their departure.

The closing words are then explained. Allah is Almighty in His requital of whoever transgresses His command, against whoever withholds from their wives what He has prescribed, and against whoever expels them.

phrases.translation: Reasonable provisions must be made for divorced women—a duty on those mindful ˹of Allah˺
phrases.explanation:
The Exalted means thereby that to every woman who is divorced there is due, from the husband who has divorced her, a provision, and He means that which she may make use of, such as clothing and garments, or maintenance, or a servant, and other things from which one derives benefit, and the meaning of this was expounded earlier together with the disagreement of the scholars concerning it.

Another view is then recorded, that in this verse there is an indication that to every divorced woman a provision is due, since Allah sent it down to His prophet only because of the added meaning it contains in relation to the other verses about the provision, for the remaining verses contain only the exposition of the ruling concerning the untouched woman when she is divorced, whereas this verse contains the exposition of the ruling concerning all divorced women.

The phrase as an obligation upon the God-fearing is then explained from what was expounded earlier, and the disagreement of the grammarians over the similar wording in the verse concerning the doers of good, so that there is no need to repeat it here.

phrases.translation: This is how Allah makes His revelations clear to you, so perhaps you will understand
phrases.explanation: The Exalted says, just as I have made clear to you what is obligatory upon you toward your wives and what your wives are obliged to render toward you, and just as I have made known to you My ordinances in these verses, so too do I make clear to you all the remaining ordinances in My signs which I have sent down upon My prophet in this Book, that you might understand My prescribed limits, and so that you might grasp what is obligatory upon you of My imposed duties, and thereby come to know what contains the welfare of your religion and your worldly life.

phrases.translation: Have you ˹O Prophet˺ not seen those who fled their homes in the thousands for fear of death?
phrases.explanation:
By have you not seen, the sense is have you not known, O Muhammad, and this belongs to seeing with the heart and not seeing with the eye, for the prophet did not live among those whom Allah mentions in this report, and seeing with the heart means that which he perceived inwardly and of which he had knowledge. So the meaning is have you not known, O Muhammad, of those who went out from their dwellings while they were in their thousands.

The exegetes then differed concerning the explanation of His word while they were in their thousands. Some said that it refers to the number, in the sense of the plural of thousand. And others said that the meaning of it is that while they were joined in concord.

phrases.translation: Allah said to them, “Die!” then He gave them life.
phrases.explanation: And the verse is then explained at length, that Allah has by it only exhorted His servants to perseverance in the struggle in His way and to patience in the battle against the enemies of His religion, and He has encouraged them by instructing them that the causing to die and the bringing back to life lie in His hands and belong to Him and not to His creatures, and that the flight from battle saves no one from His decree when it descends upon him, just as it did not avail the fugitives from the plague, until the command of Allah came to them and laid them all low.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is ever Bountiful to humanity, but most people are ungrateful
phrases.explanation:
The sounder of the two positions in the explanation of His word while they were in their thousands is the position of those who said that by it the greatness of the number is meant, and not the position of those who said that by it concord is meant, and that they went out from their dwellings without division among them.

And the Exalted means by it that Allah is full of grace and beneficence toward His creatures, in that He gives them to perceive the path of guidance and warns them against the paths of perdition, and through others of His favors, just as He brought back to life those who went out in their thousands in fear of death after He had caused them to die, and made them an example.

phrases.translation: Fight in the cause of Allah, and know that Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation:
And fight, O believers, in the way of Allah, that is to say, in His religion to which He has guided you, and not in obedience to Satan, fight the enemies of your religion who turn people away from the way of your Lord. Do not refrain from fighting against them when you meet them, for in My hand lies your life and your death.

And it is then said that there is no ground for the claim that this is a command to those who departed from their dwellings after He had revived them, since the words can be nothing other than one of three possibilities, one of which is that He revived them and said to them, fight in the way of Allah.

phrases.translation: Who will lend to Allah a good loan which Allah will multiply many times over?
phrases.explanation:
Who is it that spends in the way of Allah, and so assists someone whose mount has grown weak, or strengthens someone in need who has aimed at struggle in the way of Allah, and gives to the needy among them? That is the goodly loan that the servant lends to his Lord.

And Allah has called this only a loan, because the meaning of a loan is that a man gives another his property in ownership, so that the latter returns to him the like of it when he requests it. And since the one who gives to the people of need in the way of Allah gives only out of desire for what Allah has promised him of rich reward with Him on the day of resurrection, He has called it a loan.

phrases.translation: It is Allah ˹alone˺ who decreases and increases ˹wealth˺.
phrases.explanation:
The reciters differed over the reading of His words with the alif and in the nominative, in the meaning that the one who will lend to Allah a goodly loan so that He multiplies it for him, and yet others read it with the retention of the alif and in the accusative, in the meaning of a question.

The correct of these readings is then given, that of the one who read it with the retention of the alif and with the verb in the nominative, since in His words who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan there lies the meaning of a conditional clause,

And the sense is then explained, that it is He in whose hand lies the withholding and the expanding of the provisions of the servants, and not another of those whom the people of shirk claimed to be gods. And by His words and gives abundantly He means that He expands, through the spreading out of provision, for whom He wills.

phrases.translation: And to Him you will ˹all˺ be returned
phrases.explanation:
And to Allah is your return, O people, so fear Allah regarding yourselves, that you neglect His obligations and overstep His limits, and that the one among you for whom He has spread out of His provision acts otherwise than his Lord has permitted him to act therewith, and that the needy one among you, when He has withheld of his provision, be brought by his want to disobedience to Him, so that he thereby earns, at his return to his Creator, that against which he has no resistance, of His painful chastisement.

One of the exegetes is then cited, and he interprets His words and to Him you shall be returned as and to the dust you shall be returned.

phrases.translation: Have you not seen those chiefs of the Children of Israel after Moses? They said to one of their prophets, “Appoint for us a king, ˹and˺ we will fight in the cause of Allah.”
phrases.explanation:
The opening calls on the hearer to see what happened to the notables of the Children of Israel after Moses. They asked one of their prophets for a king to fight with in the way of Allah, and the exegetes differ over which prophet they asked, one naming Samuel and another Joshua the son of Nun, and over the occasion.

The wording of their request is then examined. When the phrase is read with the nun it can only be read in the jussive form, as a command or as the condition answering one, and the Arabs do not suppress two such particles. Read with the ya instead, it may stand in the nominative as a description of the king, so the sense becomes appoint for us one who fights in the way of Allah.

phrases.translation: He said, “Are you not going to cower if ordered to fight?” They replied, “How could we refuse to fight in the cause of Allah,
phrases.explanation:
The passage is then read as a whole. The prophet's question asks whether they are going to cower when the fighting is written for them, and their answer puts the obstacle in the command itself rather than in any unwillingness to obey.

A point of grammar is settled along the way. It is asked why the particle is added in what is the matter with us that we do not fight in the way of Allah, when it is left out in the similar question elsewhere. The answer given is that the particle carries the sense of what is the matter with you regarding not fighting, and it is used this way because the preventing concerns only the future of actions, so one says I prevented you from standing, but not I prevented you that you stood.

A smaller point of usage is added at the same time. The word for permanence is used with the interrogative particle and with the particle of negation together, because the predicate of the negated question stands close in meaning to that of the question itself, and the speaker needs no witness for a usage so common among the Arabs.

phrases.translation: while we were driven out of our homes and ˹separated from˺ our children?” But when they were ordered to fight, they fled, except for a few of them. And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of the wrongdoers
phrases.explanation:
The clause about being driven out is then explained. It means that those of their men and women who were overcome were driven out of their dwellings and their children, and taken captive. The statement has an outward generality and an inward specificity, since those who asked for the king were still in their own houses, and only those taken captive and subdued were driven out.

The turning away is then described. When fighting against their enemy was imposed on them they turned away, except for a few, and the few are those who crossed the river with Talut. The verse closes by saying that Allah has full knowledge of the wrongdoers, meaning that He knows which of them broke what they had promised and contradicted the command of their Lord.

phrases.translation: Their prophet told them, “Allah has appointed Saul to be your king.” They protested, “How can he be our king when some of us are more deserving of kingship than he, and he has not been blessed with vast riches?”
phrases.explanation:
The Exalted means by this that their prophet Samuel said to the notables of the Children of Israel, Allah has given you what you asked for and has sent Talut to you as king. Their answer follows. How could the kingship over us belong to Talut, when he is of the tribe of Benjamin, in which there is neither kingship nor prophethood, while we are of the tribe of Judah and have more right to it.

The last part of their objection is then taken up. He has not been given vast riches means that Talut has not been given a great fortune, for he was a water-carrier, and it has also been said that he was a tanner. The word for kingship is said to mean, in this place, command over the army.

phrases.translation: He replied, “Allah has chosen him over you and blessed him with knowledge and stature.
phrases.explanation:
The answer of the prophet is then given. Allah has chosen him over you is the saying of their prophet Samuel, and its sense is that Allah has preferred him above them.

The rest of the answer is explained. The phrase about an abundance in knowledge and bodily stature means that Allah gave him ampleness in both, and in knowledge a superiority above what He gave to the others addressed, because a revelation from Allah befell him. In bodily stature he was given a height that surpassed them all, and no other received the like.

Another view is recorded on the same words. On that reading the phrase means that in addition to choosing him, Allah gave him an abundance in knowledge and bodily stature, so the extra gift is stated apart from the choice.

phrases.translation: Allah grants kingship to whoever He wills. And Allah is All-Bountiful, All-Knowing.”
phrases.explanation:
The closing words are explained. The kingship belongs to Allah and lies in His hand and not in that of another, for He gives it to whom He wills, appoints it with him and withholds it from whom He wills. So they are told not to reject that Allah sends Talut over them as a king even though he does not belong to the house of kingship, for kingship is not an inheritance but lies in Allah's hand.
