The last two words are then taken. All-encompassing means through His bounty, with which He does good to whom He loves and wishes to bestow upon whom He wills. All-knowing means that He knows who is worthy to receive the kingship that He gives, and He gives it because the man was worthy of it.

phrases.translation: Their prophet further told them, “The sign of Saul’s kingship is that the Ark will come to you
phrases.explanation:
The announcement is the proof that the leading men of the Children of Israel did not accept Allah's appointment of Talut. They asked for a sign that would confirm his truthfulness, and the sense of the answer is that already given, that Allah gives His kingship to whom He wills.

The sign of his kingship means the sign of Talut's kingship, the proof they asked for that Allah had appointed him king over them though he was not of royal line. The ark is the one the Children of Israel carried before them when they met an enemy, and no enemy stood firm while it was there. That was until they neglected the command of Allah and their dissension with their prophets grew, and then Allah took the ark from them time after time, until he took it for good.

Where the ark had been is set out. One view is that it stayed with them from the time of Musa and Harun until unbelieving kings took it. Another is that it lay in the wilderness, where Musa left it with his servant Yusha, and the angels carried it to Talut's house. The more correct of the two is that an enemy held it, since the definite article is used only for what they knew.

phrases.translation: —containing reassurance from your Lord
phrases.explanation:
The phrase in which is read as meaning in the ark, and the people of interpretation differed over what the sakina is and what it means, each of them reporting it from those before them. Some said it is a gently blowing wind with a face like the face of a human being. Others said it has a head like the head of a cat and two wings. Others said no, it is the head of a dead cat.

Others said it is merely a golden basin from Paradise in which the hearts of the prophets were washed, and the sight of it gave them rest. Others said it is a spirit from Allah that speaks. Others said it is what they recognise of the signs by which they find rest and by which their hearts are quieted. Others said it is mercy and compassion. Others said it is dignity and composure of the heart.

When the meaning is taken as these accounts set it out, any of them can stand, for all of them are conclusive signs by which the souls find rest and through which the breasts are cooled, and each of the early authorities is followed in this. And once the sense is settled, it becomes clear that the sign which was in the ark, by which the souls found rest through their knowledge of the genuineness of its affair, was named only with the word for the effect it produces, while it is something other than that effect, because of the indication of the word.

phrases.translation: and relics of the family of Moses and the family of Aaron,
phrases.explanation:
The remnant is explained first. It means the remaining thing, from the word of one who says that a remnant was left of this matter, a form of the pattern that makes the sakina from sakana, to settle. The phrase about what the family of Musa and the family of Harun left behind means from their legacy.

What that legacy was is then set out. Some said the staff of Musa and the fragments of the tablets. Others said the staff of Musa and the staff of Harun and something of the tablets. Others said the staff and the two sandals. Others said the staff alone. Others said the fragments of the tablets and what was broken of them. Others said it was the striving in the path of Allah.

The more correct statement is that the remnant may have been the staff, the shards of the tablets, the Torah or a part of it, the two sandals, the garment, and the striving in the path of Allah, or a part of that. This is a matter whose knowledge cannot be reached by deduction or by the sense of the words, and can be reached only through a report that makes its knowledge necessary. Among the people of Islam there is no report of that quality, so it is not permissible to declare one of these views right and another weak, since all are possible.

phrases.translation: which will be carried by the angels.
phrases.explanation:
The people of interpretation differed over the manner in which the angels carried the ark. Some said the angels carry it between heaven and earth until they set it down among them. Others said that the angels drive forward the beasts of burden that carry it.

The more correct of the two is that the angels carried the ark until they set it down in the house of Talut, raised up among the Children of Israel. The reason given is that Allah said carried by the angels and did not say brought by the angels, and what the cows drew forward on a cart is not the carrying of it, since carrying means that the carrier himself bears what he carries.

phrases.translation: Surely in this is a sign for you, if you ˹truly˺ believe.”
phrases.explanation:
The sense of the words is that the prophet Samuel said to the Children of Israel, in your obtaining of the ark, in which is a calm from your Lord and a remnant of what the family of Musa and of Harun left behind, carried by the angels, is verily a sign for you, that is a sign and a proof of my truthfulness in what I have conveyed to you, that Allah has appointed Talut as king over you.

The condition is explained. If you have denied me in what I told you about Allah's appointment of him and suspected me in what I said, if you are believers means that you believe me upon the coming of the sign you asked me for as proof of what I told you about Talut's kingship.

phrases.translation: When Saul marched forth with his army, he cautioned: “Allah will test you with a river.
phrases.explanation:
Something has been left out of this report, and what has already been said makes it unnecessary to state. The sense is that the ark came to them, in which was a calm from their Lord and a remnant of what the house of Musa and Harun had left behind, borne by the angels, and that they then believed their prophet, acknowledged that Allah had sent Talut as king, and submitted. He would not have set out with them except after they had taken pleasure in him and handed over the kingship, since he could not compel them.

The word for set out means that he departed with the army and marched out with them. Its original sense is cutting off, as when a man leaves a place and passes it by, and a decisive word cuts through and separates true from false.

It is said that Talut set out that day with the armies from Jerusalem, and they were eighty thousand fighters. The river is said to have been one between the Jordan and Palestine, others said it is the river of Palestine. He gave the warning because they complained to him of the scarcity of water and asked him to ask Allah for it.

phrases.translation: So whoever drinks ˹his fill˺ from it is not with me, and whoever does not taste it—except a sip from the hollow of his hands—is definitely with me.”
phrases.explanation:
Whoever drinks from it is not with me means that whoever drinks of its water does not belong to the people of Talut's authority and obedience, nor to those who believe in Allah and the meeting with Him. Whoever does not taste it is of me means whoever does not taste the water of that river, for he belongs to them.

The pronoun in both phrases goes back to the river, while the sense is of its water, and the word for water is left out on the hearer's understanding. The one who scoops a single handful with his hand is made an exception. The reciters differed over that handful, some reading it as a single act of scooping and others as the water in the palm of the one who scoops, the second preferred.

phrases.translation: They all drank ˹their fill˺ except for a few! When he and the ˹remaining˺ faithful with him crossed the river, they said, “Now we are no match for Goliath and his warriors.”
phrases.explanation:
The phrase about crossing is explained. When he crossed it means when Talut crossed the river, the pronoun in the verb going back to the river and the word he being Talut himself, and those who believed with him means that those who believed crossed it with him.

How many crossed with him that day was a matter of difference. One account says it was the number of the people of Badr, three hundred and some ten-odd men, and that none crossed except a believer. Another says four thousand crossed with Talut, and that when they saw Jalut they too turned back and said they had no power, and that three thousand six hundred and some eighty turned back as well, leaving three hundred and some ten-odd.

Another account says that the group who claimed they had no power were the people of unbelief and hypocrisy, who had turned away from Talut and from those who stood firm with him. A further account says that both groups were people of faith and that among them none drank of the water except a handful, all of them being people of obedience, but some firmer in certainty than others.

phrases.translation: But those ˹believers˺ who were certain they would meet Allah reasoned, “How many times has a small force vanquished a mighty army by the Will of Allah! And Allah is ˹always˺ with the steadfast.”
phrases.explanation:
Those who were convinced they would meet Allah means those who know with certainty they will meet Allah, and the passage shows that these are the ones who said how many a small company has overcome a large company, not those who said they had no power.

How much is meant by how many, and by the permission of Allah is meant the decree of Allah. The word for group means a band of people, the same as a company of men.

And Allah is with the patient means that Allah is the helper of those who hold themselves back for His good pleasure and obedience, and gives them victory over His enemies. It is said in the same way of anyone who helps another that he is with him, meaning that he aids him.

phrases.translation: When they advanced to face Goliath and his warriors, they prayed, “Our Lord! Shower us with perseverance, make our steps firm, and give us victory over the disbelieving people.”
phrases.explanation: The meaning of His statement they marched out is that they betook themselves to the open and level part of the land, for this reason one says of the man who relieves himself that he went out to relieve himself, because the people in former times used to relieve themselves in the open part of the land. And His statement and make our feet firm means and strengthen our hearts in the struggle against them, so that our feet may remain firm and we may not take flight before them, that is, and help us against the disbelieving people, those who disbelieved in You and thus denied You as God and worshipped another than You, and took the idols as lords.

phrases.translation: So they defeated them by Allah’s Will, and David killed Goliath. And Allah blessed David with kingship and wisdom and taught him what He willed. Had Allah not repelled a group of people by ˹the might of˺ another, corruption would have dominated the earth, but Allah is Gracious to all
phrases.explanation:
The clause is then explained. And Allah gave David the kingship and wisdom and taught him of what He willed, and the kingship is authority and the wisdom is prophethood, and taught him of what He willed means He taught him the making of the coats of mail.

The next clause is then explained. Were it not that Allah, by means of the people of obedience to Him, repelled the people of disobedience and shirk toward Him, as He did by those who waged struggle with Talut and warded off Jalut and his armies, the earth would become corrupt, that is to say, its inhabitants would perish through His punishment of them. But Allah is a Possessor of bounty toward His creation.

phrases.translation: These are Allah’s revelations which We recite to you ˹O Prophet˺ in truth. And you are truly one of the messengers
phrases.explanation:
The Exalted means by His word these are the signs of Allah, these signs in which Allah has recounted the affair of those who left their dwellings, and they were in their thousands, out of fear of death, and the affair of the notables among the Children of Israel after Musa, who asked their prophet to appoint over them Talut as king, and what follows thereafter of signs up to His word but Allah is full of bounty toward the worlds.

And He means by His word signs of Allah, His proofs, His signs, and His indications. And He says, these proofs which I have proclaimed to you, O Muhammad, and which I have made known to you, and you did not fabricate them nor compose them from yourself, for you are unlettered.

phrases.translation: We have chosen some of those messengers above others. Allah spoke directly to some, and raised some high in rank.
phrases.explanation: These are the messengers whose accounts Allah has narrated in this surah, such as Musa the son of Imran, Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Yaqub, Samuel and Dawud, and all the rest whose story is told here in the Book. The sense of the words is: these are My messengers, I have preferred some of them over others, and I spoke to some of them, and the one to whom I spoke among them was Musa, and I raised some of them in ranks above others, by way of honour and elevation of station, as the verse that follows shows when it tells of Jesus the son of Mary and of the proofs that were given to him.

phrases.translation: To Jesus, son of Mary, We gave clear proofs and supported him with the holy spirit.
phrases.explanation:
The clear proofs are the signs of his prophethood, such as healing the one born blind and the leper, raising the dead, and what resembles these, together with the Gospel which was sent down to him, in which Allah made clear what He had laid upon him.

And we supported him means that we made him strong and aided him with the holy spirit, that is with the spirit of Allah, and that is Jibril. The disagreement of the scholars over the meaning of the holy spirit, and what is most correct about it, has already been mentioned earlier, so there is no need to repeat it here.

phrases.translation: If Allah had willed, succeeding generations would not have fought ˹among themselves˺ after receiving the clear proofs.
phrases.explanation:
And had Allah willed, those who came after them would not have fought one another. The ones meant are those who came after the messengers whom He has described, the ones He preferred over others and raised in ranks, and after Jesus the son of Mary, while signs had come to them in which there was deterrence for whom Allah guides and grants success.

The words after the clear proofs had come to them mean that there had come to them of the signs of Allah that which made the truth clear to them and showed them the way. As for the phrase after them, it has been said that the two letters refer to the mention of Musa and Jesus.

phrases.translation: But they differed—some believed while others disbelieved. Yet if Allah had willed, they would not have fought one another. But Allah does what He wills
phrases.explanation:
But those who came after the messengers differed, because Allah had not willed that they should not fight one another, and so they fought after the clear proofs of their Lord had come to them, and the proof had been established against them concerning the oneness of Allah, the messengership of His messengers and the revelation of His book.

Then some of them disbelieved in Allah and in His signs and some of them believed. They did what they did of disbelief and disobedience deliberately, after they knew the proof was established against them and that they were in error. This is why the verse ends by saying that if Allah had willed they would not have fought one another, but Allah does what He wills.

phrases.translation: O believers! Donate from what We have provided for you before the arrival of a Day when there will be no bargaining, friendship, or intercession. Those who disbelieve are ˹truly˺ the wrongdoers
phrases.explanation:
O you who believe, spend in the way of Allah of that which We have provided you, give thereof as alms, and discharge the dues We have imposed. The reason is given after that: lay up for yourselves with Allah a store in this life by spending in His way, giving alms to the poor and needy and discharging what He has laid upon you, and purchase what is with Him of the honour prepared for His protected ones.

That day is a day of requital and reward and punishment, not a day of action, so you will not be able then to buy what you could. The disbelievers are the wrongdoers, meaning those who place their denial in a wrong place, who do what is not their place to do and say what is not their place to say. The denial of friendship and intercession was intended only for them, and Allah was not wrong in it, being the reward of the disbelief before. Rather they are the wrongdoers against themselves, by deeds that brought the punishment of their Lord on them.

phrases.translation: Allah! There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him, the Ever-Living, All-Sustaining.
phrases.explanation:
The word Allah was explained earlier. The phrase there is no god but He is a prohibition of worshipping anything other than Allah, the Living, the Self-Subsisting Sustainer, whose attribute is that with which He described Himself in this verse. The word Allah is said of the One to whom the worship of creation is due, and the Living, the Self-Subsisting Sustainer means that there is no god besides Him and no one worshipped besides Him. So worship nothing besides the Living, the Sustainer, whom neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes.

The Living means the One to whom belongs the abiding life and the permanence that has no beginning bounded by a limit and no end bounded by a term, since everything else besides Him, even if it is living, has a life with a bounded beginning and a stretched-out end which ceases at the ceasing of its term.

The people of inquiry differed over this. Some said that Allah called Himself the Living only because of His governing affairs in their proper ways and His determining things according to their measures, so that He is living through governance and not through a life. Others said no, He is living through a life that is an attribute belonging to Him. Yet others said no, it is a name among the names by which He names Himself, and we say it in submission to His command.

The whole sense of the words is that He is the Living, who does not die, and the Self-Subsisting Sustainer over all that is below Him, through provision, preservation, governance and the conveying from state to state, and that neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him, for what changes others does not change Him, and the passing of the nights and days does not snatch Him away from that upon which He has been from all eternity, rather He is abiding in one state and the Sustainer of all created beings.

phrases.translation: Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him.
phrases.explanation:
The drowsiness does not overtake Him means that no slumber overtakes Him so that He would slumber, and no sleep so that He would sink into heavy sleep.

The word for drowsiness is used of a person who is heavy with sleep and sleepy, and of the drowsiness of sleep in the eye, so that one says of such a person that he drowses, that a drowsiness came over him, and that he is a drowsy one.

And neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him means only that no defects afflict Him and no shortcomings touch Him, since drowsiness and sleep are two states that overwhelm the understanding of a man and snatch him away from the state in which he was before they came upon him.

phrases.translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who could possibly intercede with Him without His permission?
phrases.explanation:
To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth means that He is the Owner of all this without partner and without equal, and the Creator of all of it to the exclusion of every god and every object of worship.

As for who is it that intercedes with Him except by His permission, the sense is that who is it that intercedes for those whom He owns, if He wills to punish them, unless He grants him leave and permits him to intercede for them. Allah said this only because the polytheists said that they worship their idols only that those idols may bring them nearer to Allah, so they are told not to worship idols that avail them nothing with Him.

phrases.translation: He ˹fully˺ knows what is ahead of them and what is behind them, but no one can grasp any of His knowledge—except what He wills ˹to reveal˺.
phrases.explanation:
He knows what is before them and what is behind them means that He is the One who encompasses with knowledge everything that has been and everything that exists, and nothing of that remains hidden from Him.

And they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills means that He is the Knowing from whom nothing remains hidden, who encompasses all of that and knows it fully to the exclusion of all who are below Him, and that no one besides Him knows anything except what He wills that he should know, so that He willed it and thus he knew it. By it is meant also that worship is not due to one who is ignorant of things, so how could an idol that understands nothing at all be worshipped.

phrases.translation: His Seat encompasses the heavens and the earth,
phrases.explanation:
The exegetes differed over the meaning of the Seat, which Allah has reported as encompassing the heavens and the earth. Some said it is the knowledge of Allah, others the place of the two feet, others the Throne. Each has an aspect and a tendency, but what is most fitting for the verse is that which the Prophet's transmission has brought.

The origin of the word for the Seat is knowledge. From it the sheet on which written knowledge is set is called a writing-board, and the scholars are called the seats because they are those on whom the earth is kept in order, the tent-pegs of the earth. The Arabs call the origin of every thing by that word, so one says of a man that he is of noble origin.

phrases.translation: and the preservation of both does not tire Him. For He is the Most High, the Greatest
phrases.explanation:
The preservation of both does not weigh upon Him means that it is not difficult for Him and does not burden Him. The letters in the phrase refer back to the heavens and the earth, so the sense is that His Seat encompasses the heavens and the earth, and the preservation of the heavens and the earth does not burden Him.

As for His word and He is the Most High, it means that Allah is the Most High. The people of inquiry differed over its meaning, and the view given is that He is the Most High above His creation through the highness of His place above the places of His creation, for the Exalted is above His whole creation and His creation is below Him, just as He described Himself as being upon the Throne. They differed likewise over the meaning of His word the Magnificent.

The notes that close the discussion take up the words of the lines of poetry quoted to explain drowsiness. The wild cows are the wild cows and they are beautiful of eye, and the place where the gazelles are numerous is a place of that name. The phrase drowsiness killed him means that it struck him dead on the spot, and the word for a bird that beats its wings and stays hovering without flying is the word for its flapping, from which drowsiness is taken, and this figurative sense is the one that pleases the author more in the poetry. The word for the foam that mingles with the eye is taken from the mud that fouls the water until it overwhelms it, and the words for the wine describe the best and most expensive kind of wine, the foam that rises between the cup and the vat, and the dizziness of a man who staggers from wine.

phrases.translation: Let there be no compulsion in religion, for the truth stands out clearly from falsehood.
phrases.explanation:
The exegetes differed over the meaning of this verse. Some said it was revealed concerning a group of the people of Medina, or one man among them, who had children they had made convert to Judaism or Christianity, and who wanted to compel them to Islam when it was sent down, and Allah forbade them that, so that the children themselves might choose. The command to fight the people of the Book had not yet been given, and the verse of the Book that follows was sent down, after which this verse was abrogated and the fighting was commanded.

The meaning of there is no compulsion in religion is that no one is compelled to the religion of Islam, and the definite article in the religion is inserted only to point to the religion Allah intended, which is Islam. It is also possible that the article stands in place of the pronoun, so that the sense is that there is no compulsion in His religion, and that reading fits the verse best.

The phrase the right way has been made distinct means that the right way has become clear, and it is the same as the word for following the straight way, which is when one attains the truth. And the word for error is the same as the word for straying, used when one passes the truth and exceeds it, and thus strays.

phrases.translation: So whoever renounces false gods and believes in Allah
phrases.explanation:
The exegetes differed over the meaning of the taghut. Some said it is Satan, others the sorcerer, others the soothsayer. The correct view is that the taghut is everyone who is rebellious against Allah and is worshipped besides Him, whether by compulsion on his part over whoever worships him or by the obedience of whoever worships him, and whether that worshipped one is a human, a satan, an idol-image, an idol, or whatever.

The sense of the passage is then set out. It is not absurd to say that there is no compulsion in religion for anyone from whom the jizyah is taken, and the community has transmitted that the Prophet compelled some people to Islam and ruled that they should be killed if they refused, and that this applies to the idolaters and to the apostate, while he did not compel the rest, taking from them the jizyah and confirming them upon their religion, which applies to the people of the two Books.

If it is said that this was transmitted as revealed concerning a group of the people of Medina who wished to compel their children to Islam, the answer is that its correctness is not to be rejected, for a verse may be revealed concerning a particular case and its ruling then applies generally to everything that answers to the meaning for which it was revealed.

phrases.translation: has certainly grasped the firmest, unfailing hand-hold.
phrases.explanation:
The handhold is in this place a likeness for faith to which the believer clings. The one who holds fast to it has been likened to a man who grasps the handle of a thing that has a handle, in his holding fast to it and his grasping of it, since everyone who desires something with a handle holds fast only to its handle.

That it does not break, and the letters in the phrase refer back to the handhold.

And the sense of the words is that whoever rejects the taghut and believes in Allah has, as for obedience to Allah, grasped that whereby he, while holding fast to it, need not fear that He will forsake him or surrender him when he is in need of Him in the terrors of the Hereafter, like a man who has grasped the firmest of the handles of things, of which he need not fear that the handles will break.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation:
And Allah is All-Hearing means that He hears the faith of the believer in Allah alone, who rejects the taghut, in his profession of the oneness of Allah and his disavowal of the partners and the idol-images worshipped besides Allah.

And All-Knowing means that He knows what the man is resolved upon, namely the unification of Allah and the purifying of His lordship in his heart, and what his inner self bears within it of disavowal of the gods, the idols and the taghuts, and all else that the soul of each of His creatures conceals. No secret remains hidden from Him and no matter escapes Him, until He requites each one on the Day of Resurrection for what his tongue uttered and his soul concealed, with good if good and with evil if evil.

phrases.translation: Allah is the Guardian of the believers—He brings them out of darkness and into light. As for the disbelievers, their guardians are false gods who lead them out of light and into darkness.
phrases.explanation:
Allah is the Protector of those who believe, and the Protector means their helper and support, for He shows them mercy through His aid and support toward the good. He brings them out of the darknesses of disbelief into the light of faith, and the darknesses are an image for disbelief, since darkness keeps the eye from perceiving things and disbelief keeps the heart's sight from perceiving the truths of faith.

As for the disbelievers, their protectors are the taghut, who stand between them and faith and lead them astray, and this is their being held back from faith and deprived of good. The verse may have been sent down about those addressed in it, that is, whoever among the Christians disbelieved in Muhammad, and whoever among the idolaters believed in him but denied Jesus.

phrases.translation: It is they who will be the residents of the Fire. They will be there forever
phrases.explanation:
These are the inhabitants of the Fire, the people of the Fire who will abide eternally therein, that is to say in the fire of Hell, and not others among the people of faith, without end and without limit, forever. They are the ones who had believed in Jesus the son of Mary and who rejected Muhammad when he came to them, and concerning them this verse was sent down.

A point of language is settled at the same time. The word for the taghut is a name for a group and for a single one, and it can be made plural, which is why the verse speaks of them in the plural although the word itself is singular.

phrases.translation: Are you ˹O Prophet˺ not aware of the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord because Allah had granted him kingship?
phrases.explanation:
The question is put to the Prophet as one to be taken to heart, for it means, have you not seen, O Muhammad, with your heart? The one who argued is the one who entered into dispute, and the ground of the quarrel is given at once, namely that Allah had granted him the kingship.

The whole of the verse that follows is the account of that argument, in which Abraham called upon his Lord and was answered by the man, until the argument was settled before everyone and the one who argued could say nothing further. It is a story about the One who gives life and causes death, and about the limits of what a creature may claim.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when Abraham said, “My Lord is the One Who has power to give life and cause death.” He argued, “I too have the power to give life and cause death.” Abraham challenged ˹him˺, “Allah causes the sun to rise from the east. So make it rise from the west.”
phrases.explanation:
The one who disputed with Abraham is Abraham himself, the prophet of Allah, and the phrase about his Lord means that he disputed with him about it, because Allah had granted him kingship.

Abraham said, my Lord is the One who gives life and causes death, meaning that in His hand are life and death, for He gives life to whom He wills and death to whom He wishes. The man answered, I do that too, keeping alive whom he wished to kill and so not killing him, and that was his giving of life, and killing another was his causing of death.

Abraham then said, Allah brings the sun from its east, so bring it from the west if you are a god, and the one who disbelieved was struck dumb, his argument cut off and void.

phrases.translation: And so the disbeliever was dumbstruck. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people
phrases.explanation:
Allah does not guide the people of disbelief to an argument by which they could refute the argument of the people of truth in disputing and debating, because the arguments of the people of falsehood are void, and so the one who argued was left without an answer before everyone.

The meaning of wrongdoing is placing a thing in a place that does not befit it, and the disbeliever placed his denial of what he denied in a place that did not befit it, and he is therefore by his deed a wrongdoer against himself, and the wrong he did came back on his own head and hurt no one but him.

phrases.translation: Or ˹are you not aware of˺ the one who passed by a city which was in ruins.
phrases.explanation:
Allah joins this to the verse before it, the one about the man who argued with Abraham about his Lord, because the two are alike: in both cases the Prophet marvelled at a man who doubted what Allah can do. Some of the grammarians said that the word or is extra here, but nothing in the Book of Allah is without meaning, so it is not extra.

The exegetes differed over who this man was. Some said it was Uzayr, others said it was Irmiya ibn Halqiya, and it was said that Irmiya was al-Khidr.

That the city lay in ruins down to its roofs means it was empty of its people and its dwellers. The roofs are the structures and the houses, and every building is called a roof.

phrases.translation: He wondered, “How could Allah bring this back to life after its destruction?” So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years then brought him back to life. Allah asked, “How long have you remained ˹in this state˺?” He replied, “Perhaps a day or part of a day.”
phrases.explanation:
The exegetes differed over the town. Some said it was Jerusalem. Others said it was the town whose people left their homes in their thousands out of fear of death, where Allah told them to die. The correct view follows the correct view on the name of the man.

The likeliest account is that Allah made the Prophet marvel at a man who asked how Allah could bring the ruined city back to life. He was told to sleep, and after seventy of the hundred years an angel was sent to a king of Persia to rebuild the city, and the spirit of life was returned to the eye of the sleeping man while his body stayed dead, so he said he had remained a day or part of a day.

phrases.translation: Allah said, “No! You have remained here for a hundred years! Just look at your food and drink—they have not spoiled. ˹But now˺ look at ˹the remains of˺ your donkey! And ˹so˺ We have made you into a sign for humanity. And look at the bones ˹of the donkey˺, how We bring them together then clothe them with flesh!” When this was made clear to him, he declared, “˹Now˺ I know that Allah is Most Capable of everything.”
phrases.explanation:
Look at your food and your drink, it has not spoiled, means that the years that passed over them did not change them. His food was a basket of figs and grapes and his drink water or grape juice.

The exegetes differed over what it means that it has not spoiled. Some said it has not changed and others that it has not become putrid. The correct view is that it has not stinked, and the word is not from the word for foul water.

Look at your donkey means look at Our revival of your donkey, and at its bones, how We join them together and clothe them with flesh. The man looked and saw the bones joined and the flesh clothed upon them, and the donkey stood up braying, so he knew Allah is capable of everything.

phrases.translation: And ˹remember˺ when Abraham said, “My Lord! Show me how you give life to the dead.”
phrases.explanation:
And remember when Abraham said is joined to the two verses before it. The words have you not seen do not mean seeing with the eyes, they mean knowing with the heart.

The exegetes differed over the occasion of Abraham asking his Lord to show him how He brings the dead to life. Some said it was because he saw an animal torn to pieces by beasts and birds, and he asked to see with his own eyes what he had known by report. Others said it was because of the argument between him and Nimrod. Others said it was when the glad tidings came that Allah had made him an intimate friend. Others said that he asked because he doubted the power of Allah to bring the dead to life.

phrases.translation: Allah responded, “Do you not believe?” Abraham replied, “Yes I do, but just so my heart can be reassured.”
phrases.explanation:
Do you not believe is a question about the strength of his belief, and Abraham answers that he believes, but he wants his heart at rest.

That my heart may be at rest means that it may come to rest and be calm through the certainty which he knows. This is the view of those who take the sense to be that he might increase in faith, or that aid might be granted to him.

We have already mentioned those who said that the meaning is that his heart may be at rest in the knowledge that he is the intimate friend of Allah.

Others said the meaning is that he might know that Allah answers him when he calls upon Him and gives to him when he asks.

phrases.translation: Allah said, “Then bring four birds, train them to come to you, ˹then cut them into pieces,˺ and scatter them on different hilltops.
phrases.explanation:
Take four birds means take four of the birds. It has been mentioned that the four birds were the rooster, the peacock, the crow and the dove.

The word cut them into pieces is read with a kasra by a group from Kufa, who said that this word is not known in the usage of the Arabs for cutting into pieces, and that the kasra is a form of the dialect of the tribes of Hudhayl and Sulaym, as the words of a poet of Sulaym show: when I pulled on the rope, its thongs creaked about the ends of the stakes, with strong bindings, meaning that he cut it through.

The view of the grammarians of Basra is the sounder one, that the damma and the kasra on the letter sad mean the same and have one meaning, that the sense here is then cut them into pieces, and that the words to you are placed before the verb because they complete the words take. The clearest proof is that all the exegetes agreed on the meaning without paying heed to the kasra or the damma, and without distinguishing between the two readings. If the word had meant cutting only in the inverted form, they would have known the difference. It is the same for the reciters whichever way they read it, though the damma is the loftier of the two and the best known among the Arabs.

With a small number of the exegetes the word means to bind them firmly. As for a part of them on each mountain, some said on each quarter of the quarters of the world and others said on each mountain. A part is a portion of a thing, whether the whole of it is divided over it equally or not. It differs from a share, which is the portion over which the whole is divided equally, which is why people say shares of an inheritance and not parts.

phrases.translation: Then call them back, they will fly to you in haste. And ˹so you will˺ know that Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.”
phrases.explanation:
Then call them means that He commanded him to say to the parts of the birds, come, by the permission of Allah.

If someone asks whether Abraham was commanded to call them while they were torn apart and dead or after they had been brought to life, the answer is that the command to call them while they were scattered parts is a command of bringing into being, like the command to those who were turned into apes, and not a command of worship.

And know that Allah is Almighty, All-Wise means know, O Abraham, that He who brought these birds to life after you had torn them apart and scattered them over the mountains is Almighty in His grip when He seizes the tyrants who disobeyed His messengers, and All-Wise in His disposition.

phrases.translation: The example of those who spend their wealth in the cause of Allah is that of a grain that sprouts into seven ears, each bearing one hundred grains.
phrases.explanation:
This verse goes back to His word who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan. The accounts that stand in between, the Children of Israel with Talut and Jalut, the man who argued with Abraham and the man who passed by the ruined village, are an interjection.

He made this interjection as an argument against the polytheists, who denied the resurrection and the Hour, and as an exhortation to the believers to strive, letting them know that He is their helper though they are few. It also cut off the excuse of the Jews.

Have you ever seen an ear in which there were a hundred grains? If that exists, then it is so. Otherwise the sense may be an ear that brought forth seven ears, in each ear a hundred grains.

phrases.translation: And Allah multiplies ˹the reward even more˺ to whoever He wills. For Allah is All-Bountiful, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation:
The exegetes differed over and Allah multiplies for whom He wills. Some said that He multiplies for whom He wills the reward of his good deeds beyond what He gives to one who does not spend. Others said that He multiplies beyond the seven hundred.

The most fitting of these is that Allah multiplies beyond the seven hundred, to whatever multiplication He wills, for whom He wills of those who spend in His way, since no reward was mentioned for the one who does not spend.

And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing means that He gives more than the seven hundred to whom He wills of those who spend in His way, and that He knows who deserves the increase. Others said that All-Encompassing refers to the multiples and All-Knowing to what they spend.

phrases.translation: Those who spend their wealth in the cause of Allah and do not follow their charity with reminders of their generosity or hurtful words—they will get their reward from their Lord, and there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve
phrases.explanation:
It means the one who gives his wealth to those who strive in the way of Allah, and who does not follow up what he has spent with reproach or with injury. Reproach is making known that he has conferred a favour upon them, and injury is complaining about them.

He has laid this condition on the one who spends in the way of Allah alone, and made the reward binding on the one who does not reproach or injure, because such spending is that by which the face of Allah is sought.

For them is their reward with their Lord means the reward of those who spend their wealth in this manner. And no fear shall come upon them, nor shall they grieve means that besides the reward due to them nothing of the terrors of the Resurrection will strike them.

phrases.translation: Kind words and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury. And Allah is Self-Sufficient, Most Forbearing
phrases.explanation:
A kind word means a fine word, and the prayer of a man for his Muslim brother. Forgiveness means that he conceals what he has come to know of the other man's need and his poor condition. Are better means better with Allah than a charitable gift which he gives as charity followed by injury, that is, reproaching him for it and hurting him because of it.

Allah is free of need means that Allah has no need of what they give as charity. Forbearing means that He does not hasten the punishment against the one among you who reproaches with his charitable gift and so injures the one to whom he gives it.

phrases.translation: O believers!
phrases.explanation:
O you who believe means you who hold Allah and His Messenger to be truthful. Do not nullify your alms means do not nullify the rewards of your alms by reproach and by injury, just as the unbelief of the one who spends to be seen by the people nullified his.

To be seen by the people is his display of himself to them by his action, so that outwardly they suppose he intends Allah and praise him for it, while he does not intend Allah nor seek reward from Him. He spends it in that manner so that they may praise him, though they do not know his hidden intention. So they do not perceive his state with regard to the denial of Allah and the Last Day.

phrases.translation: Do not waste your charity with reminders ˹of your generosity˺ or hurtful words, like those who donate their wealth just to show off and do not believe in Allah or the Last Day.
phrases.explanation:
And does not believe in Allah and the Last Day means that he does not hold true the oneness of Allah and His sovereignty, nor that he will be raised after his death and requited for his deed, so that he would do his deed for the face of Allah and out of seeking His reward.

This is the mark of the hypocrite. We call him a hypocrite because of the one who openly displays his unbelief, for with none of his deeds does he wish to make anyone believe anything falsely. The hypocrite deludes the people with a deed outwardly for Allah, while inwardly his intention is doubtful and he means the praise of the people. The unbeliever, by contrast, leaves nothing obscure, for all his deeds are only for Satan.

phrases.translation: Their example is that of a hard barren rock covered with a thin layer of soil hit by a strong rain—leaving it just a bare stone.
phrases.explanation:
His likeness is as the likeness of a smooth rock upon which there is dust, then a downpour strikes it and leaves it bare. The smooth rock is both singular and plural, and it is the smooth stone. Upon which there is dust means upon the smooth rock there is dust, and the downpour is the violent, mighty rain that strikes the smooth rock. And leaves it bare means that the downpour leaves the smooth rock bare, that is, the hard stone upon which there is nothing of vegetation.

Thus are the deeds of the hypocrites, equivalent to the smooth rock with dust upon it, which the downpour struck so that it carried away the dust and left it pure. The Muslims see them outwardly as though they have deeds, because of that which they delude them with. But when the Day of Resurrection arrives and they return to Allah, all of that perishes, as the rain left the rock smooth with nothing upon it.

phrases.translation: Such people are unable to preserve the reward of their charity. Allah does not guide ˹such˺ disbelieving people
phrases.explanation:
They have no power means those who spend their wealth to be seen by the people and do not believe in Allah nor in the Last Day. On the Day of Resurrection they will have no power over any reward for anything of what they earned in this world, because they did not act for their return nor out of seeking what is with Allah, but for the praise of the people.

And Allah does not guide the unbelieving people means that He does not bring them onto the right way to the truth in their spending and in other matters, but leaves them blindly wandering in their error. And He said to the believers: do not be like the hypocrites whose deeds this parable describes.

phrases.translation: And the example of those who donate their wealth, seeking Allah’s pleasure and believing the reward is certain, is that of a garden on a fertile hill: when heavy rain falls, it yields up twice its normal produce. If no heavy rain falls, a drizzle is sufficient. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do
phrases.explanation:
And the likeness of those who spend their wealth means those who give alms with it and equip men with it on the path of Allah, who spend it seeking Allah's good pleasure and as a confirmation from within themselves concerning His promise. Allah meant by this only that their souls were certain and convinced of the promise He made to them concerning what they spent without reproach or harm, so they held firm in spending.

Some said that and as a confirmation means and as a strengthening, and some said and as a certainty. Others said it means that they scrupulously ascertained the place where they put their alms. The correct view is that this is far from the sense of the wording, for if it meant ascertaining the wording would be different. The meaning is what we have said, a confirmation by the souls of the people of themselves, the fortifying of resolve and certainty concerning the promise of Allah.

A garden means the orchard. On a height means that part of the land which rises and lifts itself above the watercourse, and it is called a height because it swells and becomes firm and elevated, and because the planting of the highlands is more beautiful than that of the valleys. The reciters differ in how they read it, with a damma or with a fatḥa, and the reading with a kasra is not permissible, while the damma is the better known of the two allowed.

Which a downpour struck means the garden that lay upon the height was struck by a downpour of rain, the heavy rain with large drops. So it brought forth its fruits twofold means that the garden doubled its fruit. And if a downpour does not strike it, then a light drizzle means the same.

The likeness means that just as the fruit of this garden was doubled when the rain fell, and the light drizzle does the same when the downpour fails, so does Allah double the alms of the one who spends seeking His good pleasure and as a confirmation from within himself, without reproach or harm.

And Allah is, of what you do, All-Seeing means, O people, that in your spendings nothing of that, nor of your deeds therein or in other matters, remains hidden from Him.

He keeps the account against you, until He recompenses you all according to your deed. He intends by this statement only a warning of His punishment, because anyone who commits something forbidden or is negligent in what was commanded of him falls under the seeing of Allah, and He keeps the account against them.

phrases.translation: Would any of you wish to have a garden with palm trees, grapevines, and all kinds of fruits with rivers flowing underneath and as they grow very old with dependent children, a fiery whirlwind hits the garden, burning it all up?
phrases.explanation:
Would any of you wish to have a garden of date-palms and grapevines, beneath which the rivers flow, and in which he has fruits of every kind. A garden means the orchard, the words for him go back to one of you, and the words in which refer to the garden. And there strikes him means that there strikes one of you. Old age, while he has weak offspring, means that the owner of the garden is struck by old age, while he has small children, and then it is struck means that the garden is struck by a whirlwind in which there is fire, so that it is burnt up. That happens precisely when he is in need of it, when his old age makes him dependent on its fruits and too weak to cultivate it, and when his children are small.

The exegetes disputed over this verse, but the sense of their statements comes back to what we have said, and the most fitting interpretation is this one, because Allah had already forbidden making mention of a favour after charity and set a likeness for the one who does that, equating him with the ostentatious hypocrite.

The wording allows if in place of that, since both can carry the sense of the future, and the Arabs allowed a perfect verb to answer an imperfect one. It is as though it were said: would any of you wish that, if he possessed such a garden and old age struck him. And a whirlwind in which there is fire: some said a wind of severe scorching heat, and others a wind of severe cold.

phrases.translation: This is how Allah makes His revelations clear to you, so perhaps you will reflect
phrases.explanation: Thus Allah makes clear to you the signs means that just as your Lord has made clear to you the matter of spending in His way, how its proper form is and what you may and may not do with it, so too does He make clear to you the signs besides that, and acquaints you with their rulings, what is permitted and what is forbidden, and clarifies His proofs, as a mercy from Him toward you. That you may reflect means that you may reflect with your intellects, and ponder the proofs of Allah therein and take instruction from them, and act according to the rulings that are in them, so that you may obey Allah.

phrases.translation: O believers!
phrases.explanation:
O you who believe means you who have held to be true Allah and His Messenger and the signs of His Book. And spend means to give the obligatory alms and to perform charity.

The exegetes differed over the sense of the verse, some of them taking the impure of what is forbidden to be meant and others taking only the inferior of what is permitted. The correct reading is the one that the companions of the Messenger transmitted, because of the soundness of its chain and the agreement of the exegetes upon it, and not the view of the one of them who differed from the rest.

phrases.translation: Donate from the best of what you have earned and of what We have produced for you from the earth.
phrases.explanation:
Spend from the good things of what you have earned means give the obligatory alms of the good that you have earned through your activity, whether by trade or by craft, in gold and silver. The good things are the high quality items: give the alms of your possessions that you have earned in a permitted manner, and give the gold and the silver, the high quality and not the inferior. And of what We have brought forth for you from the earth means spend also from what the earth has produced, so perform charity and give the alms of the date palms, the grapevines, the wheat and the barley, and everything for which charity has been obligatory among the crops of the earth.

The correct view is that Allah has urged His servants to charity and to the discharge of the alms from their possessions, and made that obligatory upon them. What He made obligatory became a right for the people who have a share in the charity, and He commanded them to discharge from the good, the high quality of their possessions, the good, because those who have a share are partners of the owners of the possessions in them. Each of two partners is entitled in proportion to his ownership, and neither may withhold from his partner his right by giving him something worse in its place.

phrases.translation: Do not pick out worthless things for donation, which you yourselves would only accept with closed eyes.
phrases.explanation:
And do not deliberately seek out the impure means do not make it your aim, do not intend it. The impure means the inferior, the not high quality: do not deliberately aim at the inferior of your possessions for your charity, but perform charity from the good and the high quality. The verse was revealed concerning a man of the Anṣār who hung up a cluster of spoiled dates where the Muslims used to hang the charity of their fruits.

And you are not to take it means you would not take the impure for your rightful claims, unless you closed an eye to it, that is, unless in taking it you would forgo a portion of what is rightfully yours. Some said that you would not accept the inferior from your debtors as what is due from them, except out of overlooking on your part. Others said that you would not take it when you buy it from the owners at the price of the good, except out of overlooking on their part.

phrases.translation: And know that Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy
phrases.explanation: And know that Allah is free of need, Praiseworthy means know, O people, that Allah is free of need with respect to your charity and with respect to all else. He has only commanded it to you and made it obligatory in your possessions out of mercy toward you, so that by it He may bring your needy to prosperity, strengthen your weak, and grant you an abundant reward in the Hereafter, not on account of any need He has for it toward you. And Praiseworthy means that He is praised among His creatures for the favours He has bestowed upon them and the abundance of His grace that He has spread out for them.

phrases.translation: The Devil threatens you with ˹the prospect of˺ poverty and bids you to the shameful deed ˹of stinginess˺, while Allah promises you forgiveness and ˹great˺ bounties from Him.
phrases.explanation:
Satan promises you, O people, on account of giving alms and on account of paying the obligatory alms that is due upon your possessions, that you will fall into poverty. And he commands you to indecency, that is to say, he commands you disobedience toward Allah and the abandonment of obedience to Him.

While Allah promises you forgiveness from Him means that Allah promises you, O believers, that He will cover your indecent deeds by remitting the punishment for them, so that He will forgive you your sins on account of the alms that you give. And abundance means that He promises you that He will recompense you for what you give in alms, so that He will bestow upon you favours from His gifts and make your provision abundant.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Bountiful, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation:
And Allah is all-encompassing means all-encompassing with respect to the abundance that He promises to bestow upon you from His abundance and the vastness of His treasuries. And all-knowing means all-knowing concerning your expenditures and the alms that you spend and give, which He tallies up for you until He will reward you for them upon your coming to Him in the Hereafter.

So the whole of the verse turns on this. The One who promises you forgiveness and bounty has no need of what you give and is not mistaken about any of it. He knows who spends to be seen and who spends seeking His good pleasure, and He keeps the account of what each gives, so that He may repay every one of them according to what he did.

phrases.translation: Allah grants wisdom to whoever He wills.
phrases.explanation: Wisdom is a gift from God, including sound understanding and the ability to act rightly. The verse reminds people that insight is not merely a product of status or information. Those who receive wisdom should respond with humility and gratitude.  Wisdom can guide a person toward justice and beneficial action.

phrases.translation: And whoever is granted wisdom is certainly blessed with a great privilege.
phrases.explanation: Wisdom is described as an immense blessing. It enables a person to recognize what matters and apply knowledge responsibly. The phrase elevates wisdom above material wealth and invites believers to value discernment and good judgment.  It is valuable because it shapes decisions and character.  Sound judgment is a lasting benefit in religious and worldly affairs.

phrases.translation: But none will be mindful ˹of this˺ except people of reason
phrases.explanation: People who reflect thoughtfully recognize the value of wisdom and divine guidance. The phrase calls for the use of reason in understanding revelation. It suggests that care and reflection help people perceive blessings that may otherwise be overlooked.  Reflection helps distinguish real insight from mere accumulation of facts.

phrases.translation: Whatever charities you give or vows you make are surely known to Allah.
phrases.explanation: God knows every charitable gift and every vow, whether public or private. This assures sincere givers that their actions are not overlooked and warns those who make vows that they remain accountable. The phrase emphasizes divine knowledge of both the act and its intention.  This includes obligations people make to themselves and to God.

phrases.translation: And the wrongdoers will have no helpers
phrases.explanation: Those who commit injustice will find no one able to rescue them from God’s judgment. This warning underscores the seriousness of violating others’ rights while handling wealth and vows. Human allies cannot erase wrongdoing that God knows.  Justice requires more than relying on human support or influence.

phrases.translation: To give charity publicly is good,
phrases.explanation: Public charity can be good when it encourages generosity or serves a clear communal purpose. The verse does not condemn visible giving outright. Its value depends on intention and whether it benefits people without humiliating recipients.  Public giving can model generosity when it does not seek self-praise.

phrases.translation: but to give to the poor privately is better for you,
phrases.explanation: Private giving is often better because it protects the recipient’s dignity and the giver from showing off. The verse recommends discretion, especially when helping the poor. It balances the potential benefit of public example with the value of humility and privacy.  Privacy also shields recipients from embarrassment and public scrutiny.

phrases.translation: and will absolve you of your sins.
phrases.explanation: Sincere charity can serve as a means of expiation for sins. The promise encourages giving while reminding people that forgiveness is ultimately from God. The phrase does not make charity a license to harm others, but emphasizes the spiritual benefit of good deeds.  Forgiveness is a hoped-for reward, not a substitute for repairing harm.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Aware of what you do
phrases.explanation: God knows whether charity is given sincerely, publicly for encouragement, or privately for humility. His awareness includes both intention and effect. This reminder helps donors focus on pleasing God rather than managing appearances.  Divine awareness makes intention more important than public appearance.  Good intentions remain known even when the gift is anonymous.

phrases.translation: You are not responsible for people’s guidance ˹O Prophet˺—it is Allah Who guides whoever He wills.
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is not charged with forcing people to accept guidance, God guides whom He wills. The verse affirms that belief cannot be imposed by human pressure. It clarifies the Prophet’s role as conveying the message and frees believers from controlling another person’s faith.  The distinction preserves the voluntary nature of faith.

phrases.translation: Whatever you ˹believers˺ spend in charity, it is for your own good—as long as you do so seeking the pleasure of Allah.
phrases.explanation: Charitable spending benefits the giver spiritually when done sincerely for God. The phrase shifts focus from controlling recipients to purifying one’s own intention. Giving should not be a tool for coercion or praise, but an act seeking divine approval.  Sincere charity is directed toward God’s approval, not control of others.

phrases.translation: Whatever you donate will be paid back to you in full, and you will not be wronged
phrases.explanation: God promises full reward for what is given sincerely, with no injustice in the final account. The return may not be immediate or material, but the divine reckoning is complete. This assurance encourages generosity without fear of losing what is valuable.  The promise reassures donors that no good is lost.

phrases.translation: ˹Charity is˺ for the needy who are too engaged in the cause of Allah to move about in the land ˹for work˺.
phrases.explanation: Charity should reach people whose commitment to God’s cause leaves them unable to travel around seeking work. Their need may not be obvious because they are occupied with service or constrained circumstances. The verse directs attention toward identifying quiet need rather than only visible poverty.

phrases.translation: Those unfamiliar with their situation will think they are not in need ˹of charity˺ because they do not beg.
phrases.explanation: People who do not know the needy may assume they are self-sufficient because they do not ask for help. The verse cautions donors against judging need by whether someone begs. Dignified restraint can conceal hardship, so communities should observe and care attentively.  Their restraint can make them easy to overlook in public settings.

phrases.translation: You can recognize them by their appearance.
phrases.explanation: Careful observers can notice signs of need in these people’s circumstances and appearance. The phrase encourages attentiveness rather than indifference. It does not invite intrusive judgment, but asks the community to look beyond explicit requests and offer support respectfully.  Observation should lead to compassionate assistance, not stigma.

phrases.translation: They do not beg people persistently.
phrases.explanation: These needy people do not repeatedly ask others for assistance. Their restraint should not be mistaken for lack of need. The verse honors their dignity and urges people to give without waiting for them to plead.  Their reluctance to ask deserves respect and sensitivity.  Community care can reach those who preserve their dignity quietly.

phrases.translation: Whatever you give in charity is certainly well known to Allah
phrases.explanation: God knows every charitable gift and the circumstances in which it is given. Even quiet generosity that receives no public recognition is fully seen. The assurance motivates careful giving and reassures donors that sincere aid is never wasted.  God’s knowledge includes giving that is never publicly announced.

phrases.translation: Those who spend their wealth in charity day and night, secretly and openly—their reward is with their Lord, and there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve
phrases.explanation: People who give consistently, at different times and whether privately or publicly, receive reward from God. The verse values sustained generosity and recognizes varied appropriate ways of giving. Its promise of freedom from fear and grief assures those who spend sincerely that their good is secure with God.

phrases.translation: Those who consume interest will stand ˹on Judgment Day˺ like those driven to madness by Satan’s touch.
phrases.explanation: The verse gives a severe image of those who consume interest, depicting their disorientation at the Resurrection. It warns against an economic practice that exploits others and distorts fair exchange. The image conveys moral consequence, not a medical description of mental illness.  The comparison warns of a profound moral and spiritual disorder.

phrases.translation: That is because they say, “Trade is no different than interest.”
phrases.explanation: Those who defend interest claim it is no different from ordinary trade. The verse rejects this equivalence, distinguishing fair commerce from a practice separately prohibited. It challenges reasoning that treats all profit as morally identical regardless of how it is obtained.  The verse calls for distinguishing legitimate profit from exploitation.

phrases.translation: But Allah has permitted trading and forbidden interest.
phrases.explanation: The verse clearly distinguishes permitted trade from forbidden interest. Profit through exchange is not treated as inherently wrong, while interest-based gain is prohibited within the passage’s moral framework. The distinction calls people to follow divine guidance rather than redefine terms for convenience.  The prohibition is stated as a divine limit, not a negotiable preference.

phrases.translation: Whoever refrains—after having received warning from their Lord—may keep their previous gains, and their case is left to Allah.
phrases.explanation: Those who stop after receiving the warning may retain what they gained before the prohibition reached them. Their past case is entrusted to God, who knows their circumstances and response. The instruction offers a path to change without requiring impossible retroactive reversal.  The rule allows a clear break from the previous harmful practice.

phrases.translation: As for those who persist, it is they who will be the residents of the Fire.
phrases.explanation: Those who knowingly persist in consuming interest after the warning face severe accountability. The verse speaks of persistence after guidance, emphasizing the seriousness of continuing a prohibited practice. It calls for repentance and reform rather than treating the warning lightly.  The warning applies to those who persist after they know the ruling.

phrases.translation: They will be there forever
phrases.explanation: The verse describes lasting punishment for those specified. Its severity warns against knowingly persisting in wrongdoing and underscores the importance of responding to guidance. The passage combines a clear prohibition with an opportunity to stop and turn back.  The lasting warning should prompt repentance before judgment.

phrases.translation: Allah has made interest fruitless and charity fruitful.
phrases.explanation: The verse contrasts interest, which is deprived of blessing, with charity, which God causes to grow. The contrast concerns moral and spiritual consequences, not merely short-term financial outcomes. It encourages people to support others through generosity rather than benefit from exploitative gain.  The comparison points to lasting outcomes beyond the apparent size of a gain.

phrases.translation: And Allah does not like any ungrateful evildoer
phrases.explanation: God does not approve of those who persist in wrongdoing and ingratitude. The phrase connects exploitative financial conduct with a broader moral failure. It warns that rejecting God’s guidance about wealth has consequences beyond the immediate transaction.  Gratitude includes avoiding practices that harm other people.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those who believe, do good, establish prayer, and pay alms-tax will receive their reward from their Lord, and there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve
phrases.explanation: Believers who do good, maintain prayer, and give alms receive reward from God and are promised freedom from fear and grief. The verse contrasts faithful conduct with the prohibited financial practices discussed nearby. It shows that belief is expressed through worship, ethical behavior, and generosity.

phrases.translation: O believers! Fear Allah, and give up outstanding interest if you are ˹true˺ believers
phrases.explanation: Believers are commanded to be mindful of God and abandon interest still owed. Faith is tested through willingness to give up unlawful gain, not only through words. The instruction calls for a decisive change in financial practice and obedience to God’s guidance.  The call to faith is made concrete through abandoning unlawful profit.

phrases.translation: If you do not, then beware of a war with Allah and His Messenger!
phrases.explanation: The warning describes persistent interest-taking after the prohibition as an extremely serious opposition to God and His Messenger. It emphasizes the gravity of exploiting others financially. The phrase is a stern moral warning and should not be used to justify private violence or vigilantism.  The severity underscores the social harm of continuing the practice.

phrases.translation: But if you repent, you may retain your principal—neither inflicting nor suffering harm
phrases.explanation: If lenders repent, they may recover the original principal without charging interest. The rule protects both sides: creditors do not lose the amount lent, and debtors are not burdened by excess. The phrase grounds the financial settlement in fairness and mutual protection.  A fair settlement prevents debt from becoming a source of exploitation.

phrases.translation: If it is difficult for someone to repay a debt, postpone it until a time of ease.
phrases.explanation: When a debtor is genuinely in difficulty, the creditor should grant time until repayment becomes manageable. The instruction protects a person facing hardship from immediate pressure. It treats compassion as part of financial responsibility and discourages exploiting someone’s temporary inability to pay.  Delay offers relief while preserving the possibility of repayment.

phrases.translation: And if you waive it as an act of charity, it will be better for you, if only you knew
phrases.explanation: Forgiving some or all of the debt as charity is even better. The verse encourages generosity beyond the required extension of time. It reminds creditors that releasing a struggling person can bring spiritual reward greater than insisting on repayment.  Forgiveness can release a person from hardship and earn divine reward.

phrases.translation: Be mindful of the Day when you will ˹all˺ be returned to Allah, then every soul will be paid in full for what it has done, and none will be wronged
phrases.explanation: The verse reminds people of the Day they return to God, when each person receives the full consequence of their deeds without injustice. This includes financial dealings that may seem private or ordinary. Awareness of judgment encourages fairness toward debtors and honesty in every transaction.

phrases.translation: O believers! When you contract a loan for a fixed period of time, commit it to writing. Let the scribe maintain justice between the parties.
phrases.explanation: Believers are instructed to document deferred debts and have a scribe record them fairly. Written terms help prevent later disagreement and protect both creditor and debtor. The passage provides detailed safeguards because financial obligations can be forgotten, disputed, or abused over time.  Recording terms also protects memories and reduces future family or business disputes.

phrases.translation: The scribe should not refuse to write as Allah has taught them to write. They will write what the debtor dictates, bearing Allah in mind and not defrauding the debt.
phrases.explanation: The scribe should record the agreement honestly and should not refuse the task without reason. The debtor dictates the obligation, with God-consciousness and accuracy required. This assigns responsibility to the person who owes the debt and prevents the written record from understating what is due.

phrases.translation: If the debtor is incompetent, weak, or unable to dictate, let their guardian dictate for them with justice.
phrases.explanation: If the debtor cannot express the terms, a guardian may speak on their behalf but must do so justly. The provision protects people with limited capacity or ability to communicate. It ensures that vulnerability does not become an opportunity for others to distort the debt.

phrases.translation: Call upon two of your men to witness. If two men cannot be found, then one man and two women of your choice will witness—so if one of the women forgets the other may remind her.
phrases.explanation: The verse sets out a witness procedure for documenting the debt. It specifies witnesses and explains the role of mutual reminder in this financial testimony. The instruction belongs to this transactional context and should not be generalized into a claim about women’s worth or ability in every domain.

phrases.translation: The witnesses must not refuse when they are summoned.
phrases.explanation: Witnesses are asked to fulfill their role when called, helping preserve an accurate record. Their participation supports justice between the parties and protects the agreement from later dispute. The verse treats truthful testimony as a communal responsibility, not merely a private favor.  Their testimony helps establish what was agreed if disagreement later arises.

phrases.translation: You must not be against writing ˹contracts˺ for a fixed period—whether the sum is small or great.
phrases.explanation: Debts should be documented whether large or small. The effort of writing is worthwhile because even modest sums can cause disagreement. Consistent records protect trust and reduce the risk that one party will later be pressured or misremember the terms.  Written records can protect even small everyday financial dealings.

phrases.translation: This is more just ˹for you˺ in the sight of Allah, and more convenient to establish evidence and remove doubts.
phrases.explanation: Written contracts are more equitable, provide evidence, and reduce uncertainty. The verse explains the purpose of its detailed procedure: fairness and clarity. Documentation serves both sides and is a practical means of preventing conflict rather than a sign of mistrust.  Clarity benefits both parties and supports impartial resolution.

phrases.translation: However, if you conduct an immediate transaction among yourselves, then there is no need for you to record it, but call upon witnesses when a deal is finalized.
phrases.explanation: Immediate exchanges do not require the same written documentation, though witnesses are still recommended when completing a transaction. The rule distinguishes deferred debts from prompt dealings. It offers practical flexibility while preserving transparency and evidence where useful.  The exception avoids needless formality for immediate exchanges.

phrases.translation: Let no harm come to the scribe or witnesses. If you do, then you have gravely exceeded ˹your limits˺.
phrases.explanation: The scribe and witnesses must not be harmed or coerced. Their role in establishing justice should not expose them to retaliation. The warning condemns intimidation and makes clear that the documentation process must protect everyone involved.  Protecting these participants is essential to a fair process.

phrases.translation: Be mindful of Allah, for Allah ˹is the One Who˺ teaches you. And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things
phrases.explanation: God-consciousness should guide financial agreements because God teaches people how to act justly and knows all things. The conclusion places the detailed procedures within a spiritual framework. Honest records and fair dealings are forms of obedience, and hidden misconduct remains known to God.  Guidance in commerce is part of divine teaching and care.

phrases.translation: If you are on a journey and a scribe cannot be found, then a security can be taken.
phrases.explanation: When traveling and unable to find a scribe, the parties may use collateral as security for a debt. The provision adapts the documentation rules to practical circumstances. It protects the creditor while recognizing that written records may not always be available.  Collateral is a practical safeguard when documentation is unavailable.

phrases.translation: If you trust one another, then ˹there is no need for a security, but˺ the debtor should honour this trust ˹by repaying the debt˺—and let them fear Allah, their Lord.
phrases.explanation: If the parties rely on mutual trust instead of collateral, the debtor must honor the obligation and remain mindful of God. Trust is not permission to avoid repayment. The verse combines personal confidence with accountability and encourages honesty even without formal safeguards.  Trust requires the debtor to fulfill the agreed obligation.

phrases.translation: And do not conceal the testimony, for whoever conceals it, their hearts are indeed sinful.
phrases.explanation: Witnesses must not hide relevant testimony. Concealment damages justice and is described as a sin of the heart as well as an outward act. The instruction underscores that truth must be preserved when financial rights are at stake.  Withholding evidence can deprive another person of a rightful claim.

phrases.translation: And Allah ˹fully˺ knows what you do
phrases.explanation: God knows whether parties honor their debts and whether witnesses speak truthfully. People may evade human scrutiny, but divine knowledge is complete. The reminder encourages integrity in private transactions and care for the rights of others.  Divine awareness supports truthfulness when no witnesses are present.
